## 1. Mission
Make surface→orbit→interplanetary→surface look seamless and run fast. Own the "rendering magic" that sells continuous traversal, plus the techniques that let a dense 3D factory render without melting the GPU.

## 2. Scope & owned subsystems
- **Scaled space**, distant celestial bodies via a second camera at huge scale; swap to real terrain on approach.
- **Multi-range depth**, logarithmic or cascaded depth buffer (draw a 1 m object and a 100,000 km planet in one frame, no z-fighting).
- **Terrain rendering**, consume world-gen's cubed-sphere quadtree; stream/blend LOD; horizon curvature.
- **Atmospheric scattering**, Rayleigh/Mie post-process; the sky-fades-to-black sell of leaving a planet.
- **Factory rendering at scale**, GPU instancing of identical parts/items; LOD that collapses distant belts to flowing textures/decals; cull/abstract un-observed item meshes.
- **Materials, lighting, VFX**, engine pipeline (Lumen/Nanite under D-001), thrust/dust/weather FX.
- **Non-goals:** what to render (world-gen, factory-sim, physics produce the data); UI/HUD (→ gameplay).

## 2.1 THE CALIBRATED TARGET (RN-352). What "correct" looks like now, as numbers

**Written 2026-08-01. Every art, asset and rendering lane calibrates against this
section. It is not taste; every line is a measurement with a way to re-take it.**

Without a written target the direction decays back to whoever last had an
opinion, which is how this project spent several passes measuring well against
the wrong thing. If you disagree with a number here, take the measurement again
and change the number, in this file, with the reading beside it. Do not work
around it.

### The one command that re-takes every number

```
cd web && npm run sync-assets && npx vite build --outDir dist-<lane>
npx vite preview --outDir dist-<lane> --port <yours> --strictPort --host 127.0.0.1
node tools/smoke/run.mjs --url=http://127.0.0.1:<yours>/ --scenario=walk \
  --width=1600 --height=900 --evalfile=tools/smoke/probes/lookdev.js \
  --evalargs='{"site":{"name":"forest","lat":-19.85,"lon":-72.7853,"yaw":300,"pitch":-10}}'
```

`probes/lookdev.js` reports, per sun elevation, the whole frame and the frame
split into **masked ground** and **masked sky** (the mask is built once at noon
and reused; see RN-335). Add `"pose": true` for a single PNG through the
shipping path, and pipe it through `tools/smoke/writeshot.mjs`.

### 1. The response curve

| | value | why it is that |
|---|---|---|
| tone curve | ACES RRT+ODT fit, three's own | one curve for the composite and for any material three tonemaps itself, so an A/B never measures "a different tonemapper" |
| exposure | **1.2** | the largest value that leaves shadow occupancy alone (`loFrac` moves under 0.8 points at three sites) and the smallest that keeps RN-152's night floor |
| contrast | **1.45**, on the slope-matched S (`curveMix` 1) | the straight line clips both ends: at 1.06 every display value over 0.972 was already white |
| saturation | **0.92** | a per-channel contrast raises chroma on its own; this is what makes the contrast a VALUE change |
| lift | **0** | a lifted black point is the first thing ART-DIRECTION.md names |
| colour space | sRGB encode in the composite, `outputColorSpace = SRGBColorSpace` | no double encode: the composite's source has no `<colorspace_fragment>` include for three to substitute |

**Negative controls, both exact and both one flag:** `?curve=0` restores the
RN-10 straight line, and `?grade=0` makes the whole grade an identity mix.
`?post=0` restores the pre-stack path.

### 2. Reference luminances

Standing eye (alt 2.0 m), yaw 300, local noon, 1600 x 900, the shipped grade.
`groundNear` is a 140 px box at 0.5 / 0.66 of the frame; `sky*` boxes are placed
off the mask's own horizon row. **These are the calibration. A change that moves
one of them by more than a few counts owes an explanation.**

| site | groundNear luma | groundNear RGB | masked-ground p50 | masked-sky p50 | ground `sat` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Forest (floor, pitch -26) | 35 | (24, 44, 19) before RN-347, brown after | 33 | 191 | 0.44 |
| Hills (pitch -10) | 43 | (40, 49, 20) | 50 | 152 | 0.53 |
| Plains (pitch -10) | 55 | (45, 67, 21) | 51 | 158 | 0.62 |
| Beach (pitch -10) | 167 | (189, 166, 111) | 167 | 174 | 0.36 |

**Shape targets, which matter more than the absolute values because they survive
a retune:**

- **`hiFrac` must not be zero.** Before this pass it was 0.00 at Hills and Plains
  noon: the top fifth of the range was empty at every site and every daylight
  elevation. It now reads 0.056 / 0.040 / 0.060 at Hills / Plains / Forest noon.
  A frame with no highlights is the definition of the flat read.
- **`loFrac` must not move much when exposure does.** That is the test that a
  contrast gain was not bought by brightening the image out of its own shadows.
- **The masked ground's `iqr` goes UP and its `sat` goes DOWN.** Value does the
  work, hue does less. Both must hold at every site and every day elevation, or
  the claim is site-specific (RN-64, and RN-334 where the fourth site disagreed).
- **Night: assert the masked GROUND's mean and median, never a whole-frame
  percentile.** At Hills midnight the sky is mean 0.06 counts with p95 = 0, so a
  whole-frame p95 at night is a statement about the ground wearing a costume.

### 2.1a THE A3 RE-TAKE (RN-1257). Same command, same four sites, one commit apart

**Taken 2026-08-13 on the Windows D3D path, `?post=1` asserted on every frame, noon rung only
(`"dots":[null]`), binary `0e53c1b` against `e1a7b68`. Both bundles built and served side by
side on 4376 and 4375, so the pair is ONE VARIABLE APART on ONE machine rather than a
comparison against a table taken on a different binary.**

| site | groundNear luma | groundNear RGB | masked-ground p50 | masked-sky p50 | ground `sat` | ground `iqr` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Forest | 35.70 -> **36.10** | (39,37,21) -> **(40,37,21)** | 29 -> **28** | 192 -> **192** | 0.44 -> **0.44** | 28 -> **28** |
| Hills | 42.50 -> **42.40** | (43,46,26) -> **(43,45,26)** | 52 -> **52** | 152 -> **152** | 0.40 -> **0.40** | 60 -> **60** |
| Plains | 64.90 -> **64.80** | (67,69,36) -> **(67,69,36)** | 65 -> **65** | 165 -> **165** | 0.51 -> **0.50** | 77 -> **77** |
| Beach | 149.70 -> **149.90** | (172,148,104) -> **(172,148,104)** | 153 -> **154** | 174 -> **174** | 0.34 -> **0.34** | 49 -> **47** |

**THE TABLE DID NOT MOVE, AND HALF OF THAT IS A RESULT AND HALF IS AN INSTRUMENT LIMIT. Both
halves are stated because reading only the first one would be the mistake.**

- **The result half.** Every biome's channel amplitudes, frequency partition, tint and
  roughness changed, the ground texture's bytes changed, and no site's `groundNear` luma moved
  by half a count, no `sat` moved by more than 0.01 and no masked-ground `p50` by more than 1.
  That is the calibration surviving a material pass, which is exactly what section 2.1 exists
  to check, and it is not luck: the grain tint is mean-preserving by construction (the field is
  centred on zero, so multiplying it by any vector leaves every channel's LEVEL alone and moves
  only its SPREAD) and the frequency partition sums to 1 with `OF_TEX_SCALE_GAIN` carrying the
  old total, so the change re-distributes energy rather than adding it.
- **The instrument half, and it is the more useful finding.** `groundNear` is a 140 px box at
  0.5 / 0.66 of the frame, and at the three `pitch -10` sites that box lands on ground **20 to
  60 m away**, while `texW` fades out over 35 to 75 m and its near boost is inside 22 m. **The
  section 2.1 box therefore sits at or past the fade of the term this pass is about at three
  of the four sites.** At Forest (`pitch -26`) the box IS inside the band, and there the box is
  mostly understorey card rather than ground. So a null in this table is not evidence that the
  ground did not change; the `artframe.js` `forestfloor` box (a different box, same site) moved
  its `iqr` 16.56 -> 18.11 on the same pair, and the pictures are not close.
- **The one deliberate move is Beach's `iqr`, 49 -> 47.** Beach is the brightest land biome and
  the luminance rule takes its row sum DOWN, 0.36 -> 0.28, because a multiplicative modulation
  already gives bright ground more absolute contrast than dark. Losing two counts of spread at
  the brightest site while the darkest site gains is the rule working, not a regression.
- **`hiFrac` stayed non-zero at Hills (0.02), Plains (0.01) and Beach (0.06)** and stayed 0.00
  at Forest, unchanged both ways. `loFrac` moved at most 0.01 at any site.

**THE FIVE CONTROL SITES ARE NOT IN THIS TABLE AND NEVER HAVE BEEN, which the campaign plan
does not say.** `ART-CAMPAIGN-2026-08-13.md` line 47 says the control sites "Mountains, Polar,
Regolith, MoonHighland, CraterFloor must not move", and section 3 below says a change that
moves them is a bug. **Neither section 2.1 nor section 2b has ever published a number for any
of the five.** They are biome ENUM names; `lookdev.js` takes a lat/lon, the four rows above are
its four sites, and three of the five are on Cinder and need `--body=cinder` plus a lunar
lat/lon that nothing in the repo records. So the control is currently a statement about the
PALETTE HEX only (section 3's own wording), and on that reading it holds exactly: RN-1257
changed no colour. **On the material reading the five have definitionally moved, because
separating Regolith from MoonHighland from CraterFloor IS the pass**, and the plan's line 47
cannot be satisfied and line 39 obeyed at the same time. Establishing first numeric rows for
the five is owed and is flagged in section 7.

### 2.1b THE LOD RE-TAKE (RN-1640, 2026-08-14). Same four sites, same command, maxDepth 14 -> 15, and it does not carry across

**WG-193 flagged this itself and named the owing lane rather than leaving it implicit.** The scatter re-seed that comes free with `maxDepth` 14 -> 15 (WG-186 to WG-193, merged at `4f152c8`) moves the `artframe.js` `forestfloor` box 26.54 -> 28.22 luma, "OUT of band" against section 2.1, and states plainly: "the §2.1 luminance table must be RE-TAKEN at this LOD rather than carried across." This is that re-take: same four sites as §2.1's own command (Forest lat -19.85 lon -72.7853 pitch -26; Hills lat -31.165 lon -86.27401 pitch -10; Plains lat -7.9675 lon 116.53189 pitch -10; Beach lat -35.6028 lon 53.30131 pitch -10; all yaw 300, alt 2.0 m, local noon), same shipped grade, `?post=1` asserted, on a real Windows D3D11 boot (RTX 4060 Ti, ANGLE), `maxDepth` at its shipped default of 15, no URL override.

| site | groundNear luma (old -> new) | groundNear RGB new | masked-ground p50 (old -> new) | masked-sky p50 (old -> new) | ground `sat` (old -> new) | ground `iqr` (old -> new) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Forest | 36.10 -> **29.0** | (34.3, 28.3, 18.3) | 28 -> **22** | 192 -> **192** | 0.44 -> **0.4387** | 28 -> **29** |
| Hills | 42.40 -> **66.1** | (72.0, 67.8, 41.9) | 52 -> **54** | 152 -> **152** | 0.40 -> **0.3952** | 60 -> **56** |
| Plains | 64.80 -> **79.9** | (81.5, 85.5, 46.6) | 65 -> **64** | 165 -> **164** | 0.50 -> **0.4698** | 77 -> **69** |
| Beach | 149.90 -> **147.8** | (168.5, 145.8, 103.3) | 154 -> **145** | 174 -> **174** | 0.34 -> **0.3498** | 47 -> **62** |

"old" is §2.1a, the RN-1257 A3 re-take, the last published row for each site before WG-186 to WG-193 landed. "new" is this lane (RN-1640), one commit past `4f152c8` (this block's own allocation commit), with the grade, the post stack, the exposure and the sun elevation all held to §2.1a's own fixture.

**THE MOVE IS NOT ONE-DIRECTIONAL, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT FOR "RE-SEED" OVER "REGRESSION".** Forest falls 19.7%, Hills rises 55.9%, Plains rises 23.3%, Beach is flat (-1.4%). A shading, exposure or tone-curve defect sits upstream of the biome and moves every site the same way; a per-cell scatter hash reseeding at a finer lattice moves each site by whatever instances happen to land inside that site's own 140 px box, which is a per-site roll with no reason to share a sign. **`masked-sky p50` is unmoved at every site to the digit or within 1 count (192/192, 152/152, 165/164, 174/174)**, confirming the sun, the exposure and the grade are all bit-identical between old and new; the whole of the delta above is downstream of the ground alone.

**THE MECHANISM IS THE ONE WG-192/193 ALREADY NAMED, AND THIS TABLE IS ITS FOUR-SITE CONFIRMATION.** `ScatterLook.CLUSTER_SHIFT`'s patch size in cells halved in world metres when `maxDepth` went 14 -> 15 (14.46 m -> 7.19 m); WG-192 restored it to 14.38 m (within 0.6% of authored); and WG-193 measured `placedPerM2` **holding at 0.46431 -> 0.46466 with `deliveredFraction` 1.0002 in BOTH arms, zero cells and zero chunks capped** -- density is unchanged and provably so. What changed is WHICH instances a per-cell hash placed, because a finer lattice is a different hash, and this table shows that reseed landing differently at four different sites rather than as one shared bias.

**ONE NEW FAILURE THIS RE-TAKE FOUND, NAMED RATHER THAN SILENTLY CARRIED: Forest's sky-mask `topRowSkyFrac` now reads 0.3237, under `lookdev.js`'s own 0.60 pass bar and well under the 0.8394 its code comment records as Forest's historical value.** Two more of `lookdev.js`'s checks that key off the same mask fail alongside it at Forest (`the sky share is plausible`, `value contrast RISES`); Hills, Plains and Beach all pass clean, zero failures. This is the same mechanism as the table move: at Forest's pitch -26 pose the re-seeded understorey now occupies more of the top of frame than before, which is real geometry and not an instrument regression (the mask rule itself is untouched). It does not change the numbers in the table above, which are read off fixed-position boxes rather than the mask, but a later lane relying on `lookdev.js`'s pass/fail at Forest should expect these three checks red until the mask's own calibration is revisited; not done here and flagged in section 7.

**THE STALE `forestfloor` 27.32 / p95 75.35 CITATION, RE-BASELINED (RN-1643).** Several dated entries in this file's own header and decision log (RN-1421/A0 2026-08-13, RN-1479 2026-08-13, RN-1524 2026-08-13, RN-1610 2026-08-14) quote the `artframe.js` `forestfloor` box at values from 24.79 through 36.10 luma and a p95 of 57.36 to 75.64, all taken before WG-186 to WG-193 landed. **Those rows are HISTORY and are left exactly as written**: each is a true reading of a real build at the time it was taken, and rewriting a past lane's own measurement to match a later LOD would falsify it. **Going forward, the `forestfloor` guardrail is 28.22 luma / p95 48.46**, verified independently in this lane on a fresh D3D11 build (matches the terrain lane's own `WG188_forestfloor_md15.json` to the digit, and confirmed again here via this lane's own `artframe.js --evalargs='{"shot":"forestfloor"}'` run). A verifier reading an older dated row and citing its number as current is reading history as a guardrail; this paragraph is the pointer that stops that.

**Shape targets for dusk, which is what a later lane should actually hold:**

- **`groundNear.warm` STAYS POSITIVE at every site down to about 1 degree.** The
  ground a player stands on gets warmer light as the sun sets, never cooler,
  because `sunT` extinguishes blue about seven times harder than red at grazing
  airmass. **A negative reading here is the assertion that would have caught a
  real cold wash, and this section had no such assertion until now.** The one
  value that reaches zero is Hills at 1.4 degrees (-0.2), where the direct term
  is gone and only ambient is left.
- **`groundNear` falls monotonically with elevation at every site.** Beach falls
  145 to 17, Plains 58 to 6, Hills 37 to 3, Forest 23 to 2. A rung that does not
  fall is a term that is not following the sun.
- **`skyLow.warm` is between -29 and -56 at every site and every rung.** The sky
  is blue and the ground is warm, and the SEPARATION between them is the thing
  worth protecting; a frame where both read the same hue is the failure mode.
- **The instrument floor is 0.05 counts of mean and 0.06 of warm at every
  daylight rung**, rising to 0.58 and 0.40 at the lowest two, where the
  understorey and the creatures are the only things left moving.

**ONE NUMBER HERE IS OWED AND IS NOT FIXED, NAMED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED.**
`groundNear` at Plains 3.5 degrees is luma 7.9 while the frame's own world band
sits at 37.5, so the ground under the player's feet is four to five times darker
than the frame around it and resolves into nothing. The mechanism is that the
direct term carries `ndl`, which on flat ground is the elevation dot and goes
linearly to zero, while `ofAtmoAerial`'s haze carries only `sunT` and merely
reddens. Nothing balances them. **Not changed this pass**, because the honest fix
is a judgement about how dark a playable dusk should be, and that is Reid's.

**AND ONE INSTRUMENT LIMIT, because it would otherwise be read as a result.**
The sky mask's rule is CHROMATIC (`B - R > 8` and luma `> 50`), so as the sun
drops the detected horizon row climbs: at Plains it moves from row 292 at noon
to row 193 at 1.5 degrees, a hundred pixels, with the geometry perfectly still.
**Any box placed relative to that horizon therefore cannot carry an elevation
trend**, which rules out `groundFar`, `groundMid` and `skyLow` for cross-rung
comparison and leaves `groundNear` and the world band, which are fixed fractions
of the frame. `probes/dusk.js` publishes the horizon row on every rung so this
is visible rather than inferred. A second defect in the same family was fixed on
the way: lookdev.js centres `groundFar` at `hz + 14` with a half-height of 26,
so twelve of its fifty-two rows are SKY, and at Hills at dusk that box read 152
while the ground under it read 7. `dusk.js` places it a full half-height below
the LOWEST column's horizon and publishes the old placement beside it as
`groundFarOld` so the noon rows above stay comparable.

### 3. Colour: what belongs to whom

**The terrain is the SUBSTRATE and the scatter is the VEGETATION, and they must
never be the same colour.** This is the rule RN-347 established and it is the
single largest thing in a ground-level frame.

- `BiomePalette.HEX` is soil, litter, sand and stone. Vegetated biomes sit at HSV
  saturation **0.25 to 0.35**. Anything above 0.40 is the old error.
- The green lives on the 3.2 M detail cards per km2 that stand on it. A plant
  that cannot be told from the ground it grows out of has no silhouette,
  whatever its geometry says.
- Mountains, Polar, Regolith, MoonHighland and CraterFloor were already substrate
  colours and are **the control**: a change that moves those sites is a bug.

### 4. Material response: roughness and metalness conventions

Effective roughness is `material.roughness * ormG`; effective metalness is
`material.metalness * ormB`.

- **A family's effective roughness p05..p95 band must be at least ~0.15 wide.**
  Below that it is a constant under a moving sun. **The rule stands; the two
  numbers this bullet carried from 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-13 were both wrong, and
  the campaign that quoted them was scoped on them. See RN-1470.** Measured off
  the shipped bytes on 2026-08-13, per role, `palette_roughness * ormG/255`:

  | family | effective band, per role | verdict |
  |---|---|---|
  | `stone` | Rock 0.549, RockDark 0.467 | widest in the game |
  | `suitplate` | Plate 0.268 | |
  | `coarse` | Soil 0.325, Sand/Regolith 0.309, Coal 0.293, Rubber 0.277, **Iron 0.130, Copper 0.114** | RN-1471 widened it; the two metal-chunk roles are still short |
  | `ore` | CopperOre 0.319, IronOre 0.226, CoalSeam 0.175 | |
  | `suitfab` | SuitGrime 0.317, SuitDark 0.242, Suit 0.224 | |
  | `panel` | Hazard 0.245, SteelDark/SuitAccent 0.224, Accent 0.204, Steel 0.184, **SteelLight 0.143** | |
  | `fur` | Chitin 0.168, ChitinBand/Under 0.169 | high and narrow ON PURPOSE (RN-461) |
  | `bark` | Bark 0.138, BarkLight 0.133 | short, and nobody has flagged it |

  **The two roles that still fail are palette-side, not map-side, and that is the
  transferable lesson.** `SteelLight` (0.143) and `coarse`'s `Iron` (0.130) and
  `Copper` (0.114) all wear a map whose span is fine and a palette roughness that
  is the lowest of their family's set (0.35, 0.40, 0.40). A narrow band is the
  PRODUCT of the map's span and the constant, so widening a shared map to rescue
  one role over-polishes the other six that wear it. Fixing these three is a
  palette edit in `of_lib.py`, priced as a re-surfacing of everything those roles
  touch, and it is deliberately not done here.
- **Metalness must carry information or be honestly constant.** As of 2026-08-13
  four families vary it: `panel` (span 0.580), `suitplate` (0.651), and the two
  RN-1474/RN-1475 additions `paintchip` (0.722) and `rust` (0.384). `coarse`,
  `bark`, `ore`, `fur`, `stone` and `suitfab` are honestly constant at 255 with a
  declared reason each in `ALLOWED_CONSTANT`. The old "three of four ORM maps"
  count predates six of the ten families.
- **Normal-map mean tilt: `coarse` is 7.7 degrees and it has the most screen area
  in the game.** Bark is 22.8. A surface family with no relief cannot respond to
  a moving sun no matter what the grade does. **`coarse` no longer has the most
  screen area: `stone` (mean 17.18, max 74.31) took the host rock at RN-742, and
  what is left on `coarse` is soil, sand, regolith, rubber and the loose item
  chunks.** The 7.7 figure is still the field's own and still low.

> **THE STALENESS TRAP THIS SECTION SET, recorded because it cost two lanes and
> is the most reusable thing on this page.** The `panel` 0.032 bullet was written
> on 2026-08-01 in the same commit range as RN-331..352. `RN-553` re-authored
> `_panel_masks` and opened the band to 0.184 **the same day, four commits
> later**, with the widening named in its own commit subject. Nobody edited the
> bullet back, and `of_panel_orm.png` changed three more times afterwards. Twelve
> days on, that one sentence had become: the scope audit's "THE headline defect",
> the ART-CAMPAIGN plan's line 13 and its A2b task, and **the stated CAUSE in
> RN-1415** for why raising the PMREM cube bought nothing. Three documents and one
> lane's conclusion, all resting on a number that had been false since the
> afternoon it was written. The `ore` "0.28 to 0.37" in the same bullet was never
> right at all under any palette this repo has shipped, and looks like a copy of
> item 5's unrelated "0.28 to 0.37 m" AO radius three bullets down.
>
> **The rule that follows: a measured number in this file is a claim about bytes
> at a date, and a lane that quotes one to justify work must re-measure it first.**
> It is ten seconds of arithmetic off the shipped PNG. Two lanes spent a day each
> on the strength of not doing it.
- **Foliage cards carry VALUE only.** `of_grass_a.png` and `of_leaf_a.png` have a
  maximum absolute R-minus-B of 6 counts. Because `Surfaces.ts` divides
  `material.color` by the scalar `albedo_mean`, **only the card's spatial
  variance and its hue survive; its mean level cannot.** Author variance and hue
  into the card; author level into the palette or `FoliageTone.ts`.

### 5. Contact and occlusion, and the number that is currently wrong

- Cascade 0: **15.47 mm per shadow texel** over 0 to 22 m on the high tier, PCF
  kernel one texel. The 22 m boundary is a **3.64x** step with no blend.
- **AO and contact are clamped in SCREEN space and the clamps BIND inside 4.87 m
  and 4.38 m.** At a standing eye the AO radius is 0.28 to 0.37 m against a
  nominal 0.9 m, and the contact march is 0.15 to 0.21 m against 0.45 m. Both
  are fixed-tap, so widening them costs cache locality, not arithmetic. **Price
  this at Plains (the most expensive frame) before changing it.**
- `AO_APPLY_FS` multiplies TOTAL radiance and the terrain has no ambient channel,
  so **AO attenuates direct sun on terrain**. `aoStrength` 0.9 and `csStrength`
  0.72 are the entire compensation.

### 6. The traps that cost this pass time, so they cost the next one none

- `__ofPost.state().sun` **freezes below the horizon**. Use
  `of.stats().sky.elevationDot`.
- A luma-only instrument reads ~0 on a hue-only change. A grade moves both.
  Decode RGB.
- **`--strictPort` fails the NEW server and the OLD one keeps answering 200.**
  Kill by PID and confirm the port is free before serving. It fired here.
- A flag's DEFAULT is a fixture. `Number(null)` is 0, so parse a missing
  parameter as MISSING and assert the boot default in its own named check.
- Measure at **four** sites, not three. Three green biomes agreed with each other
  and Beach contradicted all of them (RN-334).

**RN-1950 to RN-1955 (`lane/station-light`), 2026-08-16: TWO INSTRUMENTS THAT

**THE FINDING: EVERY RATIO PUBLISHED FOR THIS SHOT, INCLUDING THIS LANE'S, IS AN
UNDERSAMPLED MAX-OVER-MIN OF A BIMODAL PROCESS.** The station shot does not have
a "spread". It has a MODAL frame it returns to bit-identically, and an EXCURSION
that lands roughly one run in seven. At n of five to eight, max/min is a draw
from that rate, not a property of the build, and it is why the number keeps
changing between passes while nobody changes the lighting: **16.4x, 5.8x, 3.71x,
2.36x and this lane's own 5.88x are all the same non-measurement.** The
verifier's post-off arm at n of 14 shows the shape outright: **eleven readings at
18.30 and 18.31, then 34.52 and 85.62.** Eleven values agreeing to two decimal
places is not a process with a 4.68x spread; it is a tight mode plus two
excursions, and a max/min over six draws would have called it 1.37x (which is
exactly what this lane did call it) or 4.68x depending only on which six.

**WHAT TO REPORT INSTEAD, and what the next lane owes:** the EXCURSION RATE and
the two modes, at an n large enough to see the rate, plus the thing nobody has
yet asked — WHAT DISTINGUISHES AN EXCURSION FRAME FROM A MODAL ONE.
`tools/smoke/pngdiff.mjs` already shows this is answerable: a modal-vs-modal pair
moves **0.37%** of pixels (2030 darker / 2168 lighter, the ambient noise this
file already characterises) while a modal-vs-excursion pair moves **63.43%**
(172536 / 550422). That is a large, structured, both-directions difference
sitting in front of an instrument that can read it. Chasing it with more arms at
n of six cannot work, and this lane is the demonstration.

**THE TWO INSTRUMENT DEFECTS, WHICH ARE THIS LANE'S REAL CONTRIBUTION AND ARE
CONFIRMED.** Both were the basis of standing claims in this section.

*`staleMaxM: 0` COULD NEVER HAVE SEEN A WRONG ROLL.* `StationView.staleness()`
differences `m[12..14]` against `origin.toEngine(pos)`, i.e. the TRANSLATION and
nothing else, so a hull drawn at ANY orientation reports a hard zero and
`drawnParts: 2`. CE-115..117's pose claim rested on it. `stats()` now publishes
`quat`, `posB` and `posE`, the values `sync` actually composes.

*`originF`/`dirF` ARE NOT THE CAMERA.* The fields three separate passes used to
certify this shot "reproducible to FULL FLOAT PRECISION" come from `of.aim()`,
which returns `Controller.view.eye`: the f64 body-frame eye at the FIXED TICK.
`Loop.drain` then runs `observer.interpolate(alpha)` (line 411), converts through
the FLOATING ORIGIN (424) and calls `rig.setView` (425), so `aim()` can see
neither step. `of.stats().cam` now publishes `rig.nearCam`'s real engine
position, quaternion, fov, near and far — the camera that actually rasterises.

Measured through the corrected instruments, the pose and camera ARE bit-identical
across a modal and an excursion capture, so CE-115..117 holds and now has
evidence behind it rather than a certificate that could not have failed.

**AND A THIRD, WHICH THIS LANE BOTH FOUND AND THEN FELL INTO.** `run.mjs` runs
the probe (line 603), settles (607) and only then reads `stats` and `world`
(610). By that point this shot's walker is off the deck entirely:
`stationDraw.visible` false, `eyeDistM` 420355 m, `observer.altM` **1.62**. Every
counter taken from that block — `draw.triangles`, `chunksBuilt`, `shadow.active`
— describes a different frame than the photograph. **This lane read
`shadow.active: true` from it and built a whole mechanism on top, on a shot where
the rig is off.** Use the capture-instant reads in `captureDiag`.

**RULED OUT, and these survive verification.** The IBL is out, and it is the
result worth keeping: `?ibldiag=noenv` assigns NULL instead of the PMREM texture
and changes nothing else (RN-1526 built it for exactly this), and the excursions

every capture this shot has ever taken** — `SkyIbl.stats()` has published it all
along and no pass had read it — so the 40x Ocean-to-Polar albedo swing the ground
hemisphere can carry is not firing. Also flat across modal and excursion frames:

24.0279, `tick - stampedTick` a constant 272) and the headlamp
(`skyVis`/`rawVis`/`sunScale`/`ambient`/`lampCd`), which had exactly the right
shape — it drives the cone, the hemisphere ambient AND `sunScale` on a 0.12/0.6 s
time-driven adapt — and is not doing it. `ibl.builds` (9 to 12) and `scStamped`
(117 to 150) move freely across bit-identical frames and predict nothing.

**STRUCK, WITH THE CODE THAT REFUTES EACH.** Recorded because a ledger that only
carries the conclusions that survived teaches nobody where the trap was.

- **"The post stack is the amplifier" (1.37x): FALSE.** n of 6 missed an
  excursion. At n of 14 the post-off arm reads 4.68x. The corollary that every

- **The proposed layer-mask mechanism: FALSE, and refuted by a comment I read

- **The proposed next experiment (`?cascades=1`): MISCONCEIVED.** No such flag

- **`?shadowcast=0` therefore CANNOT MOVE A PIXEL ON THIS SHOT**, since casting

### 7c. THE STATION SHOT'S BIMODALITY, COUNTED AND THEN CLOSED (RN-2030 to RN-2038, 2026-08-19, `lane/station-bimodal`)

> **THIS ENTRY WAS CORRECTED BY ITS OWN FRESH-CONTEXT VERIFIER BEFORE MERGE.**
> The rate, the classifier, the separator and the fix all reproduced. **The
> MECHANISM PARAGRAPH DID NOT, and the original is struck below rather than
> quietly rewritten.** Two numeric claims are also weakened to what the data
> actually supports. The fix is unaffected: it removes the negative alpha that
> is the common cause of both the wrong story and the right one.

**THE SHOT IS FIXED AND THE CAUSE IS ONE MISSING CLAMP.** `Loop.step` clamped
the frame delta at the TOP only (`Math.min(dtIn, 0.25)`, a stalled-tab guard)
and said nothing about the bottom. `Loop.frame` builds that delta as
`(rAF now - lastMs) / 1000`, and rAF's `now` is the timestamp of the frame's
own start rather than of the moment the callback runs, while `Loop.run` hands
control back to rAF having just stamped `lastMs` from `performance.now()`. The
delta can therefore be NEGATIVE, which drives `acc` negative and `alpha`
negative. RN-2035 is `Math.min(Math.max(dtIn, 0), 0.25)` in
`web/src/app/Loop.ts`.

> **SUPERSEDED IN ITS MECHANISM, NOT IN ITS FINDING (CE-130 / CE-131, 2026-08-19).** The paragraph above is still the correct history and RN-2035 is still in the file, but it is no longer the whole fix: `lastMs` is now stamped ONLY from the rAF timestamp, so the delta cannot be negative in the first place, and `renderTick` clamps its alpha to match the two observers, so an out-of-range alpha could not reach the drawn hull even if one arrived. See `core-engine.md` §5o.

**WHAT A NEGATIVE ALPHA ACTUALLY DOES, AND IT IS AN ASYMMETRY BETWEEN TWO
CONSUMERS RATHER THAN A MOVING CAMERA.** The eye does NOT extrapolate.
`Controller.interpolate` and `VesselObserver.interpolate` both open with
`alpha <= 0 ? 0 : alpha >= 1 ? 1 : alpha`, so at a negative alpha the camera
is pinned to the previous integer tick and stops dead. What extrapolates is
the DRAWN HULL: `Loop`'s `renderTick` is `tickIndex - 1 + alpha` and it is
handed UNCLAMPED to `mounts.syncWatchersAt`, so `CarrierFrame.poseAt` places
the station at a fractional tick BEFORE the one the camera is frozen at. **The
camera stands still and the station slides out from under it.**

**MEASURED, AND IT IS UNAMBIGUOUS.** Across the 62 excursion runs of this
lane's own census, `phCamPosE` takes **ONE distinct value** and `phDrawPosE`
takes **62**; `phCamQuat` takes one and `phDrawQuat` takes 61. Across the 46
modal runs, where alpha is inside [0, 1) and neither consumer clamps, the two
move TOGETHER: 45 distinct values each. The separation grows linearly with the
overshoot, `eyeDistM = 4.098 + 30.07 * |alpha|` fitted over all 62
(the verifier's independent sample reads 29.6 m per unit alpha), against a
nominal 4.316 m and a deck that is 31.32 m of travel per tick.

> **STRUCK, AND RECORDED RATHER THAN DELETED.** This entry first said the
> negative alpha made `observer.interpolate` "extrapolate the eye BACKWARDS
> past the previous tick". **That is false and the clamps above refute it.** It
> was reached by reading `Loop.step` and `stationDraw.eyeDistM` and never
> reading the two `interpolate` bodies that consume the number, then confirmed
> against an `eyeDistM` that moves under EITHER story because it is a
> DIFFERENCE of two positions and says nothing about which one moved. The
> distinct-value counts above were sitting in the same ledger the whole time
> and were not taken. The lesson is this file's own: a quantity that both
> hypotheses predict is not evidence for either.

**THE RATE, AT n = 108 PER ARM, INTERLEAVED.** Two vite previews served the
unfixed and the fixed build on two ports and `pairdrive.mjs` ran one run of
each arm back to back, 108 pairs in three batches, so the arms are one variable
apart under one load rather than a serial before and after (WG-189).

| arm | n | excursions | rate | Wilson 95% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped | 108 | 62 | **57.41%** | **[47.99%, 66.32%]** |
| RN-2035 | 108 | **0** | **0.00%** | **[0.00%, 3.43%]** |

A confirmation batch on the committed tree with a quiet box read 8 of 14
shipped and 0 of 14 fixed. The fresh-context verifier, on its own build and
its own frames, read **20 of 30 shipped and 0 of 30 fixed** and confirmed
separately that driven runs are untouched by the clamp.

**"ROUGHLY ONE RUN IN SEVEN" WAS ITSELF AN UNDERSAMPLED ESTIMATE, AND IT IS
CORRECTED HERE.** The excursion fires on more than half of all runs on this
box. The task this lane inherited named 1 in 7; the measured rate is four times
that, and the earlier figure was a draw from the same small-n problem as every
ratio the shot has ever published.

**THE CLASSIFIER, AND THE GAP STATED HONESTLY ACROSS TWO SAMPLES.**
`pngdiffmany.mjs` against one designated modal reference, `pngdiff.mjs`'s own
6-count max-channel arithmetic, whole frame, **threshold 5% of pixels moved**.
On this lane's 108 shipped runs the 46 modal runs land in **[0.131, 0.663]%**
and the 62 excursions in **[39.173, 66.22]%**, and the full pairwise matrix
over 24 evenly spaced frames, 276 pairs, put none of them between 1% and 30%.
**That last claim does not survive a second sample and is withdrawn as a
general statement:** the verifier's independent run found 1 pair of 276 at
28.34% and two reference distances inside the band, giving a separation band of
0.611% to 20.304% on their data. **What both samples agree on is that the band
is wide, that nothing lands near 5%, and that the threshold is therefore not a
tuned parameter** - the narrowest empty band across both samples is still
[0.663%, 20.304%], a factor of 30. The clusters are real; their exact edges are
sample-dependent and should be quoted as such.

**WHICH INSTRUMENT SEPARATES THE MODES: `alpha` ON THE PHOTOGRAPHED FRAME, AND
IT IS PERFECT.** `phAlpha < 0` classifies all 108 shipped runs with **62 true
positives, 0 false positives, 0 false negatives, 46 true negatives**, and the
verifier reproduced it at 20/0/0/10 on their own sample. Equivalently and on
exactly the same runs, `stationDraw.eyeDistM` leaves its 4.316 m for up to
**15.34 m**. Even the smallest negative draw seen, alpha -0.046, moved 47.11%
of the pixels, which is why the process reads as BIMODAL rather than as a
continuum: alpha's sign is close to a coin flip and the smallest losing draw
already slides the hull more than a metre.

**AND NO PUBLISHED INSTRUMENT SEPARATES THEM, WHICH IS WHY FIVE PASSES COULD
NOT.** Over all 108 shipped runs, spanning both clusters, these take exactly
ONE distinct value each: `captureDiag.camF.posE`, `camF.quat`,
`stationDraw.quat`, `stationDraw.posE`, `eyeDistM`, `sunBearingDeg`, the draw
block, `iblSettleIters`, `vitals` and `shadow`. `ibl.builds` takes 9 values and
the headlamp 57, and neither predicts anything: the FIXED arm carries 29
headlamp values and 9 build counts with zero excursions. **The reason is
structural. Every one of those readings is taken on a DRIVEN frame before the
photograph, where alpha is the deterministic 0.2328482328482305 every single
time.** RN-2031 measured the gap: `preCapture` matches `captureDiag` to every
digit, and `atCapture`, taken when the blob encode resolves, is up to 404 ticks
and 1947 frames later. Neither is the photograph. RN-2034's `photoCapture` is.

**THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF ONE INSTRUMENT TRAP IN THIS SHOT.** RN-1954
found `run.mjs` reading its stats block two settle windows after the probe
returns. RN-1955 found `of.aim()` is the fixed-tick eye and not the camera, and
built `of.stats().cam` to replace it. RN-2031 finds that the replacement is
itself read on the wrong frame. And the outermost case is worse than any of
them: **`run.mjs --out` on the `station` shot is not a picture of the station
at all.** `artframe.js` returns the walker to the ground before it resolves, so
the settled playwright screenshot is the RN-352 forest at 1.62 m altitude. Every
frame in this census is `eval.png`, the probe's own in-page `of.screenshot()`,
and that is the only frame definition this shot admits.

**WHERE THE DIFFERING PIXELS LIVE: THE WHOLE FRAME, WITH NO STRUCTURE, AND
THAT IS THE ANSWER.** Not the hull alone, not the terrain limb, not the sky,
not a glow region. On a modal-versus-excursion pair the mask moves 67.03% of
the frame with every one of 48 grid cells between 29% and 95%. **The DIRECTION
of the change is not a stable property and an earlier draft of this entry
overstated it:** this lane's two masks disagree with each other (502,998 darker
against 462,267 lighter on one pair, 527,564 against 72,060 on another) and the
verifier's deepest excursion read 506,921 against 463,492. **Nor is the
excursion view a single picture:** the hull slides further at larger |alpha|,
so the camera ends up inside a bulkhead on some draws and outside against the
star field on others, and both have now been photographed. The stable, checked
statement is whole-frame displacement with no spatial structure, which is what
a moved subject predicts and a lighting change does not.

**LOAD SENSITIVITY: NO.** Batch rates 65.00% [49.51, 77.87], 47.50% [32.94,
62.50] and 60.71% [42.41, 76.43] over three batches spanning 02:43 to 04:13,
with run wall-times p50 25.6 s, 25.3 s and 24.5 s. The intervals overlap
heavily and no batch is separated from the pooled rate. The fixed arm reads
zero in all three. **Note also that the negative delta is not confined to the
first live frame after a driven window**, which this entry originally implied:
the verifier measured negative deltas recurring throughout live rAF (1408
frames median against 401 at equal tick counts). The clamp covers all of them.

**WHAT THIS RETIRES.** Every ratio ever published for this shot, this lane's
predecessors' included: 16.4x, 5.8x, 3.71x, 2.36x, 5.88x. On the shipped arm
this census reads 54 distinct box lumas from 6.18 to 41.72, a 6.75x
max-over-min, and the number would have been anything at all depending on which
six runs were drawn. On the fixed arm it reads **two values, 12.92 and 12.93**,
across 108 runs.

**FLAGGED TO ADMIN, NOT ROUTED HERE.** RN-2035 lands in `web/src/app/Loop.ts`,
which is CORE-ENGINE's file and not this domain's. Admin is routing the

**WHAT IS NOT CLOSED.** The shot's grade is still not SET here: this lane

### 7a. THESE SEVEN SHOTS CANNOT SEE THE MID FIELD (RN-1859, 2026-08-16, `lane/fade-nyquist`)

Recorded here rather than in a decision row alone, because it is a property of
the shot set and the next lane to change anything at range will hit it too.

RN-1855 moved the two terrain footprint fades, which act between a **0.026 m and
a 1.4 m pixel footprint**, i.e. on ground roughly **7 m to 44 m** from a standing
eye. Measured at three sites that band moves by 27 to 61 per cent of `iqr`. All
six MEASURED shots above were re-taken on that build in a before/after pair one
URL flag apart, and **five are bit-identical in luma, warm, sat and iqr while
`basedusk` differs by 0.01 luma**. Section 2.1's four-site table is the same
story: `groundNear` bit-identical at all four sites, `groundFar` bit-identical,
`groundMid` 0.0 to 0.6 counts, masked-ground p50 0 or 1 count.

The reason is that every canonical rectangle sits on a machine, on a structure,
or on ground within 5 m of the eye under a 0.02 m footprint. **A visible,
three-site, forty-per-cent change to the ground a player is actually walking
toward is invisible to every published baseline this project has.** That is a
gap in the shot set, not evidence that nothing happened, and the cheapest fix is
one more canonical shot at pitch -10 with rectangles placed by RANGE rather than
by fraction (`groundnear.js` now does the placing: `{"rangeRects":[8,18,25,35]}`
inverts `rangeAtRow`, and every rectangle prints its own `footM`).

**CLOSED BY RN-1906 (2026-08-16, `lane/midfield`): the shot exists and it is
`artframe.js`'s eighth, `midfield`.** Plains (-7.9675, 116.53189), standing eye
1.62 m, yaw 150, pitch -10, sun dot 0.70, props off, three 5-row strips at
18 / 27 / 35 m (`footM` 0.257 / 0.572 / 0.957). Its `box` IS the 27 m strip so it

ground moves the eye they disagree out loud instead of one quietly naming the
wrong range. On the RN-1900 build all six agree to the digit.

**AND THE YAW IS PART OF THE FIXTURE, NOT A DETAIL.** At RN-1857's yaw of 300
two dark loose-stone rocks and the far tree line fall inside the 35 m strip, and

by a handful of very dark outliers. Yaw 150 is clean ground to the horizon at
this site and the two statistics agree. Any future strip at range wants that

**THE SHOT SET'S REMAINING KNOWN HOLE, named here so it is not rediscovered:**

whose luminance rule weight is 0.487; Forest takes the full 1.000 and is where a

## 2.8 THE LOOK AUDIT (RN-1710 to RN-1726, 2026-08-15, `lane/look-audit`). WHAT STILL READS UNFINISHED, RANKED

All seven canonical shots re-captured at current `main` on real Windows D3D11
(ANGLE, RTX 4060 Ti), 1600x900, HUD-free through `of.screenshot()`, `post: true`
asserted by the probe on every frame, in `docs/screenshots/RN1710_audit_*.png`.
This is the queue for the next art waves. It is ranked by **how much a player's
impression moves per unit of work**, which is not the same order as either
severity or area.

**Nothing on this list was both cheap and high impact, and this lane therefore
landed no art change.** The two candidates that looked cheap were measured and
each failed: see R3 and R5 below and the decision rows for RN-1715 and RN-1717.

### QUEUE ORDER, CORRECTED (`lane/audit-corrections`, RN-1727, 2026-08-15)
The list below is still filed as R1 through R7 -- those labels are cited
elsewhere (RN-1730..1814's own allocation rows, `ART-CAMPAIGN-2026-08-13.md`'s
summary table) and are kept stable on purpose -- but **the PRESENTATION order
this audit originally shipped contradicted the metric its own header names.**
The header says the queue is ranked by impression-per-unit-work, explicitly
not by severity or area, and then filed R1 (ground material) first while R1's
own entry concedes it is "ranked first on area alone" and is "the last item
here that could ever be cheap" -- the opposite of what the stated metric would
put first. Found and re-derived by this correction's own fresh-context
verifier, independently of the audit that produced the list.

Re-ordered by the audit's own stated metric, reading each entry's own cost
tier against its own frame share and fix-cost text:
**R3 (MEDIUM, highest impression-per-work of anything that is a bounded
wave), R6 (SMALL-MEDIUM, tiny area but the eye lands there first), R2
(MEDIUM-LARGE, a real budget saving attached), R5 (SMALL-MEDIUM, a harness fix
that unblocks judging the campaign's own climax destination), R4 (MEDIUM,
blocked on a scope ruling rather than on cost), R7 (SMALL but frozen by
Early Decision 1, so it buys nothing until that decision changes), R1 (LARGE,
and the one item that could never be cheap).** This is a re-ordering of how
the seven are PRESENTED, not a renumbering of them, so every existing
cross-reference to "R1" through "R7" by label is unaffected.

**R1 is not dropped, and it is already being worked.** It is last by the
metric this queue names, but Reid's standing directive is that the game
should look close to done, and R1 is the largest single element in five of
the seven canonical shots (§2.1's own frame-share reading, below) -- so area
matters on its own terms even where the work is large, and RN-1730 to
RN-1759 is already allocated to it. Last-by-metric and being-worked are not a
contradiction once both are stated; leaving R1 unstated here is what would
have been the actual error.

### The rectangles, committed (`lane/audit-corrections`, RN-1727)
Every rectangle this section cites beyond the seven shots' own canonical
`box` -- the two untouched-terrain patches on `voxelface`, the peep port and
sight strip on `smelterhero`, the two sky bands on `basedusk` -- is now a
named entry in `artframe.js`'s `SHOTS.<shot>.extra` map, so the next reader of
this section reads them rather than grid-searching the PNGs the way this
correction's own verifier had to. See each shot's own manifest comment for
the exact rectangle and the verification it was checked against.

### The instrument, validated before it was believed
Rectangles that `artframe.js` was not told about at capture time were read off
the committed PNGs with a decoder carrying `statOn`'s arithmetic verbatim
(same luma weights, same `sat`, same percentiles, same `loFrac` at 0.10 and
`hiFrac` at 0.80). It was checked against the probe's own published figures
first and agreed **bit-identically on four rectangles across two shots**
(`forestfloor` box 28.22 / iqr 19.77 / loFrac 0.418; `smelterhero` box 47.42,
`sunface` 71.90, `band` 58.77). Readings below are only used because of that.

### R1. THE GROUND AT WALKING DISTANCE HAS A THIRD OF THE SURFACE VARIATION OF THE MACHINE STANDING ON IT
- **Measurement.** On `voxelface`, eye about 1.5 m off the ground, two
  rectangles of untouched terrain read `iqr` **22.13** and **16.06** (p05 65.55
  and 80.75, `hiFrac` 0) — a smooth blur with no micro-detail. The dug cut face
  in the same frame reads `iqr` 36.78. In the same lighting family the smelter's
  clean plate (`sunface`) reads `iqr` **53.66** and its refractory column
  (`hearthL`) **63.40**.
- **Frame share.** The largest single element in five of the seven shots:
  effectively 100 per cent of `voxelface`, and roughly 45 to 60 per cent of
  `machine` and `forestfloor` below the horizon.
- **Fix and cost.** Per-biome tangent-space normal plus a detail albedo on the
  terrain shader. **LARGE, and already refused once with a reason**: A3 declined
  tangent-frame terrain this campaign (needs world-gen RN-45 per-chunk noise
  phase; float32 ULP is 0.0625 m at the Forge radius). This is a world-gen plus
  rendering wave, not an art wave.
- **CORRECTED, RN-1727: this is the biggest AREA in the frame, not the top of
  the queue's own stated metric.** It is the last item here that could ever be
  cheap, so by impression-per-unit-work (the metric this section's own header
  names) it is ranked LAST, seventh of seven -- see "QUEUE ORDER, CORRECTED"
  above. It is worked anyway, ahead of cheaper items, under RN-1730 to
  RN-1759, because Reid's directive is that the game should look close to
  done and area matters to him even where the work is large.

### R2. THE UNDERSTOREY IS FLAT CARDS, AND THE WHOLE NEAR-SHADOW BUDGET IS SPENT DRAWING THEM AT LOD0
- **Measurement.** `check_shadow_lod.py` put 46 subtrees at the **full 4.0x**
  multiplier at audit time, every cascade still on tier 0. **CORRECTED by
  audit-corrections, RN-1727: one of the 46 was the launch pad, and RN-1690 to
  RN-1696's own form pass (merged after this audit) has since moved the pad to
  2.0x, so the count going forward is 45.** The list is almost entirely
  foliage: all five `detail_cards` tiers, every `bush_scrub` tier, every
  `props_*` grass tuft, `tree_broadleaf` and `tree_conifer` Full/Half/Low.
  `tree_conifer` LOD1 deviates **1250.89 mm** from LOD0 and `tree_broadleaf`
  LOD1 **480.31 mm**, against cascade 1's 56.25 mm texel, so no cascade may draw
  a cruder tier. Only the two `_Stump` tiers (60.50 and 77.87 mm) earn cascade 2.
- **Frame share.** 30 to 45 per cent of the lower half of `forestfloor`,
  `ruin`, `basedusk` and `machine`.
- A5 already took the cards 256 -> 1024 px, so **resolution is not the remaining
  defect; geometry is.** The cards are 2 to 3 triangle spikes with hard alpha
  edges and no thickness, and they read as paper stuck in mud.
- **Fix and cost.** Cross-quad or three-plane cards with a bent normal, plus a
  shadow-safe LOD1 so the cascades stop paying 4.0x. MEDIUM-LARGE: an asset wave
  with a budget consequence attached, and the budget consequence is a saving.

### R3. MASONRY TILES AT 0.6 m AND THE RUIN IS 35.2 m WIDE, SO THE STRUCTURE HIGH-WATER MARK READS AS WALLPAPER
- **Measurement.** `surfaces.json` gives the `stone` family `tile_m` **0.6**;
  `ruin` is 35.2 x 11.4 x 35.2 m, so the cella wall carries about **59 repeats
  across and 19 up**. At the shot's own 34 m standoff the motif is ~15 px in a
  1600 px frame and forms a plainly visible regular lattice.
- **Frame share.** The ruin fills about a quarter of its own frame, and `stone`
  also carries `foundation` (4 m), `launch_pad` (24 m) and every boulder and
  prop rock, so it is on screen in most frames.
- **THE FREE KNOB WAS TESTED AND IS NOT THE FIX, AND THAT IS THE useful half of
  this entry.** `?tile=stone:1.8` (RN-953's own sweep, one multiply, no
  regeneration) visibly converts the wall from knurled wallpaper to stone, and
  the negative controls are perfect: on `smelterhero`, `box` 47.42, `sunface`
  71.90, `firebox` 29.81, `band` 58.77 and `plate` 41.00 are **bit-identical to
  the digit**, only the two stone rectangles move (`hearthL` iqr 63.40 -> 59.76,
  `hearthR` 21.74 -> 24.88), and `voxelface` is bit-identical too, which
  separately proves the dug face is **not** this family. But the family's
  consumers span **0.18 m (`items_atlas`) to 35.2 m (`ruin`), a factor of 195**,
  and at 1.8 a 1.4 m boulder carries **0.78 repeats** — under one, which is
  exactly the failure RN-953 named for `suitplate`. 1.2 was measured as the
  compromise and the crop shows the lattice still plainly there.
- **Fix and cost.** Split a `masonry` family (`tile_m` about 2.0) in
  `texgen.py` and point the ruin's, launch pad's and foundation's `Rock` roles
  at it. MEDIUM, and cheaper than it looks: `FAMILY_TILE_M` has exactly three
  uses in `texgen.py` (a print, the manifest's `tile_m`, and `texels_per_m`) and
  feeds no pixel generation, so a tile-size change alone moves **no texture
  bytes** and the byte-identical determinism gate is not at risk.
- Highest impression-per-unit-work of anything here that is a bounded wave.
- **CLOSED, in two passes (RN-1780 then RN-1835).** RN-1780 took the world
  scale (0.6 m -> 1.8 m, 59 repeats -> 19.6) and its verifier found that the
  wall still read as patterned cut cliff, because the field was still
  `stone`'s isotropic fracture. RN-1835 replaced the field with coursed
  ashlar: level courses, staggered head joints, a chamfered mortar bed at
  every boundary, per-block tone and wear, and rain wash running down from
  each bed. `cella` iqr **23.15 -> 29.20** and shaded `cellaDark`
  **4.93 -> 6.86** on real D3D11, with `sky` and `hill` bit-identical. See
  RN-1835 and RN-1836; the launch pad's share of the trade is stated in the
  latter rather than left for the pad lane to discover.
- **REOPENED AND CLOSED A THIRD TIME (RN-1970), on a finding neither earlier
  pass could see.** RN-1835's verifier measured the family as the MOST
  repetitive of the three architectural ones on the column-averaged
  autocorrelation of the rendered wall, while it measured the LEAST
  low-frequency height contrast: the residual repeat was entirely in the
  per-block ALBEDO tone, where ten independent draws averaged four at a time
  down a column gave the tile a light half and a dark half. The blocks are now
  blended across the face by an exhaustive assignment search, with a
  per-course tone and two within-block bedding terms that are column-neutral
  by construction. Column-averaged luma std **7.13 -> 3.35 counts** and its
  correlation at half a tile **-0.68 -> -0.05** on the shipped map, per-block
  contrast held at 0.247. See RN-1970 to RN-1979.

### R5. THE STATION SHOT IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE, SO THE STORYLINE'S CLIMAX DESTINATION HAS NO JUDGEABLE FRAME
- **Measurement.** Six captures of the identical command. Box luma **21.78,
  3.73, 5.69** at `timeOfDay` 0.35 and **8.76, 10.48** at the shipped 0.60: a

  black, which is the signature — the instrument pinning the sun works perfectly
  and is pinned to the wrong body. `pose.lonDeg` differs every run: 149.458,
  149.417, 149.329, 149.214, 148.874, 148.717.

  move the station, and `__ofPost.state().sun` is essentially **constant across
  every phase and every shot** in this lane's twenty-odd reports (its y
  component is exactly 0.3872324843550918 in all of them), which is consistent
  with a world-fixed sun and a rotating body. Under that, a phase pin cannot
  change the light on an orbiting subject at all. This extends §2.6's existing
  trap note ("`__ofPost.state().sun` freezes below the horizon") rather than
  contradicting it.
- **Found on the way, and it is a real doc/code contradiction:** `timeOfDay:
  0.60` ships while the manifest comment three lines above it says the shot
  takes phase 0.35. `git log -S` finds `timeOfDay: 0.60` in A0's own commit
  (3afaea1) and `timeOfDay: 0.35` in **no commit at all**.

  position**, which is a physics or core handle the probe does not currently
  have, or it needs re-siting. Ranked fifth for that reason: it buys a

"target grade" docs/` returns exactly one hit, the plan sentence that
