## 2.9 OWED, ROUTED OUT OF R4 (RN-1875, 2026-08-16, `lane/view-model`)

### THE VIEW-MODEL PASS HAS NO SHADOW TERM, AND IT IS THE LARGEST REMAINING LOOK DEFECT ON THE ONE ASSET IN EVERY FRAME
`Frame.ts` renders `scenes.viewModel` as pass 4 with its own camera and depth
range. Its lights are `Boot.ts`'s `addLighting(scenes.viewModel, sunDir, 3,
false)` -- a `DirectionalLight` at the same 3.0 the near sun carries, with
`castShadow` never set and no `ShadowRig` attached -- plus `Headlamp`'s
`vmHemi` and the shared `SkyIbl`. So the arms and the held tool are lit by a
sun **nothing can occlude**, in a frame whose world is shadowed by cascade 0.

**The measurement, four canonical shots, model pixels isolated by the RN-1876
`hideVm` control and differenced per pixel.** Model mean luma divided by the
same frame's own mean luma outside the model:

| shot | world luma | model luma | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voxelface` (sunlit pit, dot 0.88) | 98.55 | 54.20 | **0.55** |
| `ruin` (open approach, dot 0.35) | 81.74 | 100.42 | **1.23** |
| `forestfloor` (canopy shade, dot 0.70) | 29.92 | 82.71 | **2.76** |
| `machine` (shaded site, dot 0.45) | 31.48 | 105.91 | **3.36** |

**A 6.1x spread on a quantity that should be near 1 in every frame, and the
error changes sign.** That is what makes it a missing TERM and not a mistuned
constant, and it is why `lane/view-model` deliberately did not touch
`VM_HEMI`: `ruin`'s 1.23 is the control proving the absolute level is already
right wherever the sky is open, so any dimming that helped the two shaded
frames would break the two that are correct.

Second reading of the same fact, in one frame with no cross-shot comparison at
all: on `machine`, the smelter is a stock `MeshStandardMaterial` 5.19 m away in
the near pass and reads box luma **19.58 / warm -4.17**; the view model is the
same class of material 0.62 m away in pass 4 and reads **105.91 / +37.83**.

**What a fix would have to be.** Either cascade 0's shadow map read by a light
in the view-model scene, or the occlusion at the player's eye sampled once per
frame and applied as a scale on the pass-4 sun. The second is much the cheaper
and `Headlamp` already owns the shape of it (`sunScale`, driven from
`skyVis`), but `skyVis` is a ROCK-thickness oracle: it is 1.0 under a tree
canopy, which is exactly the `forestfloor` case. Rendering domain, not an art
wave.

**Also owed, feel workstream (A7):** the hand does not close on the haft.
RN-1880 put a cord grip wrap on the 20 cm the fist occupies, which gives the
fingers something to be closing on, and the bind pose still rests the hand on
top of the shaft rather than around it. Closing it is a bind-pose change plus a
`fp_grip` retune across all twelve `FP_*` clips.

## 2.9a THE VIEW-MODEL PASS NOW HAS A SHADOW TERM, AND IT DOES NOT FIX THE FOUR SHOTS (RN-1990 to RN-1997, 2026-08-16, `lane/vm-light`)

**WHAT LANDED.** `web/src/render/ViewModelLight.ts`. Pass 4's sun is named
`vmSun` in `Boot.ts`, and once per frame -- from inside `Frame.render`, after
the near pass and before the view-model pass, which is the only window in which
the term is this frame's -- it is handed **cascade 0's own shadow map**, bias,
normal bias, radius and map size, with cascade 0's shadow matrix
post-multiplied by a translation of the engine eye. That composition is the
whole trick: `CameraRig.setView` puts `vmCam` at the origin with the near
camera's orientation and `Avatar.placeViewModel` fixes the model there too, so
view-model space is engine space **translated** by the eye, with no rotation and
no scale, and a matrix that maps engine metres to shadow UV maps view-model
metres to the same UV after one translate. Nothing is re-rendered and no second
map is allocated: `vmSun.shadow.autoUpdate` and `needsUpdate` are both false,
which is the documented condition on which three's `WebGLShadowMap.render`
skips a light before it would draw into its map. `Avatar`'s FP rig now loads
with `receiveShadow: true` (it was false, and three's own line is
`receiveShadow ? getShadow(...) : 1.0`, so a wired light with unwired meshes is
a silent identity that reads exactly like the defect).

**COST**, WG-189's interleaved paired method, off phase
`__ofVmLight.receive(false)` -- which is the correct off phase and
`shadow(false)` is not: zeroing the shadow INTENSITY still calls `getShadow` and
still takes its five PCF taps, while clearing `receiveShadow` takes three's
other ternary arm and also skips this file's per-frame traverse. 5 interleaved
pairs of 4 s, real D3D11, RTX 4060 Ti: **median p50 8.30 -> 8.40 ms, delta
+0.10 ms against a 1.4 to 1.5 ms within-arm spread and 0.60 ms of off-arm drift,
not resolvable from zero.** Pass 4 itself 0.30 ms in both arms (spread 0.10).
Draw calls 74, programs 43, unmoved.

### AND NOW THE HONEST HALF: THE FOUR SHOTS DO NOT MOVE, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED

| shot | ratio before | ratio after | model/behind before | after | caster over the player? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `voxelface` | 0.577 | 0.569 | 0.676 | 0.668 | **no** |
| `ruin` | 1.000 | 1.030 | 3.409 | 3.469 | **no** |
| `forestfloor` | 2.320 | 2.323 | 2.696 | 2.647 | **no** |
| `machine` | 2.931 | 2.933 | 2.889 | 2.955 | **no** |
| `basedusk` | 0.950 | 1.005 | 3.348 | 3.598 | **no** |
| `station` | 4.134 | 3.977 | 1.812 | 1.750 | rig off in orbit |

Both arms are one variable apart **inside one page load**
(`__ofVmLight.shadow`), so this is not two scene builds compared. Every movement
above is inside the mask's own noise: the model's pixels are found by
differencing against a view-model-suppressed control, and foliage moving between
the two grabs swings the mask by 10 to 15 per cent, which is worth several
counts. `station` also demonstrates the stale-map guard: in orbit `ShadowRig`
clears `castShadow` on every cascade, and the term correctly reports shadow
intensity 0 in both arms rather than shadowing the arms with the last daylight
frame's trees.

**`casterHere` IS A MEASUREMENT, and it is the finding: the term is correct
and inert on all six canonical shots because none of them stands in a cast
shadow, and cascade 0 itself only ever receives props, never terrain.** This
used to be told in full here; it is now `RN-1993` in section 3, one source of
truth for the shot-set gap rather than two, and it is not this pass's to
close (see `RN-1993`'s own status).

**WHERE IT DOES BITE**, `probes/vmshade.js`, RN-352 forest site, sun dot 0.70,
81 stations scanned by the map and 19 measured with a matched on/off pair at
each: at the stations whose own texel holds a caster nearer the light,
**the model drops 9.87 counts, 19.9 per cent (n = 6)**, and the
model-over-world ratio moves **1.90 -> 1.51**; at the stations whose texel is
clear the same toggle moves it **4.82 counts (n = 13, and one degenerate
near-black station at world luma 4.4 carries 38 of that: the other twelve mean
about 2.0)** and the ratio moves **2.69 -> 1.97**. The clear-station residual is
owed and not a defect: the model spans 0.3 to 0.7 m and its pixels sample a
spread of texels around the eye's, so a leaf over the tip of the haft is a real
occlusion of a real pixel.

### TWO NEGATIVES WORTH MORE THAN THE POSITIVE

**1. THE AMBIENT IS NOT THE TERM, AND NOW THERE IS A NUMBER.** This lane built
the obvious mechanism fix -- derive `VM_HEMI`'s open-sky endpoint from the same
`stockFloor` call the near hemisphere reads, two lines away in `Headlamp.ts`, so
the two cannot drift -- and then sized the term before shipping it and reverted
it. On `forestfloor`, model luma 72.43: `__ofVmLight.ambient(0)` reads
**68.95**, so the whole view-model hemisphere is **3.5 of 72 counts, 4.8 per
cent**; `sun(0)` reads **22.32**, so the direct sun is **50.1 counts, 69 per
cent**; the remaining 17.8 is the shared sky IBL. A term worth 4.8 per cent
cannot move a ratio out by a factor of three. Worse, `stockFloor` returns
intensity 1.0 and carries its level in the COLOUR, so binding the INTENSITY to
it is arithmetically a multiply by one and the change would have read as a
mechanism and shipped as a retune. Recorded beside the constant in
`Headlamp.ts`. Taking the world's COLOUR as well is a real change and a
different one; it costs the arms their warm underground fill and it is worth
3.5 counts.

**2. RN-1875's "the ratio should be about 1" IS THE WRONG BAR, and the
four-shot spread is mostly the DENOMINATOR.** Across the four shots the model's
own luma spans 55.3 to 99.2 (**1.79x**) while the world it is held against
spans 24.1 to 82.8 (**3.43x**). A held tool with a fixed albedo in front of a
world whose albedo and incidence swing 3.4x cannot sit at 1 in all four frames,
and the sign change follows the world, not the model. The remaining defect on
those frames is therefore NOT a missing shadow map; it is that the model's
illumination barely responds to the shot at all, which is a question about the
pass-4 sun's incidence against a camera-locked rig and about the shared IBL, not
about occlusion. That is the next lane's item and it is now stated as a
measurement rather than as a ratio.

### THE INSTRUMENTS, WHICH ARE THE REUSABLE PART
* `artframe.js` `{"vmRatio": true}` and `{"vmArms": [...]}`: the model's own
  pixels by per-pixel difference against a `hideVm` control, three denominators
  published together (whole frame, frame-minus-model, and **the world the model
  occludes**, read out of the control frame at exactly the masked pixels), and
  N arms of `__ofVmLight` state measured in one page load. `ambientAbs` sets an
  ABSOLUTE hemisphere intensity, because a constant multiplier written into an
  invocation would measure a different ambient on every shot and call it one
  control.
* `probes/vmlight.js`: the wiring gate. Wired, receivers non-zero, the eye's
  shadow coordinate inside `getShadow`'s own frustum test, **the compiled
  programs actually carry a `directionalShadowMap` sampler** (read back through
  `onBeforeCompile`, because `castShadow` on the CPU and `USE_SHADOWMAP` in the
  shader are joined only by an ordering), and the map has casters in it.
* `probes/vmshade.js`: the behavioural gate, and its own two scars are the
  lesson. `of.look` takes a DELTA and `of.teleport` re-derives the tangent
  frame, so one correction lands short: the first walk **alternated between two
  yaws on odd and even stations**, which moved the cascade centre 7 m and made
  the eye's texel flip between unrelated cells every step, and the two
  populations it reported were the two yaws, not sun and shade. And measuring
  the model twice, each against its own fresh control, puts the wind clock into
  both halves of the subtraction; one control and one mask per station turned a
  12-count scatter on the negative-control stations into about 1.3.
* `probes/vmcost.js`: WG-189's interleave with `receive` as the off phase.

**A NULL THAT COST THREE MEASUREMENT PASSES, named so it costs none next time.**
With the term wired, receivers at 13 and shadow intensity at 1, all four shots
moved by less than the mask noise. "The arms are not in anybody's shadow here"
and "the lookup never lands" are the same number in a ratio table. Forcing the
shadow bias was tried first and **cannot work**: reversed depth puts the
comparison at `z >= stored`, and an empty texel stores 0, so no bias in `[0, 1]`
can shadow against it, and the forced-bias arm returns "lit" for exactly the
reason the real one does. Only reading the map itself separated them.

## 2.10 THE WORLD LOOK AUDIT (RN-2065 to RN-2075, 2026-08-19, `lane/world-audit`). DISTANCE, SKY AND THE AIR

Full document with every frame, every rectangle and the feasibility argument:
**[docs/web/WORLD-AUDIT-2026-08-19.md](../web/WORLD-AUDIT-2026-08-19.md)**. This
section is the pointer plus the deltas; the audit is the detail.

Section 2.8 audited the close and mid range on 2026-08-15 and its R1 to R7 are
unchanged by this pass. This one audits what 2.8 structurally could not see, for
the same reason RN-1859 gave about the mid field one range band earlier: **the
furthest subject any canonical shot framed was the ruin at 34 m.** Nine frames
inside forty metres cannot judge a horizon, and the world's weaknesses are past
it.

### THE FIVE NEW POSES, and why two of them needed a different scenario
`vista` / `vistadawn` / `vistanoon` are ONE pose (mtn, lat 2.036 / lon 144.056,
yaw 120, pitch -2, biome 5) differing in exactly one manifest field, so the day
arc is a controlled comparison at a fixed camera. Six frames were taken to
choose that site and five are recorded as rejects in the manifest, two of them
because the reject IS a finding (plains: the world visibly ends at the canopy
ring; hills2: distant snow reads as white paper over a black mid ground). The
other three are the same trap twice: **a high site is not a high view.** mtn at
yaw 300 and at yaw 210 both stand the eye on a slope facing uphill.

`flyover` (1,200 m) and `limb` (120 km) carry `--scenario=surface` and
`--scenario=orbit` in their own invocations, because **`Controller.teleport`
discards its third argument** (`_altM`, contract stated in `Controller.ts` and
`ConfigTypes.ts`), so no shot run under `--scenario=walk` can ever leave the
ground. The branch refuses on `observer.mode !== 'FLY'` and asserts the eye
altitude landed within `max(50, 2%)`, because a silently grounded flyover is
`station`'s three-pass failure in another costume: a frame that looks fine,
measures fine and is of the wrong thing.

### THE FOUR NUMBERS THE QUEUE IS RANKED ON
1. **The `?atmos=0` control splits one apparent defect into two.** At 1,200 m
   the horizon band is iqr **20.08** with the atmosphere and **89.17** without
   (-77.5%), while the ground straight down is **7.79** and **7.21** (unchanged).
   The white ground in that frame is the haze in its far half and terrain with
   no material in its near half, and either one alone reads as the other.
2. **The day arc inverts the frame.** One pose, 66.89 -> 44.31 -> 5.85 degrees:
   near scree **167.51 -> 134.14 -> 33.01**, far ridge **205.31 -> 198.86 ->
   231.51**, far-to-near ratio **1.23 -> 1.48 -> 7.01**.
3. **The sky brightens toward the sun and never reddens.** Sun-side against
   anti-sun at 5.85 degrees: **110.83 / 60.35, 1.84x**, so the integral resolves
   direction and the colour lane is TUNING. Horizon `warm` over the same 61
   degrees: **-101.06 / -91.87 / -86.23**, 14.83 counts and still deeply blue.
4. **The world empties when the eye leaves the ground.** `flyover` **188,081
   triangles at 1,200 m**, **231,089 at 400 m**, against **2,759,465** at a
   standing eye on plains, with no tree in any aerial frame and both `?atmos=0`
   controls proving absence rather than haze. The exact trigger is NOT diagnosed
   here and is the lane's first job: at 400 m the 620 m canopy ring still
   subtends a 474 m horizontal disc of ground and the frame is empty anyway.

### THE COST CEILING, WHICH GATES EVERY FIX ABOVE
The plains vista at a standing eye with nothing built is **2,759,465 triangles,
71 calls** on an RTX 4060 Ti at 1600x900: over `StatsProbe`'s ALERT triangle
threshold (2.7e6) and over the 16.6 ms frame budget on every box measured, at a
ratio of about 4.5x against the vista pose's cost (absolute milliseconds are
box-and-run-dependent: this audit's p50 read 32.1 ms on plains against readings
of 6.9 ms and 10.1 ms on `vista` for the same pose). `midfield` p99 **64.6
ms**, `ruin` p99 44.0 ms. Meanwhile the frame with the most DISTANCE in it,
`vista`, is 591,906 triangles: **distance is not what costs, the understorey
card population at LOD0 is.** That is the same fix as the vegetation gap, which
is why one lane buys both.

### THE QUEUE (severity, then storyline exposure)
Blocking: **1** aerial-perspective whiteout (a+b) · **2** no vegetation from the
air (b) · **3** no terrain material past ~75 m, and 75 to 600 m is a genuine
texture hole between the ground-texture fade at 35-75 m and the macro tint that
starts at 600 m (b) · **4** the cost ceiling (b, and (c) only if density AND
distance are both wanted) · **5** shadows stop at 300 m and the last cascade
paints a texel-staircase black region at altitude whose dark side FLIPS between
400 m and 1,200 m (b + a) · **6** the low-sun inversion (a+b) · **7** the 620 m
world edge, same lane as 2 (b).
Clearly behind: **8** sky colour, and the `aerosolTint` (0.38, 0.39, 0.43) is
blue-biased so the one term colouring every distant surface pushes the world
away from warmth at every hour (a) · **9** no clouds anywhere in `web/src` (a
for a dome layer) · **10** snow and rock read as flat paint (a) · **11** the
Ocean biome renders as blue TERRAIN and the good water shader is worn by one
pond (b) · **12** LOD ribbons on the shell at the terminator (b) · **13** stars
visible at 1,200 m in a blue sky (a).
Acceptable: **14** no large-scale AO · **15** the fixed day arc.
Unmeasured and said so: **16** the sun disc, because **no canonical frame in
this project contains it** · **17** foliage aliasing in motion.
At bar: **18** the limb at 120 km, which is the best frame the project has
(ring luma 93.27, iqr 101.39, sat 0.626 over a 0.10 sky; 52,913 triangles, 21
calls, p50 1.1 ms) · **19** the atmosphere's architecture, one analytic integral
whose uniform record is shared BY REFERENCE between the sky and both terrain
materials, so the horizon cannot disagree with the sky.

### THE FIVE LANES THIS BECOMES
**L1 haze** (1+6, shader-local, cheapest change and the largest number of
pixels, and every later lane is judged through frames it distorts) ·
**L2 distance vegetation** (2+7+half of 4, a third baked LOD rung and an
altitude-scaled canopy radius) · **L3 far terrain material** (3, normal-only
first, geometry handed to the ceiling study) · **L4 shadow reach** (5) ·
**L5 sky colour** (8+10+13+9's cheap half, all class (a), so an art pass can run
it while L2 and L3 are built).

### TWO THINGS FOUND ON THE WAY, NEITHER OF WHICH IS THIS AUDIT'S SUBJECT
**`artframe.js` could not run outside `--scenario=walk` and never had.** The
sandbox gate read `of.game().mode`; `of.game()` returns null with no gameplay,
so `flyover` died with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading
'mode')` out of `page.evaluate` before any shot code ran. Null-safe now, sandbox
rule unchanged for the shots that declare `needsSandbox`.

**`station` came back INTERIOR again** at RN-1935's `yawOff: 105`
(`drawEyeDistM` 4.316, `drawnParts` 2, `staleMaxM` 0; `alpha` varies per run
and stays inside [0,1] -- this audit read 0.924 -- so the RN-2035 clamp defect
is ruled out). Section 2.8 R5 stays open: INTERIOR is the stable fact and the
storyline's climax destination still has no judgeable exterior frame. Re-flagged
rather than re-diagnosed, because it is not a world-graphics question and this
lane had no mandate to reopen it.

## 2.11 THE TERRAIN NOW WEARS A MATERIAL, TO ABOUT SEVENTY-FIVE METRES (RN-2160 to RN-2169, 2026-08-19, `lane/a3-splat`)

Fidelity lane A3 phase 1, against
[`docs/web/FIDELITY-GAP-2026-08-19.md`](../web/FIDELITY-GAP-2026-08-19.md)
section 1 difference 2 ("their terrain wears materials; ours wears a palette")
and the world audit's gap 3 ("the terrain has no albedo, normal or ORM texture
at all"). Base `origin/main` at `f2a5e02f`. Server `127.0.0.1:4788`,
`--strictPort`, sentinel written into this worktree's own `dist` and fetched
back before the first probe, killed by the PID that owned the port (the other
lane's 4297 listener was still up afterwards, which is the check that the
teardown was not a blast radius).

### WHAT SHIPPED

`tools/blender/terraintex.py`, a third deterministic texture generator beside
`texgen` (mesh families) and `groundtex` (the terrain's detail maps), and
separate for the reason groundtex is separate from texgen: the SAMPLING
CONTRACT differs, not the pixels. Six layers, grass / dirt / rock / cliff /
scree / snow, one RGBA PNG each at 1024 px, **R albedo value, G normal x,
B normal y, A roughness detail, every channel centred on 0.5**.

Four channels and not eighteen maps because six layers x albedo/normal/ORM is
eighteen samplers and WebGL2 guarantees sixteen. An atlas needs `textureGrad`,
which GLSL ES 1.00 does not have; a `sampler2DArray` needs GLSL ES 3.00 and
therefore a port of all twenty-three terrain shader chunks. What made six
samplers enough is that the layer HUE and the roughness BASE are client
constants (`TerrainSplat.ts`), which is BiomePalette's own colour-authority
rule and texgen's "ALBEDO IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT" argument reused.

Shader side: `TerrainSplat.glsl.ts` and one block each in the albedo, bump and
light chunks. **No new draw call** -- this is the same terrain draw with more
fetches, inside a bare-uniform branch so `?splat=0` and the low tier cost
nothing rather than costing twelve fetches multiplied by zero.

### THE WEIGHT RULES, AND THE FACT THAT NONE OF THEM IS A NEW SELECTOR

`cover` is `coverSel`, the shipped slope smoothstep, so the splat cannot
disagree with the albedo, the grain and the relief about where a cliff starts.
`cliff` is a near-vertical band BELOW coverSel's own lower edge, so what lies
between them is rock. `scree` takes the steep domain's high half by
`vRelief / maxRelief`, the SAME altitude coordinate the snowline already uses.
grass/dirt split on `vMatW.x`, which is BiomeMaterial's grass-clump weight and
is already the game's answer to "how vegetated is this biome" -- reused rather
than duplicated as a seventh per-biome table, which would have cost a varying.
`snow` DISPLACES the other five rather than adding to them. The five are
normalised and scaled by `(1 - snow)`, so the six sum to **exactly 1** at every
fragment, which is what clause C3 below needs.

### THE CONVERGENCE RULE, WHICH IS THE ANSWER TO "WILL THE WORLD CHANGE COLOUR AS I WALK"

Stated in full in `TerrainSplat.ts`; four clauses, each arithmetic or asserted.
**C1** every channel of every layer has measured mean 0.5, asserted by
`terraintex check` on the SHIPPED BYTES (all four channels, all six layers,
tolerance 0.006), so a minified sample IS the palette colour, the geometric
normal and the palette roughness. **C2** the value term is mean-preserving per
channel (a centred field times a fixed tint), which is the macro tint's own
scar applied. **C3** the chroma term is luminance-preserving STRUCTURALLY: the
hue is a convex combination of Rec.709-unit-luminance vectors, luminance is
linear, and `assertHueLuminance` THROWS at module load if a row drifts. The
probe reads all six back at 1.000000 through `splatDefault().hueLuma`, so the
clause is observable and not merely asserted. **C4** both fade bands reach zero
inside the near field and neither is a new number: 35-75 m is texW's own band
and 30-60 m is the relief bump's.

### THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERED, AND IT SAYS C4 IS A BACKSTOP AND NOT THE MECHANISM

Three arms of `midfield` (the plains standing eye, props off by that shot's own
rule), one flag apart on one build, fresh process each.

| rectangle | `?splat=0` | fine rung only | fine + coarse rung |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 18 m strip iqr (footM 0.257) | 32.84 | 34.19 | 33.69 |
| 27 m strip iqr (footM 0.572) | **12.34** | 18.06 | **29.76** |
| 35 m strip iqr (footM 0.957) | 17.92 | **17.84** | **24.77** |
| whole-frame iqr | 44.27 | -- | **55.15** |
| box luma / world luma | 114.75 / 130.07 | -- | 112.71 / 128.87 |

The middle column is the finding. **With one rung the term did NOTHING at 35 m
(17.92 off against 17.84 on), and `?splatfade=300,600,300,600` moved that by
0.00 counts and the 27 m figure by 0.07.** So the fade bands were not what
retired the term: **clause C1 was, and it got there forty metres earlier than
the band was written for**, because at 35 m the pixel footprint is 0.957 m
against a 2 mm texel, which is mip 8. Nothing was broken. The material simply
stopped at a third of the near field, and no instrument in the lane would have
said so without the one-variable control.

The fix is the standard second rung, tapped from the SAME six textures at
`repeats / 4` (tiles 7.2 to 14.5 m) and cross-faded on the PIXEL FOOTPRINT over
0.15 to 0.60 m. **footM and not dist**, for the reason the whole material
already keys on it: at a grazing pose the dFdy arm binds and grows as the
SQUARE of the range, so a distance-keyed handover would swap rungs at one range
looking down and a completely different one looking along the ground.

### THE SECOND CONTROL, BECAUSE A 7 PER CENT LEVEL DROP HAD TO BE ATTRIBUTED

On the mountain-slope pose the full term takes the frame's level down 7.1 per
cent, which a convergence rule that claims to be mean-preserving owes an
explanation for. `?splatnrm=0` (value and chroma only, one flag) separates it:

| rectangle | splat off | value + chroma only | full |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| nearG luma | 164.66 | **165.56 (+0.5%)** | 160.26 (-2.7%) |
| nearG iqr | 20.07 | 31.00 (+54%) | 32.79 (+63%) |
| world luma | 113.24 | 111.96 (-1.1%) | 107.23 (-5.3%) |

**The albedo halves move the rectangle where the term is strongest by +0.5 per
cent**, which is C2 and C3 holding. The whole of the darkening is the NORMAL
term, and it is Lambert's own response to a surface that now has relief: a
facet turned away is clamped at zero and its neighbour turned toward the sun
cannot pay it back. That is the material appearing, not the palette moving.

### BUDGETS

**Textures** 32.0 MiB as RGBA8 with a full mip chain (six 1024 px layers),
8,880,037 B on disk, so the ceiling study's 104 of 260 MB becomes **136 of
260**. **A CAVEAT ON THE INSTRUMENT: `render.vramMB` read 104.2 in BOTH arms of
every pair**, so it is not counting these uploads and must not be quoted as
evidence about them; the 32.0 MiB is computed and published in
`of_terrain.json`, not measured by the probe. **Texture units** 6 of a
guaranteed 16, on top of the 2 the ground maps already take. **Draw calls
47 -> 47** and triangles identical in every pair. **Frame**, three
fresh-process pairs on the heaviest pose, ratio framing because absolute
milliseconds are box-and-run dependent: terrain pass **3.0-4.6 ms** off against
**3.0-5.3 ms** on, frame p50 **4.4-4.7** against **4.4-5.0**. The ranges
overlap completely, so twelve fetches per terrain fragment are under this
instrument's noise floor on this pose. **That is not a claim of exactly zero.**

### THE HERO FRAMES, JUDGED HONESTLY

`docs/screenshots/RN2160_{meadow,vista,mtnslope}_{before,after}.png`.

**MEADOW (`midfield`, plains standing eye).** Moved, and it is the difference
the gap analysis asked for. The before frame is a smooth olive wash that has
lost all structure by about twenty metres; the after frame carries a fibrous
sward out to roughly forty. It reads as a surface rather than as a painted
plane. It is not yet grass: the blade grain is strongly directional and at a
grazing eye it reads as BRUSHED rather than as blades, and the near foreground
is busier than it should be. **Section 1 difference 2 partially closed at this
pose; difference 1 untouched (that is A2's carpet).**

**VISTA (`vista`, the 4.7 km ridge).** Barely moved, and correctly so. `nearG`
went iqr 27.93 -> 29.28 and `world` saturation 0.354 -> 0.364; the horizon band
is **3.00 in both arms to the digit**, `mid` is 15.21 in both, and every sky
rectangle is bit-identical. This is the convergence rule visible as a
non-result: the splat touches the near band and leaves the distance exactly
where it was. **Section 1 difference 2 NOT closed at this pose. The vista is
the haze lane's frame and phase 2's, and this lane should not be credited with
it.**

**MOUNTAIN SLOPE (`mtnslope`, the eye on a slope facing uphill).** The
largest move in the set: `nearG` iqr 20.07 -> 32.79 (+63%), `mid` 42.65 ->
56.49 (+32%), saturation 0.152 -> 0.211, warmth 25.1 -> 34.8. The before
frame's substrate is a pale grey-white wash with soft blotches under sharp rock
props, which is the "table with objects on it" reading one substrate up; the
after frame has continuous gritty tonal structure and the props stop
contradicting the ground they sit on. Honestly, though, it reads as **dust and
grit rather than as scree**: the scree layer's flat-facet structure does not
survive to this range, and much of this slope sits in the cover/steep
transition where the weights hand it dirt and rock rather than scree.
**Section 1 difference 2 substantially closed at this pose.**

**THE POSE IS A COMMITTED SHOT NOW, AND IT WAS NOT WHEN THIS SECTION WAS FIRST
WRITTEN.** The frames above were originally taken by overriding `vista` on the
command line (`--evalargs='{"shot":"vista","yaw":300,"pitch":-8}'`), which
photographs correctly and RECORDS NOTHING: a fresh-context verifier reproduced
the +63 per cent ratio at a guessed pose and a different absolute level, which
is the whole failure mode. `mtnslope` is now a row in `artframe.js`'s `SHOTS`
with a documented invocation, and **every committed rectangle reproduces to the
digit** across all three arms (before nearG 164.66 / 20.07, after 160.26 /
32.79, `?splatnrm=0` 165.56 / 31.00), so no figure in this section moved. Only
the whole-frame `world` rectangle differs, by 0.1 counts of luma and 0.12 of
iqr, which is the per-process settle-tick variance NUMBERS.md already documents
and is not a committed rectangle.

Its rectangles are `vista`'s fractions to the digit so these frames stay
readable against the row, but **three are renamed and not moved**: at yaw 300
the slope fills the frame, so the boxes `vista` calls `skyL`, `skyR` and
`skyHz` land on GROUND here and are `upL`, `upR` and `upC` in this shot. A
rectangle whose name asserts a subject it does not contain would have published
three "sky" luminances measured off a mountainside. `hzBand`, `mid`, `nearG`
and `box` keep their names because at this pose they still mean what they say,
and it is `nearG` that every figure above is quoted on.

**AND COMMITTING IT FOUND A LIVE DEFECT IN THE PROBE.** `artframe.js`'s pose
dispatch is a flat chain of `if (name === ...)` blocks with **no final else**,
so a shot that is in `SHOTS` and in none of those blocks is never posed: it
photographs wherever the walk scenario spawned, and `valid`, the rectangles,
the sun solve and the render stats are all perfectly correct about the wrong
place. `mtnslope` did exactly that on its first run (`setup: {}` and `vramMB`
82.4 against this site's own 104.2) and was caught only because this lane
already knew what the right numbers looked like. Fixed for `mtnslope` by adding
it to the vista branch, and named in a comment on that line so the next author
of a shot sees it; the general guard is not this lane's to add, because it
touches nine other shots' code paths.

### OWED, AND THE CROSS-DOMAIN CONTRACT

- **Phase 2, the 75 to 600 m band**, is the third rung. It wants a different
  COORDINATE as well as a different scale, and that is the contract: past the
  max-depth ring the chunk UV's world size doubles at every LOD step, so a far
  rung needs **world-gen's per-chunk phase attribute reduced mod the tile
  period on the CPU in float64**. `TerrainArt.glsl.ts`'s own header already
  names it and already assigns it to world-gen; this lane is the second
  consumer to need it and the first for which it is load-bearing rather than a
  nicety. Adding a third rung on the chunk UV would put a scale step in the
  exact band phase 2 has to make seamless.
- **Anti-tiling is partial and is not claimed otherwise.** Three free things
  ship (a chunk-periodic UV warp at 0.006 UV, chosen as a DERIVATIVE budget of
  11 per cent -- 0.15 of a mip level -- rather than as a look; the
  incommensurate 9.6 m patch field in the weights; per-layer phase). Stochastic
  or hex-tile sampling is the real answer and costs three taps per layer, which
  at six layers and two rungs is thirty-six fetches.
- **The snow band is still paint in the albedo.** The splat gives snow a normal
  and a roughness, which is where snow's material actually lives, but the flat
  white `mix` to (0.88, 0.92, 0.98) above it is untouched on purpose: it is a
  shipped term with shipped reference luminances. World audit gap 10 is
  therefore only half closed.
- **The meadow's blade grain reads as brushed.** A directional field at a
  grazing eye plus anisotropy 16 is the suspected mechanism; it is named rather
  than diagnosed, because nothing in this lane measured it.

---

## 2.11 THE IMAGE PIPELINE (RN-2130 to RN-2139, 2026-08-19, `lane/a1-image`). FIDELITY LANE A1

The first lane run under the fidelity charter
([docs/web/FIDELITY-GAP-2026-08-19.md](../web/FIDELITY-GAP-2026-08-19.md)) and
under its Option D process change: **this lane is judged by LOOK against the
charter's section 1 numbered differences, and every instrument below is a
regression rail rather than a definition of done.** Three hero poses, before and
after, `docs/screenshots/RN2130_{meadow,vista,vistadawn}_{before,after}.png`.
Frames were taken one build apart in separate processes on a sentinel-verified
`vite preview` this lane owned, killed by PID.

### THE HERO POSE THAT DID NOT EXIST, AND NOW DOES
`meadow` in `artframe.js`: the plains site (-7.9675, 116.53189, biome 2) at a
standing eye, pitch -8, dot 0.55. It is RN-2065's most damning SWEEP REJECT
promoted to a manifest row, because the charter's process requires the frame the
player stands in and every one of the ten canonical shots either looks at
something built or looks at a ridge. It is also the most expensive frame in the
file (2,785,433 triangles, 72 calls); cost is L2's subject and this lane neither
improved nor worsened it (2,785,433 before and after, to the triangle).

### WHAT SHIPPED, AS FIVE DECISIONS
1. **A tone response driven by sun elevation** (`web/src/render/post/ToneDrive.ts`,
   new). Exposure is `1.15` at night, `1.70` at a low sun and **exactly `1.20`
   at a high sun**, which is RN-208's measured value kept deliberately: the half
   of the day arc that moves is the half that was never calibrated. A **highlight
   shoulder** in display space above a knee at 0.52, 0.50 at noon and 0.72 at a
   low sun, exactly zero and zero-derivative at the knee so no mid tone can move
   under it. `?tone=0` restores the fixed-exposure image.
2. **A palette, stated as a palette: ONE MEADOW, LIT AT TWO TEMPERATURES.** Warm
   dry-straw light on what the sun touches, cool blue-green in what it does not,
   because the sky is the only other lamp in the scene. Split tone widened from
   +-0.035 to a measured max deviation 0.14 along the warm/cool axis (`shadowTint` [0.91, 0.99,
   1.14], `highlightTint` [1.055, 1.01, 0.93], both still averaging ~1.0 so the
   grade moves hue and not exposure), plus a **green harmonisation** that pulls
   the vegetation hue family onto one sage-olive axis **at each pixel's own
   luminance**, so it moves hue and never value.
3. **AO from black blobs to coloured occlusion.** `uStrength` in `AO_APPLY_FS` is
   a **vec3** now: a multiply blend cannot add sky colour back, but it can occlude
   the three channels by different amounts, which is the same statement from the
   other side. Day weights 1.00 / 0.86 / 0.62, so an occluded pixel loses its
   warmth before it loses its brightness. Strength 0.9 -> 0.60, radius 0.9 ->
   0.55 m, power 1.35 -> 1.15. `?occtint=0` restores the grey multiply exactly.
4. **A sky-tinted ambient fill** (`TerrainAmbient.ts`). The daylight floor is now
   two authored endpoints blended on the same elevation weights the exposure
   uses, and `TERRAIN_SKY_AMBIENT` goes **0.32 -> 0.88**. `?ambientfill=0`
   restores both halves in one flag.
5. **Bloom restraint**: threshold 0.75 -> 0.86, strength 0.14 -> 0.10, because a
   halo authored against an uncompressed top end now lands on one the shoulder
   has pulled down.

### THE THREE HERO JUDGEMENTS, WRITTEN AGAINST THE BAR AND NOT AGAINST YESTERDAY

**MEADOW: the largest move of the three, and still not a Space Engineers
grassland.** Charter difference 3 (black shadow blobs) is the one that genuinely
closed: near-ground `loFrac` **0.318 -> 0.172**, i.e. the share of the ground at
the player's feet below display luma 24 nearly halved, and what is left in the
hollows now has a hue instead of being absent. Difference 4 (ungraded frame)
partially closed: the substrate's blue channel goes **27.8 -> 39.5** and its
`warm` **23.99 -> 19.20**, so the field's three arguing greens (lime blades,
forest-green tufts, khaki substrate) now sit on one axis and the ground reads as
one material rather than three; sky-to-ground balance improves from **3.74x to
2.89x** (`skyHz` against `nearG`) and the far band comes off the clip
(**217.86 -> 205.59**, `hiFrac` **0.993 -> 0.818**). Against the SE bar,
honestly: this now has sky-lit shadows with colour in them and a harmonised
green field, which is two of the four things I named. It does NOT have the
composed sky-to-ground balance (the sky still owns the top third and the horizon
is still a cream band) and it emphatically does not have gentle blue distance,
because there is no depth in the composite to grade against. And the frame's
DOMINANT read is still charter difference 1: a sandy substrate with discrete
tufts standing on it. A better image made that defect **more legible**, not less.
This is a real improvement and it is not close to the bar; A2's carpet is what
closes the gap and this lane's job was to make sure A2 is judged through a
competent image.

**VISTA: nearly unmoved, and that is the honest verdict.** `hzBand` 198.86 ->
194.56, `nearG` 134.14 -> 140.31, whole-frame luma 123.13 -> 124.79. The sky is a
shade deeper and more saturated at the zenith (`skyL` sat 0.711 -> 0.730, warm
-95.62 -> -102.05) and the near scree carries slightly more value, and that is
the whole of it. The reason is structural rather than a tuning failure: this
frame is rock, scree and haze with no vegetation for the harmonisation to act
on, almost nothing in shadow for the fill or the AO retune to reach, and a far
half whose `iqr` is **3.64** because the atmosphere has already destroyed the
signal. A grade cannot create contrast that is not in the image. **Charter
differences 3 and 4 moved by a few per cent here and difference 2 (no terrain
material) is untouched and owns the frame.** By the charter's own standard a +2
per cent frame is a failure, and this is one; it belongs to L1 (haze) and L3 (far
terrain material) and I am not going to dress it up.

**VISTADAWN: the frame that stopped inverting, and the clearest win in the set.**
Before, the far ridge was **231.51 with `hiFrac` 1.000** -- every pixel of it
above 200, a blown white wall -- standing behind a foreground at **33.01**, a
far-to-near ratio of **7.01**. After: ridge **202.92, `hiFrac` 0.484**,
foreground **53.43** (`loFrac` 0.209 -> 0.089), ratio **3.80**. The inversion is
roughly halved and the paper wall has become a haze with tone in it. The colour
move is the bigger half: horizon-sky `warm` **-86.23 -> -30.48** and the far
band's `warm` **20.91 -> 61.49**, so a 5.85 degree sun finally produces a warm
horizon under a blue zenith instead of the audit's "brightens toward the sun and
never reddens". **Charter difference 4 substantially closed on this pose and
difference 3 partly.** Against the bar: it now reads as a dawn rather than as an
overexposed noon, but the distance is STILL the brightest thing below the sky and
the mid ground still carries the flat 300 m cascade region as one dead grey mass.
The warmth here is a GRADE and not physics, and it is labelled as one in the
code: the scattering integral still does not redden, and until L1 and A4 fix that
this frame is wearing makeup.

### RAILS, AND ONE CONTROL THAT DEFLATED MY OWN LARGEST NUMBER
`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `vite build` clean; `cd web && npm run check` **6 of 7
with only the pre-existing `check:limits` red**, and none of the four files this
lane touched or added is among its violations (`PostStack.ts` 397, `ToneDrive.ts`
269, `AoGlsl.ts` 266, `CompositeGlsl.ts` 213). `check:boot` PASS on real D3D11.
Every non-hero canonical shot legitimately moved, because the grade is global and
that is by design; `machine` whole-frame luma 34.43 -> 38.30 and `voxelface`'s
RN-1727 committed rectangles **`groundA` 22.13 -> 22.70 and `groundB` 16.06 ->
19.63**, published here so the next reader is not comparing against a stale row.

**The `?ambientfill=0` control, one flag apart on one build, says the sky-ambient
raise bought far less than the arithmetic predicted.** On the meadow: near-ground
luma **63.69 with the fill and 61.60 without**, `loFrac` 0.172 against 0.193, and
the three sky rectangles **identical to the digit** (a clean positive check that
the flag does exactly what it claims and nothing else). So of the +14 counts the
near ground gained, the 2.75x sky-ambient raise is worth **about two**, and the
rest is the AO retune. The mechanism is worth carrying and is a cross-domain
finding: **`StockFill.stockFloor` gives the scatter props a hemisphere fill of
`TERRAIN_AMBIENT * AMP`, the FLOOR ONLY -- the sky-ambient WEIGHT that lights the
terrain never reaches a single blade of grass.** Sky-lit shading on the
understorey therefore cannot be delivered from `TERRAIN_SKY_AMBIENT` at all, and
whoever builds A2's carpet or A4's probe needs to know that before they tune it.

### OWED, AND SAID OUT LOUD
- **No depth-aware distance grading.** `PostStack` composites after the view-model
  pass, so the depth attachment at that moment holds the player's forearms, not
  the world. "Gentle blue distance" is NOT closed by this lane and belongs to L1
  and A4.
- **The exact pre-A1 image is the before BUILD, not a flag.** `?tone=0`,
  `?ambientfill=0`, `?occtint=0`, `?greenpull=0` and `?shoulderamp=0` each restore
  the state immediately before the term they name (all five registered in
  `run.mjs`'s `PAGE_PARAMS`), but the palette constants in `PostDefaults.ts` are
  not URL-restorable as a set, so there is no single flag that reproduces
  `9a215e42`'s frame.
- **The dawn warmth is a grade standing in for a missing physical term** (audit
  gap 8). When L5 warms the scattering integral, `WARM_LOWSUN` must come back
  down or the two will double up.

## 2.11 THE GROUND-COVER CARPET (RN-2145 to RN-2152, 2026-08-19, `lane/a2-carpet`). FIDELITY LANE A2

> Closes the gap analysis' **section 1 difference 1**: "the ground IS grass
> there; here grass sits ON the ground", named there as roughly half the
> perceived gap to the D-020 bar. Judged by the hero-frame process (gap doc
> Option D), not by instrument deltas. Frames: `docs/screenshots/RN2145_*`.

### 2.11.1 What it is

A **separate layer from the prop scatter**, which keeps bushes and trees. Two
GPU-instanced rungs behind **two draw calls**, both reusing texgen's existing
`grass` family (`of_grass_a.png`, 1024, `alpha_test` 0.35): no new texture
family, no `texgen.py` change, no `ROLE_FAMILY` entry.

| rung | card | tris/instance | density | reach |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tuft | 2 crossed quads, 2 height segments, 0.27 u span (3 painted blades) | 8 | `32 / (1 + d/10)^2` per m2 | 26 m, hands over from 20 m |
| mat | 1 quad, 1 segment, full 11-blade span, 1.10 x 0.42 m | 2 | 1.55 per m2 flat | 95 m, fades in over 12 to 20 m |

Files: `web/src/render/grass/{GrassTuning,GrassPalette,GrassCard,GrassGlsl,GrassMaterial,GrassPool,GrassSample,GrassCover}.ts`.
Instruments: `web/tools/smoke/probes/{grasscover,grasswind}.js`. Pose:
`artframe.js`'s new `meadow` row.

### 2.11.2 The three rules that make it a carpet rather than denser scatter

**COLOUR COMES FROM THE GROUND, AND THE FADE CANNOT SHOW AS A VALUE STEP.**
Every instance samples `BiomePalette.terrainAlbedo` at its own cell (the
acknowledged CPU twin of the four lines the terrain fragment draws the ground
with) and rotates it toward green **at constant Rec.709 luminance**
(`GrassPalette.coverAlbedo`). Worked: Plains `0x6d6a47` is linear (0.153, 0.144,
0.063), luma 0.140; the rotation gives `#4E723E` at luma 0.140 exactly. So what
is lost across the fade is chroma and texture, never light. **Measured with the
one-flag isolator `?grasstint=0`** (blades exactly the substrate colour): the
rotation costs 1 to 3 per cent of luma at every range rung, which is the
luminance preservation working.

**LIGHT COMES FROM THE SAME PLACE THE GROUND'S DOES.** The carpet is a
`ShaderMaterial` holding `TERRAIN_AMBIENT`, `TERRAIN_SKY_AMBIENT`, the
atmosphere record, `uBodyCenter` and `uCascadeFar` **by reference** (RN-64's
argument, WaterMaterial's pattern), and inlining the same
`TERRAIN_SUN_IRRADIANCE`. It is the **fifth ShaderMaterial on the DW-10 ledger**
and the argument for it is lane A1's measurement: `StockFill.stockFloor` lights
scattered props from the ambient FLOOR only and the sky-ambient weight never
reaches an instance, so a carpet lit that way would sit in the old grey floor
while the ground under it wore the sky tint.

**THE FADE IS IN PIXELS, NOT METRES** (RN-1855's derive-do-not-type rule).
`px = cardHeight * grow * (viewportH / (2 tan(fovY/2))) / dist`, computed live
in the vertex shader from the camera's own pixels per radian, which `Systems`
pushes each frame. At the reference viewport the window lands at about **60 to
92 m**, and the metres are the consequence rather than the input.

### 2.11.3 What the frames found that no number would have

Four defects, each caught by looking and each recorded because the cause is
reusable:

1. **The card mipped to a solid wedge.** `texgen.py` widened the blade until the
   coverage cleared the 0.35 cutoff so that "distant mips converge toward solid
   rather than dissolving". Right for a prop card, wrong for a carpet whose
   subject IS the gaps. Fixed by fewer wider blades per card (u span 0.42 to
   0.27) plus a rescale of the sampled alpha about the cutoff; **the texture is
   untouched, so no prop moves**. `?grasssharp=1` is the exact control.
2. **Green shark fins.** A 0.18 m card over three blades is a 5 cm blade at
   30 cm tall, aspect 1:6.7. 0.13 x 0.38 gives 1:10.6 and 6.3 px at 4 m, which
   is as slim as FXAA-only alpha testing holds still (world-audit gap 17).
3. **A pin cushion.** Vertical cards have straight silhouettes and nothing in a
   meadow does. A per-instance LEAN combed by a common bearing derived from
   PropWind's own phase vector moved the read more than any other change.
4. **A lawn.** One green per biome measured sat 0.603 against bare ground's
   0.526. Plains' rotation weight dropped to 0.74 and gained a per-instance DRY
   DRIFT **along the same line toward the substrate**, so blades vary without
   any of them being able to disagree with the ground. Now 0.576.

**AND THE FIXTURE WAS WRONG BEFORE THE FEATURE WAS.** `meadow`'s first
rectangles were hand-written fractions; inverting the range map afterwards put
them at 3.8, 8.5 and 11.8 m, so **not one reached the mid field**, which is the
band a carpet is most likely to leave bald and the band the judgement is about.
At a 2 m eye, 25 to 60 m of ground is about seven pixels, so a hand-picked
fraction cannot land there. They are `rangeRects [4, 10, 25, 55]` now.

### 2.11.4 The numbers

Real D3D11, RTX 4060 Ti through ANGLE, 1600x900, `meadow` pose (Plains
-7.9675 / 116.53189, yaw 150, pitch -12, sun dot 0.699 measured):

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| instances | 74,939 (tuft 17,440, mat 57,499) over 25 chunks |
| draw calls | **+2** (71 to 73), programs **unmoved at 44** |
| triangles | **+254,518**, 2,762,904 to 3,017,422 (**+9.2%**) |
| VRAM | **unmoved**, 104.2 MB |
| resident chunks | **unmoved**, 330 |
| refused / cells capped / backlog | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `placedPerM2` / `askedPerM2` / delivered | 2.12 / 1.89 / **1.123** |
| frame cost (WG-189, 5 interleaved repeats, 400 frames) | **-0.44 ms against within-arm spreads of 3.83 and 2.10: NOT SEPARATED** |

**The triangle number is the one to argue with, and it is stated as a breach.**
The plains standing eye was **already over `StatsProbe`'s 2.7 M ALERT before
this lane** (2,762,904; the world audit flagged the same pose at 2,759,465) and
the carpet takes it to 3,017,422. Two things bound it and neither is an excuse:
the carpet **casts no shadow**, so its triangles are drawn ONCE where a prop
triangle is drawn four times (the ceiling study's 58.8 per cent), and 254,518 is
**30 per cent of the 853,675 triangles that study priced as recoverable shadow
waste**. The frame-cost gate the ceiling study asks for would have flagged this,
and it still does not exist.

**Determinism** (`probes/grasscover.js`, a real round trip and not a re-read:
1.2 km away so every chunk is dropped, then back so every chunk is rebuilt from
its own key): digest `54cbcf74-456b1741` to `6ab96204-f8849c97` away (the
control is armed) to `54cbcf74-456b1741` back, **74,939 instances both times**.

**Wind** (`probes/grasswind.js`, the clock pinned at three offsets in one
settled sequence, mean per-tile luma change): carpet + props **3.77**, props
only **2.28** (`?grass=0`), neither **0.63** (`?wind=0`). All three separate.
The still arm is a control that WENT RED first: `?wind=0` drops PropWind's hook,
which stops the props and cannot stop a `ShaderMaterial` reading the shared
clock directly, so the carpet kept swaying with the flag off (34.59 counts where
there must be none). The carpet now reads PropWind's `enabled`.

### 2.11.5 THE FINDING THIS LANE OWES ANOTHER, AND IT IS THE LARGEST ONE HERE

**Screen-space AO takes 44 to 57 per cent of the carpeted ground's luminance
against 31 to 32 per cent of the bare ground's, and that alone is the difference
between the carpet reading brighter than the ground it replaced and darker.**
Four arms, one flag apart on one build, `meadow` `box`:

| | AO on | AO off | AO takes |
|---|---|---|---|
| carpet off | 63.08 | 91.50 | 31.1% |
| carpet on | 58.66 | 104.47 | **43.9%** |

At the 4 m rung it is worse: bare 58.40 / 85.25 (31.5%), carpeted 38.26 / 89.26
(**57.1%**). On `forestfloor`, where there is no direct sun to hide it, the
carpeted floor reads **10.02 with AO on and 26.87 with it off**, against the
bare floor's 23.98. **So the carpet is not darkening the ground; the AO is
darkening the carpet.** This is the gap analysis' difference 3 (AO at strength
0.9, radius 0.9 m reads as hard dark blobs) meeting a layer with real depth
complexity. `render/post/*` is lane A1's and this lane did not touch it.

### 2.11.6 The seam this lane publishes to A3, and the honest partial result

`GrassPalette.coverAlbedo(substrate, biome, out, dry)` and the `COVER` table are
**the carpet side of the fade-target contract**. A3's far-field grass layer
should target `coverAlbedo` at the fade end, and then far ground and near carpet
agree by construction rather than by tuning.

**Until it does, the residual is real and is visible in the frame:** past the
fade the ground is the bare biome substrate again, and on the meadow pose that
is a khaki band along the horizon where the green stops. The luminance-matched
rotation means it is a CHROMA step and not a value step, and the aerial
perspective has already taken most of the chroma out by then, but it is there.
**This lane cannot close it from its own files without repainting the biome
palette, which is RN-347's decision and A3's ground.**

Two more stated limits: the carpet **casts no shadow** (deliberate, see the
triangle note), and at 2 to 4 m there is still bare substrate visible between
blades. The near field reads as a meadow; it does not yet read as turf.

## 2.12 THE FAR-FIELD COVER CONVERGENCE (RN-2195 to RN-2199, 2026-08-20, `lane/fade-target`). FIDELITY LANE A3 PHASE 1.5

Closes the seam A2's `GrassPalette.ts` named as its own single largest owed
finding: past the carpet's fade (~90 m) and past the splat's own chroma fade
(C4's 35-75 m band), the ground reverted to the bare biome palette, a khaki
band along every meadow horizon where the carpet's green stopped. Base
`origin/main` at `e0daf76d`. Server `127.0.0.1:4173`, `--strictPort`, sentinel
written into this worktree's own `dist` and fetched back before the first
probe, killed by the PID `netstat` named for that port.

### WHAT SHIPPED

`web/src/render/materials/TerrainCoverFar.ts` and `.glsl.ts`, a new pair on
`TerrainSplat`'s own precedent (TS holds the constants and the proof, GLSL
holds the shader half). The rotation is GrassPalette.coverAlbedo's own body
(`r *= 1 - 0.45k`, `g *= 1 + 0.30k`, `b *= 1 - 0.15k`, renormalised to source
luminance) mirrored into GLSL, because GLSL cannot import a TypeScript
function. **It is not assumed to agree, it is proven to:**
`assertFarCoverMatchesGrass()` calls the live `coverAlbedo` at module load and
throws if the mirror disagrees by more than float rounding, on
`assertHueLuminance`'s own precedent. The green weight is `COVER[2].green`
(Plains, "the meadow pose's own biome" by GrassPalette's own comment),
imported **live** rather than copied, so it cannot drift even if A2 retunes
Plains' row; it is then discounted to the carpet's own **population mean**
(0.69, not its brightest blade) using GrassPalette's DRY_SPREAD (0.62, read
from its source since it is not exported) against GrassSample.ts's
near-uniform per-instance `dry` draw, because a rectangle that samples many
blades and the ground past them should converge on the carpet's *average*,
not its greenest instant.

Wired into `TerrainFragAlbedo.glsl.ts` **inside the existing
`if (uSplatAmp...)` branch**, right after the near hue term's own mix, reusing
locals already in scope: `splatVeg` (`clamp(vMatW.x * 3, 0, 1)`, the splat's
own grass/dirt selector) and `coverSel` (the shared slope selector), so no new
varying and no seventh per-biome table (ofSplatW's own argument, applied a
second time). Faded in by `1 - splatFadeA`, the near hue term's own C4 curve
**inverted**, so the two terms are complementary on ONE boundary rather than
needing a second fade constant. New isolator `uSplatFarAmp` / `?splatfar=0` /
`?splatfaramp=`, on `splatAmpFromQuery`'s pattern exactly (RN-150's
dead-default guard included), registered in `run.mjs`'s `PAGE_PARAMS`
whitelist per that file's own rule (RN-698). `TerrainSplatHandle.ts` gained
`setSplatFar`/`getSplatFar`/`splatFarDefault()` on `splatDefault()`'s shape.

### THE TRAP: THE BRIEF'S OWN INSTRUMENT WAS AIMED SHORT OF THE DEFECT

The brief pointed at `meadowfield`'s `rangeRects [4, 10, 25, 55]` as "exactly
the instrument" for the no-hue-step proof. **Measured, one flag apart, fresh
process: at 55 m (the realistic pose, props and carpet ON) `?splat=0` moves
that rectangle's rgb by under one count, and `?splatfaramp=100` -- a hundred
times the shipped amplitude -- moves it by nothing at all.** The carpet is
genuinely opaque there: a screen rectangle at 55 m is the blades' own colour,
not the terrain under them, so no terrain-level term (this lane's or any
other) can be proven or disproven at that range. A `?grass=0` plus
extreme-amplitude control (isolating the mechanism from the carpet
entirely) confirmed the term reaches and visibly, correctly rotates a
specific horizon band while every closer rectangle stays inertly
identical -- the mechanism is real, and the instrument was simply pointed at
the wrong range to see it, which is exactly the "verify the instrument, not
only the feature" rule this project's whole harness history argues for.

**The fix was an additive rectangle, not a different pose.** `meadowfield`
gained `extra.hz` (y 0.28 to 0.33, a plain screen fraction on `extra.sky`'s
own precedent, not a `rangeRect`, because the true horizon there is many
hundreds of metres away and `rangeRects`' flat-plane inversion is not the
right tool for it), located by looking at the rendered frame rather than by
range math. The committed pose, `box` and `rangeRects` are byte-unchanged.

### THE NUMBERS, one flag (`?splatfar=0`) apart, fresh process, shipped amplitude

`meadowfield`'s new `hz` rectangle: rgb **(151.76, 163.28, 133.17) -> (149.48,
163.88, 132.57)**, luma **158.65 -> 158.56 (-0.06%)**, warm **18.59 -> 16.91
(-1.68)**, sat **0.238 -> 0.246**. Luminance barely moves while warmth drops
and saturation rises: the chroma-only, luminance-preserving signature the
whole convergence rule promises, measurable at the ACTUAL boundary for the
first time. Noise floor at that rectangle is exactly zero (two repeats of the
`before` arm, `?splatfar=0` both times, bit-identical to 3 decimals), so the
delta is real and not settle-tick jitter.

**Vista negative control** (Mountains, `vMatW.x` 0.02): sky rectangles
(`skyL`/`skyR`/`skyHz`) bit-identical to 3 decimals across three fresh-process
repeats of the same flags. Ground rectangles move by at most 1.1 rgb counts
(`nearG` r 145.86 -> 144.77) with luma unchanged to 2 decimals (140.18 ->
140.17), attributable to Mountains' own small, pre-existing veg weight
(already the game's answer to "how vegetated is this biome", not a new table)
rather than a green wash on scree or rock the biome does not have.

### C1-C4, AND WHY THIS TERM DID NOT NEED A FIFTH CLAUSE

Every existing splat clause is unchanged: this term does not touch the six
layers, their weights or their hue table, so C1-C3 hold exactly as RN-2160
left them (`splatDefault().hueLuma` still reads 1.000000 for all six). C4 is
extended rather than broken: the far term's own fade is the near term's fade
**inverted**, so there is still exactly one boundary constant
(`SPLAT_FADE_ALBEDO`) governing both halves of the handoff.

### OWED

- **The mean-discount (0.69) is this file's own approximation**, not part of
  GrassPalette's contract (the cross-check proves the ROTATION FORMULA agrees,
  not the discount). It is closed by the hero-frame measurement above, not by
  the arithmetic alone, exactly as GrassPalette's own green weights were
  captured rather than derived.
- **Phase 2's 75-600 m band** (RN-2160's own owed item) would give this term a
  world-locked coordinate to ride past the max-depth ring; until then it rides
  the same chunk-UV scale step the splat's near layers do, which is outside
  this band's own reach (past 75 m the chroma target no longer depends on UV
  scale at all, so the step does not apply to THIS term, but is worth naming
  for the next reader).
- **The snow band and the scaled/far scene are both untouched**, on purpose:
  this term lives inside the same `#ifndef OF_SCALED` guard the rest of the
  splat does, and snow displaces cover entirely (`ofSplatW`'s own rule), so
  there is nothing for it to rotate once snow owns a fragment.

## 2.12 THE SKY BECOMES A PARTICIPANT (RN-2175 to RN-2189, 2026-08-20, `lane/a4-sky`). FIDELITY LANE A4

> Closes the gap analysis' **section 1 difference 3** ("their sky is a
> participant; ours is a backdrop ... and we have no cloud system at all") and
> world-audit gaps **8** (the sky never reddens), **9** (no clouds) and **16**
> (no canonical frame contains the sun). It **partly** closes gap **1** (aerial
> perspective) and it **refutes the two instruments gap 1 was measured with**.
> Hero frames `docs/screenshots/RN2175_{vista,vistadawn,flyover,meadow}_{before,after}.png`
> plus `RN2175_dawnsun_after.png`, `RN2175_limb_after.png` and
> `RN2175_vista_c_noclouds.png`.
>
> **Correction, 2026-08-20.** Three record-versus-measurement errors below (the
> `?aerosol=0` control described as bit-identical, the meadow ground rectangles
> described as unmoved, and several control-arm percentages quoted from a
> mid-lane read) were found and fixed by a fresh-context verifier re-measuring
> against this lane's own HEAD build; the corrected numbers are the verifier's
> HEAD figures, recorded here rather than silently overwritten so the history
> stays honest.

### 2.12.1 What shipped, as six decisions

1. **The sun path is integrated ANALYTICALLY (Chapman) instead of marched.**
   `ofSunOD` in `web/src/render/materials/AtmosphereAero.glsl.ts`. The old code
   put a **three-step uniform midpoint rule** over a path 65 km long at noon and
   over 200 km long at dawn, through an atmosphere whose density lives in its
   first ten. `ofChapman`'s closed form has the exact plane-parallel high-sun
   limit `H / sin(elevation)` **independent of the curvature radius**, which is
   the property the whole design rests on: the curvature can only change the
   answer at grazing angles. It also removes `lightSteps` from inside
   `viewSteps`, so it is cheaper than what it replaced. `?sunarc=0` restores the
   march exactly; `?sunarc=1` uses the body's own curvature.
2. **`sunCurveK = 10.6`, and it is the one CHOICE in this lane rather than a
   correction.** Forge is a 600 km body with a 5.6 km scale height (D-006). Feed
   those to an exact Chapman integral and the grazing sun column at a 5.85
   degree sun is **36,940 m against Earth's 70,320**: about half. Half the
   airmass is half the reddening, so **a physically exact single-scattering
   model on this planet cannot produce a sunset**, and the shortfall is the
   planet's radius, which is a gameplay decision. The sun path alone is
   therefore integrated against Earth's curvature (52,285 m at 5.85 degrees).
3. **The boundary layer is one layer for the whole frame, not one per ray.**
   `ofAtmoAerial` referenced `min(a0, a1)`, i.e. whatever a ray happened to land
   on was declared to be at the bottom of the densest air, so a ridge at 500 m
   and the valley 300 m below it hazed identically and climbing THICKENED the
   haze. It is now `uAeroRef.x`, the ground under the observer, written once per
   frame by `SkyPass.update`. `ofAeroColumn` clamps density at 1 below the base
   (valleys fill with haze rather than going super-dense) and splits the segment
   at the ray's true midpoint altitude, so the chord's bow is carried.
   `?aerobase=0` restores the per-ray reference and is EXACT: with that base
   every height is non-negative, the clamp never fires, and `ofAeroColumn`
   reduces algebraically to the closed form it replaced.
4. **The SKY ray carries the boundary layer, which is where a dawn's colour
   actually comes from.** `ofAtmoSkyAero`, one call site, the sky quad's
   escaping branch. This is the term the first attempt tried and reverted, and
   the difference is that the confinement is now ARITHMETIC: the same analytic
   column self-limits at `H / sin(elevation)`, so the zenith collects exactly
   `sigma * H` = **0.056 of optical depth** and no march can make it more. It
   meets the ground half at the horizon by construction, both being the same
   integral, one truncated at the surface and one escaping. `?skyaero=0`.
5. **The ambient is the sky's own hemisphere, sampled on the CPU.**
   `web/src/render/materials/SkyProbe.ts`, nine directions (zenith plus rings at
   20 and 50 degrees), cosine weighted, azimuths placed relative to the sun each
   frame. It replaces `ofAtmoScatter(p, up, 1.0e9, 2, 2)` in the terrain, the
   carpet and the sky's ground shell through one shared accessor
   `ofAtmoSkyAmb`, and it drives `TerrainAmbient`'s daylight floor in place of
   lane A1's two authored endpoints, **which is the handoff A1 wrote**. The
   zenith is the worst possible single sample of a dawn: it is the one part of
   the dome that has not reddened, so the fill in every shadow was midnight blue
   while the horizon burned. `?skyirr=0` restores both halves in one flag.
6. **A cloud deck, inside the sky material.** `SkyClouds.ts`: a 256-square
   deterministic `DataTexture`, a real ray-shell intersection at 4,200 m over a
   20 km tile, drifting on the SIM clock, lit by the same `sunT` the terrain's
   direct term uses so it is white at noon and warm at dawn with no second rule.
   **No new draw call and no new program.** `?clouds=0`, `?cloudamp=`.

### 2.12.2 THE FINDING THIS LANE OWES THE NEXT ONE: BOTH INSTRUMENTS IN AUDIT GAP 1 ARE INVALID

The brief said to prove the aerosol work with "the flyover hzBand pair and the
atmos=0 control (iqr 20.08 hazed vs 89.17 clear)". Neither number measures the
aerosol, and this is the lane's largest reusable result.

- **`?atmos=0` deletes the SKY BOX.** `flyover.hzBand` straddles the horizon, so
  in that arm a third of the rectangle is pure void (`loFrac` **0.33**). Most of
  the 89.17 is the ground-against-nothing step, not lost terrain contrast.
- **`flyover.hzBand` cannot measure a term that only touches terminating rays**,
  because a third of it is sky the term cannot reach by construction. The proof
  is a sigma sweep: at **a quarter** of the extinction the band moves 13.88 ->
  **15.30** against a true ceiling of 29.17, i.e. cutting the term by 4x buys
  ten per cent of the gap, because what is left is the sky half.
- **The honest control is `?aerosol=0`: sigma zero, sky PRESERVED rather than
  deleted.** Unlike `?atmos=0`, which removes the sky box outright and fills a
  third of `hzBand` with void, this control keeps the sky painted, which is what
  makes it valid for isolating the aerosol term. It is **not bit-identical**
  between arms: `flyover.skyBand` reads **149.03 / 29.97 / -54.96** by default
  against **148.64 / 30.48 / -56.53** under the flag. That the sky moves at all
  is by design, not a control failure -- the sky ray carries the boundary layer
  (decision 4), so the sky itself is now a participant even with the aerosol
  term zeroed. Against that control the aerosol was taking **44.5 per cent** of
  the contrast off the flyover's all-ground `box` (31.71 hazed against 56.47
  clear) and **7 per cent**, not thirty, off the straight-down `under`
  rectangle (7.50 against 8.07).
- **The valid rectangle for this term at the flyover is `box`, which is all
  ground.** Every claim below is made on it.

### 2.12.3 The numbers

**THE AEROSOL, `flyover.box`, all ground, fresh process per arm.** Target stated
before the change: recover at least half of the contrast the term destroys.
**Landed at 76 per cent of that recovery** (a mid-lane read had this at 80 per
cent; superseded by the verifier's HEAD re-measurement): iqr **31.71 ->
51.05** against the `?aerosol=0` ceiling of **56.47**, with whole-frame `world`
luma held at 143.21 against 160.89 before and **132.76** with the term off (a
mid-lane reading of 129.97 for the term-off figure is superseded by this HEAD
number). The
mechanism is the MAGNITUDE, which is what the audit's own sentence asked for
("the ordering is right at every rung; only the magnitude is wrong"): sigma
**4.5e-4 -> 1.4e-4**, a Koschmieder visual range of **8.7 km -> 27.9 km**, i.e.
a hazy day by the WMO's own table becoming a clear one.

**AND THE RE-REFERENCE, PRICED HONESTLY, BOUGHT NOTHING IN PIXELS.**
`?aerobase=0` one flag apart on one build: on `mtnslope` **every rectangle is
identical to the digit in both arms**; on `flyover.box` it is worth **-1.06 of
iqr and +5.25 of luma**, i.e. very slightly the wrong way. It ships because it
is STRUCTURALLY load-bearing rather than because it moved a frame:
`ofAtmoSkyAero` needs a single frame-wide base to have a meaning at all, and the
clamped analytic column is what makes the sky term safe. Stated as a null so the
next lane does not re-buy it.

**THE DAY ARC AT ONE POSE, which is the table audit section 3 asked for.**
`skyHz.warm`, the same rectangle, one build apart:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `vista`, 44.3 deg sun | **-86.15** | **-23.45** |
| `vistadawn`, 5.85 deg sun | **-30.48** | **+56.51** |
| arc across the two | **55.67** | **79.96** |

The audit's bar was "differs by more than the 14.83 counts it does now, by a
stated margin"; the raw pre-A1 arc was 14.83, A1's grade took it to 55.67, and
the model now carries **79.96** of it. The sun-side / anti-sun split at dawn is
`skyL` **183.17** against `skyR` **149.39**, with `skyL.warm` +44.39 against
`skyR.warm` +32.89.

**WHAT THE CHAPMAN CORRECTION IS WORTH ON ITS OWN, and it is much less than the
arithmetic promised.** `?sunarc=0 / =1 / default`, `vistadawn.skyL.warm`:
**-46.12 / -45.98 / -45.56**. The linear red-to-blue ratio of the in-scattered
source at 5.85 degrees improves **0.425 -> 0.73**, a real 72 per cent, and it
shows up as **under one count** of display `warm`, because ACES compresses a
170-luma sky toward white. **That is why decision 4 exists**: the visible half of
a dawn's colour is aerosol, not molecules, and the model had none in the sky.
Where the correction DOES show is the direct term: `vistadawn.mid.warm` 50.71 ->
56.79 and `hzBand.warm` 63.62 -> 67.82 across the same three arms.

**THE CLOUD FIELD IS DETERMINISTIC AND ITS COVERAGE IS NOW SEED-STABLE.**
`window.__ofClouds.report()`, three FRESH processes at three different scenarios
and sites: digest `dfb765d0-7043099e`, cover 66.623, identical every time. **A
changed input changes the output** (`?seed=99` gives `fd1f8e8c-7809daa8`, cover
50.098), which is the wiring check. **And the first version failed its own seed
sweep:** thresholding the raw octave sum gave cover **91.2 on the default seed
and 27.1 on `?seed=99`**, i.e. overcast against nearly clear with nothing in the
design choosing either. Stretching each field to its own range first brings that
to **66.6 against 50.1**. This is RN-2167's lesson inverted: there a percentile
stretch DESTROYED an authored intention, here the absence of one destroyed the
only constant that was authored.

**`?clouds=0` IS AN EXACT CONTROL AND SAYS SO.** On `vista`, `box`, `hzBand`,
`mid` and `nearG` are identical to the digit in both arms (176.67 / 18.50,
183.96 / 2.21, 174.25 / 15.21, 143.36 / 24.78) and only the three sky rectangles
move. The deck reaches exactly the sky and nothing else.

**BUDGETS.** Draw calls and programs UNMOVED at every pose (`vista` 50 / 45,
`flyover` 25 / 34, `meadow` 74 / 45, `limb` 21 / 23); triangles identical to the
digit at every pose; `vramMB` 104.2 unmoved, which per RN-2166 is a field that
does not count texture uploads and is quoted here only as "did not move". The
cloud texture is **256 KB computed at runtime, never written to disk**. The sun
path is one closed form where it was `viewSteps * lightSteps` marched samples, so
the sky and terrain shaders both got cheaper; **no timing claim is made**,
because this lane did not run an interleaved sweep and a p50 that moved a
millisecond on one box is not evidence.

**THE ORBITAL LIMB SURVIVED THE SIGMA CUT, which was the stated risk.** The
vertical aerosol column is exactly `sigma * H`, so it fell 0.18 -> 0.056 of
optical depth. `limb` at 120 km: `ring` luma **92.46**, iqr **96.00**, sat
**0.60**, against the audit's 93.27 / 101.39 / 0.626, at 21 calls and 52,913
triangles. Holding the product by raising H was measured and rejected: a taller
layer puts an eye at 1,200 m back inside it and gives the flyover's contrast
straight back.

### 2.12.4 The five hero judgements, written against the bar

**VISTA: the clearest win, and the sky is finally doing something.** Before, a
deep blue gradient over a cream wall. After, a broken cumulus deck with blue
between it, converging into the distance with real perspective, and the far mesa
at frame left legible as a SHAPE where it was a solid cream field. Against the SE
bar this now has "blue gradient sky with believable clouds" and "distance goes
gently blue", which is two of the four things difference 3 names. **What it does
NOT have is any material out there**: `hzBand` iqr is **2.21**, and the
`?aerosol=0` ceiling on that rectangle is **6.00**, so removing the haze
altogether would still leave a nearly flat ridge. **The vista's milk wall is not
the haze and this lane can prove it**; it is audit gap 3 and belongs to A3
phase 2. The sky also paid for its air: `skyL` sat 0.73 -> 0.39 and luma 72.87 ->
106.60. A sky that saturated twenty degrees above the horizon was never
plausible, but this is a real change to a calibrated frame and Reid should rate
it.

**VISTADAWN: transformed, and it is the frame the lane exists for.** Before: a
midday blue sky over a blown cream ridge, which the audit called an overexposed
noon. After: a golden-hour sky, warm at the horizon and cooling upward, ridges
that read as silhouettes with structure, and a foreground with warmth in it.
`skyHz.warm` -30.48 -> +56.51, `mid` iqr 39.56 -> **79.31** (the mid ridges got
their modelling back), `box` iqr 21.93 -> **79.99**. Against the bar this is the
first dawn this project has rendered that reads as a dawn rather than as a
filter. **Two honest costs.** The foreground got DARKER, `nearG` 53.40 -> 45.95,
because the corrected sun path takes more out of a 5.85 degree sun than the
three-step march did; that is 14 per cent of the ground A1 bought back and I am
not dressing it up. And the anti-solar sky at dawn is neutral (`skyR.warm`
+32.89) where it should still be blue-violet; the forward-phase split took it
from +5.12 to a usable place but not to a correct one.

**FLYOVER: the largest measured move and the ugliest frame.** Before: a milk
sheet, ground and sky both, with a barely visible shadow. After: a blue sky with
a cloud deck, and ground that is visibly green with texture in it, `box` iqr
31.71 -> **51.05** and `box` luma 159.98 -> 125.30. **And the frame is now
dominated by a defect this lane did not cause and made more legible**: audit gap
5's hard-edged texel-staircase cascade region across the near half, which the
haze used to hide. That is the honest state of it: a correct atmosphere has
exposed a broken shadow, and the shadow-reach lane now has a much clearer target.
The `under` rectangle is unmoved at 7.36 against an 8.07 ceiling, so the ground
directly below a 1.2 km flight still has no material, exactly as the audit's
negative control said. Stars are still visible at 1,200 m in daylight (gap 13),
which was on this lane's list and is NOT closed.

**MEADOW, THE REGRESSION EYE-CHECK, AND EVERY RECTANGLE MOVED BY DESIGN, GROUND
INCLUDED.** The ground rectangles are **not** identical to the digit, and
saying so was a record error caught by the fresh-context verifier: `box` moves
**74.69 -> 77.03** (luma 55.56), `mid` **110.51 -> 112.46** (luma 46.50),
`nearG` **68.44 -> 70.72** (luma 56.85), `shade` **77.80 -> 79.97** (luma
58.79) -- a real, consistent reach of about **+2.3 counts** on every ground
rectangle, not noise. The cause is decision 5's `SkyProbe` ambient: the sky
floor now genuinely reaches the carpet and the splat, which `?skyirr=0` proves
by collapsing the move back to zero. A2's carpet and A3's splat are therefore
TOUCHED, intentionally, by the new sky-coloured ambient floor, and that reach
is published as moved-by-design rather than as a regression. The three sky
rectangles moved further still and are also **published as moved-by-design**:
`skyHi` warm -72.57 -> -14.40 and `skyHz` warm -38.96 -> +8.01. **`skyHi` is now sometimes a CLOUD
rectangle** (its fractions land on a cell in this frame), so that number says
"there is a cloud there" and must not be read as "the upper sky went warm". By
eye the after has more air and more incident and a slightly hazier zenith; the
before's clean blue is arguably the prettier sky and the after the more
believable one. Reid's call, and it is the kind of call the charter says is his.

**DAWNSUN, A NEW COMMITTED POSE, and it found a defect in the disc.** `dawnsun`
is `vistadawn`'s site turned to face the sun (`sunYawOffDeg` **0.00**, derived
from `vistadawn`'s own -52.70 rather than guessed) with the horizon placed at
y = 0.60 by arithmetic. It closes gap 16. The aureole is right and it is physical
-- the Mie and aerosol forward lobes together give a warm bloom that falls off
through `glareIn` to `glareOut` -- and **no glare term was added**, which is the
restraint the brief asked for. **The disc itself is a DARK SPECK.** Measured on
the frame: a 12 px box on the sun reads mean **202.79 with p01 185.46** against
neighbouring sky at a uniform **208.19**, and the arms attribute it (`?sundisc=0`
moves `sunCore` 206.10 -> 203.31 and its iqr 1.93 -> 6.14; `?skybodies=0` does
NOT remove it), so it is the sun sprite and not a celestial body. **The mechanism
is NOT diagnosed** -- an additive sprite cannot darken its destination and this
one measurably does -- and it is handed on rather than guessed at. Second honest
note on this pose: looking INTO a 5.85 degree sun through the layer, every sky
rectangle sits above 200 with `hiFrac` 0.75 to 0.88. That is what a real camera
sees and it is also a clipped frame; it is what made `aerosolTint` come down from
0.40 to 0.32.

### 2.12.5 Owed, and the cross-lane contract

- **A1's `WARM_LOWSUN` must come down, and this lane could not do it.** A1's own
  handoff: "when L5 warms the scattering integral, `WARM_LOWSUN` must come back
  down or the two will double up." It lives in `web/src/render/post/ToneDrive.ts`,
  which the AO lane owns this wave, so this lane did not touch it. **The split
  chosen: the integral owns the SKY's and the HAZE's colour entirely, and the
  grade keeps a reduced highlight warmth for SURFACES only.** Arithmetic on the
  dawn frame: at `TONE.warm` = 0.9645 the highlight tint is
  [1.1466, 1.0080, 0.8296], which accounts for about **37.5 of `skyHz`'s 56.51
  counts of warm** while the physics adds 83.3. **Recommended constant:
  `WARM_LOWSUN` [1.090, 0.998, 0.888] -> [1.030, 0.999, 0.963]**, one third of
  its current deviation, which lands `skyHz.warm` near +31 at dawn instead of
  +56.51. One line, and it needs Admin to route it to whoever holds `post/` next.
- **`SkyProbe.ts` is a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION of a GLSL model** and is named as
  one in its own header. Every constant comes from the same `AtmosphereParams`
  record, so there is no number to keep in sync, only structure, and the triple
  is published (`__ofAmbient.report().skyIrr`) so a probe can hold it against the
  sky pixels. Nobody has yet.
- **`SKY_FLOOR_K = 0.36` is a calibration to A1's `AMBIENT_NOON`, not a
  derivation.** At the Hills site under a dot-0.92 sun the probe reads
  (0.1152, 0.1639, 0.2435) and 0.36 reproduces A1's green and blue; red lands at
  0.0415 against A1's authored 0.048, i.e. the model's noon sky is slightly
  bluer than the endpoint guessed for it. Reported rather than corrected with a
  per-channel gain, because a per-channel gain is the authored triple coming back
  in through the window.
- **Not closed and on this lane's list**: gap 13 (stars at 1.2 km) and gap 10's
  remaining half (the snow band's flat white albedo). Clouds cast **no terrain
  shadow**, deliberately, and a player cannot fly through them.
- **`docs/web/NUMBERS.md` has an unresolved merge conflict at line 2170**
  (`<<<<<<< HEAD` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> origin/lane/a3-splat`) on `main`. Not
  this lane's region and not touched; flagged for Admin because it sits in the
  binding process document.

## 2.13 THE DAWN RETUNE, A4'S OWED CONSTANT PAID (RN-2235 to RN-2239, 2026-08-20, `lane/dawn-retune`)
