### 2.13.1 The retune

`WARM_LOWSUN` [1.090, 0.998, 0.888] -> **[1.030, 0.999, 0.963]**, A4's own
recommendation (2.12.5), landed **unchanged** after judging both hero frames by
eye: the recommendation neither over- nor undershot, so no further iteration
was made. `vistadawn.skyHz.warm`, the same rectangle, one flag apart on one
build:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `skyHz.warm` | **+56.51** | **+33.03** |
| `skyR.warm` (anti-solar, frame-right at this pose) | **+32.87** | **+15.84** |
| `skyL.warm` (sun-side, frame-left) | +44.39 | +22.75 |

A4's arithmetic predicted the retune would land `skyHz.warm` "near +31 at
dawn instead of +56.51"; it landed at **+33.03**, within a count of the
prediction. `skyR` moved more than half the way toward neutral but stayed
positive (+15.84) at this specific rectangle; the cleaner proof that the
anti-solar sky is now genuinely readable as cool is `dawnsun.skyUp` (directly
overhead, away from the 5.85 degree sun), which crosses the sign: **+5.84 ->
-11.81**, i.e. actually blue-violet rather than "less warm", the difference
the brief asked to see. `dawnsun.hzBand.warm` 52.69 -> 41.19 and
`dawnsun.sunCore.warm` 61.60 -> 37.60: the warmth concentrates toward the sun
and the horizon instead of painting the whole dome.

**By eye** (`vistadawn`, `dawnsun`, both hero poses at RN-2175's own
invocations): the landscape keeps its warm, golden-hour light on every surface
the sun reaches, ground included, and the difference from the "before" frame
is entirely in the sky and haze layer, where it belongs. The frame no longer
reads as a uniform sepia filter laid over the whole image; the upper sky and
the region furthest from the sun now carry visible blue-violet rather than the
same cream-gold as the horizon. The two honest costs A4 already logged
(`vistadawn.nearG` darker under the corrected sun path, and `skyR` not
reaching a fully negative warm at that specific rectangle) are unrelated to
this constant and are not reopened here.

### 2.13.2 Noon identity, proved rather than argued

The low-sun blend `TONE.warm` (`ToneDrive.ts`) is `nightK * (1 - dayK)`, and
`dayK = smooth(elevationDot, 0.06, 0.42)` saturates to 1 above an elevation dot
of 0.42. `vista`'s sun sits at dot 0.699 (44.31 degrees), a full 0.28 past
saturation, so `TONE.warm` is exactly 0 there **independent of `WARM_LOWSUN`'s
value**: the highlight tint reduces algebraically to `tune.highlightTint`
unchanged, by construction, not by tuning. Measured rather than only argued:
`vista.skyHz.warm` **-23.46 before and -23.46 after**, `vista.box.warm`
**20.59 / 20.59**, `vista.world.warm` **0.80 / 0.81** (the 0.01 is float
rounding on an unrelated frame, not a moved term) -- every rectangle bit- or
near-bit-identical across the retune. Noon is untouched.

## 2.12 FIDELITY LANE A5: the far tier, the sky ambient on the props, and the 344,118 triangles that were not where anyone was looking

`lane/a5-vegetation`, base `origin/main` at e0daf76d, 2026-08-20. Block
RN-2200 to RN-2219; **RN-2200 to RN-2206 used, RN-2207 to RN-2219 surrendered
unused.** Frames `docs/screenshots/RN2200_*`. Served from a `vite preview` this
lane owned on `127.0.0.1:5392`, sentinel `dist-a5/of-sentinel-rn2200.txt`
fetched back before the first probe, killed by PID. Real Windows D3D11 (ANGLE),
RTX 4060 Ti, 1600x900.

### 2.12.1 RN-2200, the defect that had to go first

`PropLibrary.register` held two named slots per (stem, material) and filled the
far one with `if (hit[2] === '0') slot.lod0 = m; else slot.lod2 = m`. The `else`
is the bug: every tier that is not zero went into ONE slot, so the far geometry
was whichever mesh `Object3D.traverse` reached last. Dormant, because every prop
atlas ships exactly `_LOD0` and `_LOD2`; **invisible-to-harmful the moment one
ships a third rung**, because a `_LOD3` impostor card authored beside a `_LOD2`
cone would silently BECOME the LOD2 and every canopy tree from 45 m out would
draw four triangles while the cone rotted as dead bytes.

New `web/src/render/instancing/PropLods.ts`: `PROP_LODS = 4`, a `PropPart`
carrying a real `lods[]` keyed by tier, and `geomAtTier` walking DOWN to the
finest rung an asset ships (`NodeBatch.geomAt`'s rule and its reason).

**Proven both ways, and as a STATIC LINK rather than a probe**, because a probe
run against the shipped two-rung atlases cannot tell the broken rule from the
fixed one: `web/scripts/check-proplods.mjs` reproduces the OLD grouping verbatim
and asserts it loses the LOD2 on the same three-rung input the new grouping
passes, and asserts the new grouping is order-independent while the old one is
not. Wired in as `check:proplods`, so **the board is 8/8, not 7/7**.

### 2.12.2 RN-2201, the props join the sky ambient's authority, and A1's inference is corrected

A1's finding was that `StockFill` gives the props `TERRAIN_AMBIENT * AMP`, the
floor only, so the sky-ambient weight never reaches a blade of grass. New
`web/src/render/materials/PropSkyAmbient.ts` splices the terrain's own
`ofAtmoScatter(pM, up, 1e9, 2, 2) * uSkyAmbient` into the stock prop and node
programs from the SAME shared `IUniform` objects, published once from
`BootBodyScope` beside the carpet's wiring; chained into `PropWind`'s and
`RockShader`'s hooks (FurShader's precedent, one `onBeforeCompile` per material)
and installed standalone on the ten batches with none. 29 programs, 0 anchor
misses.

**AND THE MEASURED SIZE IS A TENTH OF A COUNT.** Three interleaved repeats per
arm: forestfloor box 19.79 -> 19.89 (+0.10);
meadow nearG 68.44 -> 68.69, shade 77.80 -> 77.99; `skyHi` 148.75 and `skyHz`
183.90 IDENTICAL TO THE DIGIT in both arms; `?propsky=20` gives +1.79, i.e.
exactly linear.

**THE TOLERANCE, corrected by this lane's verifier.** The MEAN lumas above
reproduced to 0.00 across their three runs, and that is the claim. It was
originally written as "every luma reproduced to 0.00", which reads as covering
the whole table and does not: the SPREAD statistics are not flat run to run.
The verifier reproduced `iqr` at 16.43 where this lane recorded 16.36, so the
honest tolerance on `iqr` is **+-0.07**, not zero. Nothing in the finding moves
-- +0.10 on a mean that repeats exactly still clears a +-0.07 band on a
different statistic -- but a stated tolerance that is wrong in the tight
direction is exactly the instrument defect this file's own catalogue is for, so
it is corrected rather than argued. So the term is real, it moves the props and not the sky it is
derived from, and **A1's inference named a real absence and overstated its
size**: the props were never unlit by the sky (RN-64's IBL captures a sky AND a
ground shell and every stock material samples it), they were outside the sky
ambient's AUTHORITY. They are inside it now, so A4's sky work reaches them with
nothing to keep in step. Two controls, because the change adds a value AND a
cost: `?propsky=off` removes the splice (the cost arm), `?propsky=0` keeps the
program and zeroes the value (the value arm); they photograph identically.

### 2.12.3 RN-2202, the far rung exists, and its measured triangle value today is ZERO

Every tree and every canopy prop now ships a `_LOD3`. `props_common.Prop` gains
`lod3` (callable only: a decimate ratio cannot make a card), emitted by the same
three lines LOD2 takes and fitted to the SAME box. The harvest trees get four
triangles of crossed leaf quad, fitted by the ONE transform `main()` already
replays from `Full_LOD0`; `props_canopy` gets a trunk stub plus crossed quads at
twelve. `contracts.json` gains 11 `_LOD3` nodes and 3 parts rows, and
`props_canopy.max_tris_total` 1996 -> 2032 with the arithmetic stated (the atlas
was EXACTLY at its cap: 742+50+334+28+784+58 = 1996, plus 3x12).

**The old contract comment forbidding a crossed quad here was true and is not
now**: it says "there is no texture pipeline, so an untextured crossed quad
renders as a solid rectangle", and RN-181 moved OF_Leaf into the alpha-tested
`leaf` card family. The rung therefore needs no texgen family, no `ROLE_FAMILY`
row and no new material.

Client: `LODS` 3 -> 4; `NODE_LOD3_M = 310`, derived (the LOD2 trunk stub is
0.40 m across and one pixel wide at 312 m in the shipped 1600x900 / 60 degree
frame, 779.4 px per metre per metre of range); `NodeField.lodFor` rewritten as a
walk over a `NODE_LOD_M` table so a rung is a table entry rather than a fourth
branch; `CANOPY_LOD3_M = 420` (the shortest canopy tree at 20 px). Scatter picks
three bands, and a prop with no impostor has `lod3M === lod2M` and `lod3 ===`
LOD2's id, so the ladder is inert for it by arithmetic rather than by a branch.

**forestfloor reads 1,616,640 with the rung and 1,616,640 without it, to the
digit.** Two reasons, both measured:

1. Nodes past 310 m are already per-instance frustum culled out of the eye pass.
   `attachFarShadowSkip` (RN-2203) removes them from the cascades too and
   reports **106,194 casters skipped against a frame delta of exactly zero** --
   the counter failure `ShadowLod.ts` already catalogues, now reproduced on a
   second subsystem and worth reading as confirmation rather than as a new bug.
2. **THE AERIAL POSE HAS NO TREE SOURCE AT ALL** (2.12.6).

### 2.12.4 RN-2204, THE HEADLINE, and nobody was looking at it

`PropLibrary` set `perObjectFrustumCulled` on the UNDERSTOREY batches only. The
BIOME batches -- 45.4 per cent of the forestfloor frame, `props=0` measures
734,300 of 1,616,640 -- had it off. That choice was measured at 9,340 props in
the NEAR pass and its own comment says the measurement went stale; it never
looked at three shadow cascades sweeping the same pool against a box a fraction
the size. Widened, behind `?propcullbiome=0`, which reproduces the pre-change
build to the digit:

| | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| forestfloor triangles | 1,616,640 | 1,272,522 +-24 | **-344,118 (-21.3%)** |
| forestfloor shadow-only | 834,045 | 598,373 | **-235,672 (-28.3%)** |
| meadow triangles | 3,039,951 | 1,819,419 | **-1,220,532 (-40.2%)** |

The culled arm is NOT flat: it jitters about 24 triangles run to run
(1,272,498 observed), because which instances a per-instance frustum test admits
depends on where the settle tick left the camera, and that is the whole point of
the mechanism. The uncalled arm IS flat at 1,616,640, for the same reason: it
admits everything. The delta is quoted from the medians and the jitter is three
parts in a hundred thousand of it.

Against the ceiling study's **853,675** the shadow figure is **-30.0 per cent**,
and the meadow crosses back under `StatsProbe`'s 2.7 M ALERT threshold, which it
had been exceeding. Pixels: box 19.89 / p05 3.65 / loFrac 0.76 / iqr 16.36
IDENTICAL TO THE DIGIT in both arms over three interleaved repeats, and pngdiff
0.57 per cent against a same-arm noise pair of 0.54 per cent. Frame time: p50
8.40 against 8.00 with within-arm spreads of 4.00 and 3.50, i.e. no separation,
reported as under the noise floor rather than as a number.

### 2.12.5 RN-2205 and RN-2206, the asset uplift

**Translucency** (charter difference 5, "no translucency approximation"): A2's
wrap-plus-forward-lobe model, term for term, with **A2's own two constants**
(0.55 wrap, 0.42 gain) so a tuft of carpet grass and a scatter fern standing in
it glow into a low sun by the same amount. Foliage programs only, so a boulder
pays nothing. `?foliagetrans=0` is the value control: meadow nearG 68.69 ->
69.25, shade 77.99 -> 78.64, sky rectangles identical to the digit -- it moves
SHADE more than lit ground, which is the property a wrap term is for.

**The one term that is not the carpet's**, and it is a stated limitation rather
than an omission: the carpet closes with `mix(shadow, 1, 0.35)` and a stock
`MeshStandardMaterial` in three r185 exposes no shadow factor to a splice.
`getShadowMask()` lives only in `shadowmask_pars_fragment`, which `meshphysical`
does not include -- the first attempt used it and took the whole build to
`VALIDATE_STATUS false`. So the factor is the constant **0.35**, the carpet's
own shadowed floor: a foliage prop glows by the amount a SHADED blade does,
everywhere. That costs the sunlit crown 65 per cent of the effect and buys the
guarantee that a fern on a shadowed forest floor cannot light itself.

**Polygon budget** (RN-2206): the two plains grass tufts go from `segs=3` to
`segs=4`, five triangles per blade to seven. Three levels can put only ONE bend
in a blade's arc, so its outline is two straight runs meeting at a corner, and a
corner at 1 m is exactly what "chunky" describes. The fern was already at 4 and
is the precedent. Cost, measured: meadow 1,819,419 -> 2,000,049, **+180,630
(+9.9%)**, paid out of RN-2204's 1,220,532. `Plains_GrassTuftA` 181 tris against
its unchanged 200 cap and `GrassTuftB` 195 against 240, so no budget row moved.
`detail_cards.glb` deliberately untouched: one triangle there costs 6,873.

**Soft normals were already shipped** and are named here so the charter item is
not double-counted: `FoliageNormal.ts` (RN-1766) already bends a prop's foliage
normals outward from its own base centre at 0.55, which is the soft-normal
approximation for a card. Nothing was added; nothing needed to be.

### 2.12.6 THE FINDING THIS LANE OWES THE WORLD AUDIT

The audit read 188,081 triangles at 1,200 m, saw no trees in any aerial frame,
proved the absence with an `atmos=0` control, and concluded that no impostor
tier existed. **Measured, this lane, on the real build:** `--scenario=surface`
builds no `Gameplay`, `of.game()` is `null`, and `TreeField` is ticked from
`GameplayFrame:31` off `d.player.body.feet`. **The flyover has never had a tree
to draw, at any radius, with or without an impostor tier.** Separately, the
scenery canopy tier is retired at runtime (`Config.canopyRadiusM` defaults to 0
per WG-116 and Reid's "all trees should be minable"), so `props_canopy.glb` is
not even loaded by default and `ScatterTuning.CANOPY_RADIUS_M` is a
documentation constant nothing reads.

After the whole lane, `flyover` still reads **188,081 triangles and box 159.98,
identical to the digit**. **There is therefore ONE frame and not a pair:**
`docs/screenshots/RN2200_flyover_unchanged.png`. The lane originally shipped a
`_before` and an `_after` that were byte-identical, which asserts the identity
instead of showing it and would let a real future change hide inside a pair
nobody re-diffs; the verifier caught it. The single frame is the honest artifact
-- the pose is unchanged by this lane, and the reason it is unchanged is the
finding above rather than a null result. The far rung is built, contracted, validated,
selected, shadow-skipped and correct; the pose that would exercise it needs a
Gameplay/boot change this lane did not make. **The transferable rule, and it
belongs in the trap catalogue: an absence proved by a negative control is still
only an absence. `atmos=0` proved no tree was DRAWN; it could not distinguish
"the tier is missing" from "the subsystem that owns trees is not running in this
scenario", and three weeks of queue was built on the first reading.**

Also measured and left for whoever takes it: `MAX_CELL_M = 64` caps the scatter's
reach at about 3.4 km from a 1,200 m eye, because the finest resident chunk band
there is depth 9 at 57.9 m cells and depth 8 at 116 m is refused; the gate is a
3-D distance from the EYE, so a radius R at altitude h covers a ground disc of
only `sqrt(R^2 - h^2)`.

(b) The shipped improvement is carried by the bays, and part of it is dilution: the bay steps are large non-periodic content, they nearly triple the profile's rms, and a normalised autocorrelation divides by exactly that. (c) **The "offset" half of RN-1822 is invisible to this metric by construction and that is the transferable part:** column-averaging destroys the v axis, so a joint jogged into two half-height lines 0.315 m apart correlates at the tile lag exactly as well as one full-height line. | RN-1610 | **THE LOW-TIER SUN DISC LOSS (RN-1573) IS FIXED BY FLOORING `iblSize` AT 256 ON EVERY TIER, ON RN-1415's OWN ALREADY-MEASURED COST, NOT A NEW ONE** | RN-1572/1573 authored the sun disc at its real 0.53 deg, ~2.25 texels at a 256 cube, and RN-1573 named the low-tier consequence without fixing it: at `iblSize` 64 (low) the disc is missed ENTIRELY (`brightTexels` 0, a 2x disc boost moves the cube maximum by a ratio of exactly 1.0000) and at 128 (med) it also misses (this lane's own measurement, not previously taken: `brightTexels` 0, `peakRatio` 5.20). Two of three tiers shipped the night's headline improvement to nobody. Three candidates were priced: **(a) floor the cube on every tier, (b) widen the disc only inside the IBL capture pass at small cube sizes (angular clamp to ~1.5 texels), conserving irradiance while the presented sky keeps 0.53 deg, (c) tier-dependent disc width.** Chosen: **(a)**, on the fewest-moving-parts test the brief set, because the cost was ALREADY MEASURED and did not need re-measuring: RN-1415 priced a 64->256 raise on this exact GPU at **0.6 to 1.0 ms a rebuild, CHEAPER than the 10.5 ms `SkyIbl`'s own docstring records at 64**, amortised over 240 frames plus an elevation trigger. Flooring low/med to 256 is not a new cost, it is reusing a number this repo already paid for and found negative (256 is cheaper than 64 was on this GPU, not merely affordable). (b) and (c) both add a capture-time branch and a second code path to buy a saving that is already zero; rejected on RN-1522/RN-1524's own standing lesson that a change bought for its cost must be shown to move something, and here the floor moves the SAME thing (b)/(c) would, for less code. **Implementation:** `web/src/render/Quality.ts` TABLE, `iblSize: 64` (low) and `iblSize: 128` (med) both become `iblSize: 256`; the `?iblsize=` override (RN-1415) is untouched and still restores any value including the pre-fix 64/128 for a negative control. **VERIFIED, real D3D, `probes/ibldiag.js`, `--quality=low`/`--quality=med`, `envsize` matching each tier's OLD cube size for the "before" arm (the diagnostic capture is size-parametrised independent of the live tier, so the old defect is reproducible on the current binary via `envsize=` without a second build):** low tier (`envsize=64`) pre-fix-equivalent: `peakRatio` 5.07, `brightTexels` 0/393,216, `pass: false` ("the disc boost did not change the cube maximum"). Low tier post-fix, live cube (`envsize=256`, and `of.stats().ibl.size` independently reads 256): **`peakRatio` 234.05, `brightTexels` 1/393,216, `pass: true`.** Med tier (`envsize=128`) pre-fix-equivalent: `peakRatio` 5.20, `brightTexels` 0. Med tier post-fix (`of.stats().ibl.size` reads 256): identical shape to low, sun present. **`artframe.js` `smelterhero` at `--quality=low --post=1`, canonical `machine` box (RN-1527's 99.7%-IBL-lit, no-direct-sun subject) `iblsize=64` vs default: luma 19.12 -> 19.02, essentially flat, and the `sunface` extra box (RN-1574's direct-sun subject) 67.34 -> 66.72, also flat.** Neither moving is the EXPECTED and CONSISTENT result, not a null: RN-1524 already established that a moderate-roughness (0.55), diffuse-dominated rectangle's MEAN luma barely moves under even a 200x disc boost (20.43 -> 20.44) because a 1-to-2-texel bright feature is a vanishing fraction of a GGX lobe's solid angle at that roughness; the real, large, honestly-reported signal is in the cube's own peak statistics above, exactly where RN-1573 measured the defect. `sunface`'s ~67 on low tier (comparable to RN-1574's high-tier 71.90) additionally confirms RN-1571/1574's direct-sun fix was already tier-independent and is not what this lane touched. **High tier: BIT-IDENTICAL, not merely unedited.** The `TABLE.high` line (`iblSize: 256`) was not touched by this diff, and that claim was checked rather than trusted: `artframe.js` `forestfloor` at `--quality=high --post=1` was captured on this fix, then the fix was `git stash`ed, the bundle rebuilt and re-served, the identical capture re-taken, and **the base64 PNG payloads compare byte-for-byte `===`**; every other field that differs between the two JSON reports (frame counts, ms timings, oracle call counts, sun-tick drift) is run-to-run scheduler noise, not pixels. **The presented sky is untouched on every tier by construction, not merely by measurement**: `SkyPass.ts` (the direct atmosphere/sun-disc render) has no functional reference to `iblSize` or `scene.environment` anywhere in it (grep-verified) -- `iblSize` only sizes the separate PMREM capture `environmentFrom` reads FROM the sky pass's own rendered output, never the reverse, so a cube-resolution change cannot reach the pixels the player looks at directly, only the reflections stock PBR materials borrow from it. `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` clean. | Accepted | 2026-08-14 |

| RN-1526 | **THE MIRROR ARM WAS HALF-ARMED AND REPORTED ITSELF ARMED, AND A VERIFIER CAUGHT IT: THE PER-PART CHANNEL ASSIGNS `roughnessFactor`, IT DOES NOT SCALE IT** | A fresh-context verifier ran `?ibldiag=mirror` with `?ibldisc=15` and `=200` and got luma 20.44 to 20.61 / iqr 15.31 to 15.51 against this lane's reported 24.54 / 31.32, and correctly refused to merge on it. **Reproduced exactly and the verifier's reading was right: `?ibldiag=mirror` ALONE renders the canonical box at luma 20.43 / p95 39.12 / iqr 15.30, BIT-IDENTICAL to the shipped frame, while `machineMatState()` reported `overrides: 14` and every material row read `metalness 1, roughness 0.02` live.** The cause is that `PartMaterial`'s injected GLSL ASSIGNS both factors from the per-vertex channel rather than scaling what the material carries, so with the channel on `MeshStandardMaterial.roughness` and `.metalness` are dead uniforms and `iblDiagOverride` writes numbers no fragment ever reads. **This is MachineMat's own failure mode (a) ("the injection is a silent no-op") wearing a green light, and the instrument this lane built to catch it counted the CPU-side write rather than anything downstream of it.** The first commit's arm happened to carry `?machinemat=0` beside it in every run, which is why the lane never saw the null; the flag was documented as required and that is precisely the shape that gets run without it. **FIXED, and not with a sentence: `machineMatEnabled()` now folds `iblDiagMirrorOn()` into the one predicate the bake gate and the injection gate already share, so the arm carries its own precondition, and `machineMatState().mirrorForcedOff` publishes why the channel is off.** After the fix, the verifier's exact invocation `?ibldiag=mirror` with no second flag reads **24.54 / 65.78 / 31.32**, reproducing this lane's figure, and `?ibldiag=mirror&ibldisc=200` reads 24.55 / 31.28, leaving RN-1524's conclusion unchanged. The shipped frame with no flags is 20.43 / 39.12 / 15.30, unmoved. **THE TRANSFERABLE RULE: an arm that needs a second flag beside it to mean anything will be run without it, so the precondition belongs in the code and not in the comment; and a counter that counts an assignment is not evidence that anything reads it.** | Accepted | 2026-08-13 |

| RN-961 | **The ripple pass, shipped: a rigid per-cell rotation, because constant-theta-in-a-cell removes the shear identically rather than bounding it** | RN-955's diagnosis was that rotating about the UV origin is not a rotation of the pattern. The sharper statement, and the one the fix is built on: **the shear came from theta VARYING, not from where the rotation was centred.** The map `p -> R(theta(p)) * p` has Jacobian `R + (dR/dtheta)(grad theta)p^T`, and that second term is the whole disease. Hold theta constant inside a cell and it is IDENTICALLY ZERO: the map becomes `p -> R*(p-a)+a`, a rotation about a point, an isometry. Not a bounded shear, an exact one. So side C cannot fire on it by construction rather than by tuning. What it costs instead is a SEAM, paid down two ways: the angle is a value noise sampled AT the integer cell index, so it is **constant within a cell and continuous between cells** (those sound opposed and are not, and a per-cell hash would have made every seam a maximal jump); and two half-offset grids are blended by centrality, so where one grid is at a seam the other is at a cell centre. Costs no fetch for the angle, which is ALU. The gradients are differenced INSIDE each grid's rotated frame and blended with the value's own weights, because differencing the blended height would carry a `grad(w)` term belonging to the blend rather than the ground and would light a ridge along every cell boundary. `?reliefswing=0` is the negative control. | Accepted | 2026-08-03 |

Shipped instead: `of.setSunElev(dot)`, which solves against `observer.up` AT THE MOMENT OF THE CALL (reusing `SkyPass.solveSunT`, the same solver Boot runs, so the two paths cannot drift) and returns `{wantDot, gotDot, err, t}` so an unreachable target is visible rather than silently rounded to the nearest achievable; and `stats().sky.sunSolve`, which publishes what the boot solve was aimed at and where. **The refusing case is reachable and was proven in the same loop**: at the pole `dirForT` pins the sun's y at 0.42 before normalising, so `dot(sunDir, up)` is the constant 0.3872 at every phase, and an ask of 0.90 returns `err 0.5112` while an ask of 0.3872 returns `err 0.0000`. | RN-33 | **An optical depth over a finite path is analytic, never marched, because a quadrature rule weights its samples by the path length and a path can be 500 km long** | The aerosol column uses `L * H / (h1 - h0) * (exp(-h0/H) - exp(-h1/H))`, the closed form for a linear height profile, with the `dh -> 0` limit taken explicitly because a horizontal ray is both the commonest case and the one that zeroes the denominator. A composer that assumes one scene and one depth buffer (three's own `EffectComposer` among them) would read the VIEW MODEL's depth, the last pass to write, and compute ambient occlusion for the player's forearms against a world no longer in the buffer. The near 1:1 scene is also the CORRECT subject: a planet 600 km away in the far scaled pass has no contact shadow, and the arms are a separate depth range whose occluders are not in the same buffer. Consequence, stated because it is a choice and not an accident: AO never touches the sky, the far scaled planet or the view model, while bloom and the grade see all four passes, which is what makes the sun disc and the engine plume bloom. `EffectComposer` was also unusable without breaking the DW-10 seam, since it takes a concrete `WebGLRenderer` and `Renderer.ts` is the only file allowed to name one; the stack talks to a three-method `PostHost` instead | **Accepted, shipped, driven-verified** (probe asserts occlusion CONTRAST, not that the pass ran) | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-11 | **A post pass may not sample any attachment of the framebuffer it writes to, and the rule earns its own buffer** | The obvious three-pass AO folds the upsample into the multiply: read half-resolution AO plus full-resolution depth, multiply into scene colour. The structural fix, and not a workaround: the depth-aware upsample resolves to its own full-resolution R8 buffer first, and the one pass that touches scene colour samples exactly one texture the scene framebuffer does not own. Cost of the rule is 1.4 MB and one draw call; the thing it buys is that the multiply is a one-tap shader with no depth uniforms at all, which is also why it cannot get the background test wrong. Separately, a contrast of 1.06 about a pivot of 0.4135 was applied to the ACES output, where mid-grey is 0.18: every value below the pivot was pushed down, hardest at the dark end, and the sky's red channel went 37.9 to 7.9 of 255 while every whole-frame mean stayed unremarkable. The grade now runs after the sRGB encode, where mid-grey really is 0.5. **General form: a metric and a curve both have a domain, and neither announces when it is being evaluated outside it** | **Accepted, both fixed and re-measured** | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-13 | **A before/after pair must re-pin every quantity that a data-dependent wait can move, and the sun is one** | The first before/after pair from this lane showed a warm-to-cool shift across an entire hillside that looked exactly like a colour grade and was entirely SUN ANGLE. The build recipe places machines by trying camera pitches until a ghost is legal, so two runs of the same recipe consume different amounts of sim time, and the sun moves with sim time. Setting the time once at the top of a probe is not enough: it has to be set again after every data-dependent wait and immediately before the frame that is captured. The pair was not wrong by a little, it was wrong in a way that invented a result for the effect under test. Related and worth keeping next to it: I then read a green wash across the ground in the after image and was ALSO wrong, and only measuring the two captures region by region settled it (ground 1.5% darker, its green bias identical in the before). **WG-28 says structural validation cannot replace looking at the thing; this is the converse, and both are true** | **Accepted** (probe re-pins; screenshots retaken) | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-14 | **A baked occlusion map and a screen-space one divide by SPATIAL FREQUENCY, and the way to prove it is to shrink the radius, not to threshold a face** | The material lane's ORM map bakes occlusion INSIDE one surface (panel gaps, bolt recesses, centimetres); this stack computes occlusion BETWEEN separate pieces of geometry (a machine's foot on ground, metres). Multiplying two terms that describe the same thing double-darkens and reads as muddy. The separation is structural rather than tuned: `aoRadiusM` 0.9 m on a half-resolution buffer is physically incapable of resolving a panel gap. **The first attempt to check this was the wrong instrument and is the lesson.** It asserted that a machine face away from contact darkens less than 6%, measured 10.1%, and would have been "fixed" by moving the threshold: the band it sampled is the smelter's own RECESSED PANELS, which are decimetre-scale and are legitimately this term's business, and "how much does this band darken" is not a statement about spatial frequency at all. The check is now: re-run the entire measurement with the radius set to 5 cm, the scale a bolt recess lives at, and require it to produce nothing. If the signal does not exist at that scale, no tuning of the shipped radius can be competing with the baked map | **Accepted, shipped** | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-8 | **A face is lit by the sky it can SEE and by the ground beside it, not by a sky term evaluated along local up** | Task 109's black cut banks. `skyAmb` was traced along `up` for every fragment, so it was a constant, and a near-vertical face with `ndl` clamped to zero kept 2.5 to 5.9 per cent of flat ground's light and rendered black. Neither replacement term is tuned: `skyView = 0.5 + 0.5 * dot(n, up)` is the share of the dome the face sees, and the bounce term's radiance is literally the flat-ground branch the shader already computes at that point, using `vBiomeColor` which IS that ground's albedo there. Two properties follow and both are checked: a flat fragment has `skyView == 1` and is algebraically unchanged (measured 154.8 -> 155.4), and every term goes to zero together at night and under shadow. Isolated with a CIRCULAR pit so that bearing is the only free variable, which is what makes the 155-count azimuthal spread attributable to `dot(N, sunDir)` and nothing else | **Accepted, shipped, driven-verified** (cut face over sunlit floor 0.135 -> 0.313, tolerance 0.18 derived from clear-sky diffuse; headlamp lift 16.99 unchanged) | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-9 | **A batch key must carry every property the batch's MATERIAL expresses, and the moment a material gains a map, the surface family becomes one of those properties** | `NodeBatch` bucketed by `metalness > 0.5`, which was free while every role was a flat colour and stopped being free the instant the bucket got a normal map: Leaf, LeafDeep, LeafDry, LeafLight, Grass, Ice and Oil shared `matte` with Bark and Rock, and the texture pass had recorded a REASON for each of those seven being left bare ("sub-pixel blades at any real viewing distance", "a double-sided card whose normal map fights the flat-shaded silhouette"). A rock normal map on a foliage card is worse than no map. The key is now `(family, metalness)` and the recorded decision survives the batching. Two properties follow and both are asserted against the LIVE materials rather than the table: every `flat` material carries zero maps, and every mapped one carries all four with `aoMap.channel === 0` and `repeat === 1/tile_m`. The cost is exactly one extra batch, measured at +4 draw calls of a 150 budget, which is the main pass plus three shadow cascades and nothing else. **The general form: three copy-pasted `normalize()` functions and two independently-derived bucketing rules is how a shared decision drifts, so the role -> family decision lives in ONE module and is checked against the shipped manifest at runtime** | **Accepted, shipped, driven-verified** (normal map alone moves the ground 2.78 counts mean over 288k px against a sky control of exactly 0.000; UVs 294 copied / 0 synthesised across all three paths) | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-6 | **The near voxel mesh draws ONLY what the heightfield cannot express, and it imports the terrain's COLOUR but not its LIGHT** | Two surfaces exist by construction and are allowed to: /core's 1 m solidity shell and the smooth `surfaceRadius` the chunk draws (DW-26). Any face the near mesh puts on the derived surface is a second drawing of ground the chunk already drew, offset by up to half a cell diagonal, so it pokes through as cube corners. The rule makes the mesh's responsibility a property of the surface rather than of the edit sets, which is what "faces of an edit" got wrong: `levelArea` edits a scatter of cells and their faces are isolated cubes. Colour comes from `BiomePalette` so cut rock and the hillside are one substance; light stays `Headlamp`'s, because the terrain program ignores three's light list and shading the mesh with it silently disabled the headlamp | **Accepted, shipped, driven-verified** (924 exposed -> 20 drawn; pad-vs-ground 33.6% -> 7.6%; lamp lift 3.46x -> 11.5x) | 2026-07-26 |

## 4. Architecture & approach
- **Scaled space transition:** maintain two representations per body, a far proxy (low-poly + baked) rendered by the scaled camera, and near streamed terrain. As the observer enters a body's approach band, cross-fade proxy→terrain; floating-origin keeps near terrain at small coords. The handoff is the "no loading screen" moment.
- **Depth:** log **or cascaded** depth in the near camera only (RN-2); the scaled camera uses plain depth at its own scale; the two are composited, not depth-merged (near always over scaled). Spike 1 measures UE's reversed-Z float first, cascaded preferred over `SV_Depth` (Nanite-compat). See [spike1-rendering §3](../spikes/spike1-rendering.md).
- **Factory LOD ladder (conceptual, not built before Phase 1):** (0) full instanced meshes + animated items near; (1) instanced machines, items as scrolling material far; (2) machines as impostors, no items; (3) not rendered, sim is on-rails anyway ([core-engine](core-engine.md) SimProxy). LOD band ties to the same active/on-rails distance bands. **Nanite's intended home** (RN-5).
- **Atmosphere:** UE5 **Sky Atmosphere** component (Rayleigh/Mie, surface→space fade-to-black out of the box) driven by camera altitude + sun direction + `FAtmosphereProfile` from [world-gen](world-gen.md) (D-006). Custom analytic LUT is a Phase-1 fallback. Forge only; Cinder airless. See [spike1-rendering §4](../spikes/spike1-rendering.md).

## 5. Interfaces & dependencies

### Published this pass (RN-1200): `self.__ofMachineMat`, and one line that is now a CONTRACT

`state()` (enabled / flagPresent / mode / bareOn / bareFlagPresent / bare / baseRoughness /
baseMetalness / baked / roles) and `table()` (the per-ROLE rows `PartMaterial` actually
wrote, plus **`distinct`**, `injections` and `missing`). `distinct` is the discriminating
field and it tells the three states apart with one number: **0** under `?machinemat=0`,
exactly **1** under `?machinemat=flat`, and **17** across the 18 shipped machine roles under
the default. `table()` is also the ONLY reachable read of `partMatState()` on this path,
because `SpiderFlock.partMatStats` needs a flock; without it the anchor-miss failure mode
would have no read-out in a machine frame at all.

**`MachineBatch.makeMaterial`'s `metalness: 0.45, roughness: 0.55` are now an interface, not
an implementation detail.** `tools/blender/render_machines.py:326` regex-reads them as
numeric literals and raises rather than guess. They must stay literals in that constructor;
`MachineMat.assertMachineBase` throws at boot if they and `MachineMat`'s copy disagree.
Changing the machine base is therefore a two-file act with a third-party consumer, and it
needs an Admin-logged decision like any other published interface.

### Published this pass (RN-845): `window.__ofBodies`, the second body's driven surface

`report()` (present / reason / drawn / **refusedId** / texW / texH / bakeMs / oracleSamples /
uvResidual / **eyeM** / simSecs / per-body distanceM, angularDiamDeg, posM, texelM, relief
min-max, and an `optics` record READ BACK OFF THE LIVE UNIFORMS rather than recomputed),
`aim()` (yawDeg / pitchDeg exactly as `of.look` takes them, elevationDeg, angularDiamDeg,
distanceM, aboveHorizon), `planetshine()` (onGround and onBody, both as a fraction of the
sun's irradiance, plus a Rec.709 luma so a lighting lane does not re-derive one),
`facts()`, `airProfile(id)`, `setRelief` / `setDetail` / `setDebug` / `setTimeS`, and
`setFov` (which is `CameraRig.setFov`, present since W1 and never called by anything;
**a zoomed frame has a different shadow-LOD ladder, so no triangle, draw-call or LOD
number may be taken from one**).

Flags, all registered in `run.mjs`'s PAGE_PARAMS in the same commit: `?skybodies=0`
(structural control, nothing is constructed), `?skybodyrelief=`, `?skybodydetail=`,
`?skybodytex=`, `?skybodytime=`.

### Consumed from physics (PH-161), and this is the whole of it

`_of_body_state(bodyId, simTimeS)` -> 6 f64 in the PARENT's frame, and
`_of_body_facts(bodyId)` -> 4 f64 `[radiusM, muM3S2, soiRadiusM, orbitPeriodS]`. Both are
symbol-detected; a client on an older wasm reports what it is missing and draws nothing.
**No number about a body's position or size appears anywhere else in the render tree**, and
if one ever does it is a bug: that is the whole point of `render/CelestialEphemeris.ts`.

**Depends on (inbound), Spike-1 contracts now PINNED (code against these, not the prose):**
- **core-engine** ([spike1-core-engine.md §5](../spikes/spike1-core-engine.md)): `FUniverseCoord`+`FFrameId` & `ToEngine/FromEngine`/`FFloatingOrigin`; `FReferenceFrame`/`IFrameGraph` (`ToUniverse(SimTime)` for body/star positions); `ISimProxy.Position()/Velocity()`; `ISimClock.Alpha()/TickIndex()`. **Events: `OnOriginRebased(DeltaEngine, NewOrigin)`** (re-anchor near scene + atmosphere transform; scaled scene untouched) and **`OnSOIChange(FSOIChangeEvent)`** (re-target approach body). A `UniverseCoord` carries its frame, never a bare `FVector`.
- **world-gen** ([spike1-worldgen.md §4–§5](../spikes/spike1-worldgen.md)): `FTerrainChunk` (center as `FUniverseCoord`, chunk-local positions, skirts, `MaterialId`); `ITerrainProvider::OnChunkReady`/`OnChunkEvicted`/`UpdateStreaming`; `FBodyParams`/`FAtmosphereProfile` (we consume radius/atmosphere, D-006, hardcode nothing). Re-project chunk transforms on `OnOriginRebased` via `CenterUniverse.ToEngine`.
- **physics** (later): entity transforms (interpolated) for vehicles/parts.
- **factory-sim** ([spike3-factory-sim.md §6](../spikes/spike3-factory-sim.md)): the **factory→render stream, PINNED by factory-sim, CONFIRMED here (RC-8), now EMITTED + numerically validated headlessly (factory-sim FS-14: `EmitEntityStates`/`EmitBeltFlowStates`/`GetLineItems`)**. `FFactoryEntityState` (~32B/visible entity: `Id`,`TypeId`,`Position` as `UniverseCoord`,`FQuat16` orient, `VisualState`,`AnimPhase`,`Lod` hint,`Flags`), `FFactoryBeltFlowState` (per visible line: `ItemTypeDominant`,`FlowSpeedQuant`,`Density`,`Compressed`), and on-demand `GetLineItems(LineId)→{itemType,unitOffset}[]`, **the only O(items) call, pulled ONLY at RN-3 LOD-0**. Stream is **delta-only**, drained at render FPS, transforms interpolated via `ISimClock::Alpha()`. Belts emit `FFactoryBeltFlowState` only on flow-state *change* (a steady belt is silent). We evaluate items' world placement via the sim's baked `pathUnitToWorld` (sim never evaluates it; only we do, only for LOD-0 items). **See RC-8 resolution below + §5.4 factory-LOD-ladder mapping.**
**Provides to (outbound):** the rendered frame; camera/observer transform feedback for LOD/AOI; screenshot/observation hooks (useful to [networking](networking.md) AOI tuning).
**Open contract gaps flagged to Admin (Spike 1):**
- `FAtmosphereProfile` has Rayleigh fields but **no Mie params**, request world-gen add `MieScaleHeightM`/`MieScatteringScale`/`MieAnisotropy` (non-breaking; D-006-owned by world-gen). Placeholder Mie used meanwhile.
- UE5 Sky Atmosphere renders **only one atmosphere on screen at once**, fine now (only Forge has one), a constraint for the multi-atmospheric-body future.
**~~Still to negotiate later~~ → NEGOTIATED & CONFIRMED:** the factory→render stream schema (fields, update rate) was pinned by factory-sim Spike 3 §6 and is **confirmed sufficient for RN-3 here (RC-8, below)**, with one *non-breaking* field-add requested (`AABB`/bounds for culling; see RC-8 §4).

### RC-8 resolution, does the factory→render stream clear the render wall? **CONFIRMED (with one additive field request), and now NUMERICALLY VALIDATED HEADLESSLY.**
> *Owner: rendering · Closes reconciliation item [RC-8](../spikes/PHASE0-SUMMARY.md#4-consolidated-reconciliation-register) (the #1 open Phase-0 cross-risk). Co-validation of the integrated real-hardware case stays a Phase-1 joint task with factory-sim. Date: 2026-06-14; **headless numeric validation added 2026-06-15**.*

> **HEADLESS NUMERIC VALIDATION (2026-06-15, jointly with factory-sim).** The RC-8 verdict below was reasoned *on paper* from the §6 contract. It is now **backed by integers**, with no GUI and no GPU: factory-sim emits the §6 stream (`EmitEntityStates`/`EmitBeltFlowStates`/`GetLineItems`, additive + read-only) and a numeric render-cost model (`core/include/of/render_cost.h`, tested in `core/tests/test_render_cost.cpp`, the `render_cost_tests` ctest suite, 133 checks green) scores it against the RN-3 ladder. **The numbers confirm every load-bearing claim of this resolution:**
> - **The O(items)→O(lines) collapse is real and quantified.** A **100,000-entity** stress scene with a realistic LOD spread, Near0 1,500 machines / 300 lines · Mid1 8,000 / 2,000 · Far2 30,000 / 6,000 impostors · OnRails3 60,500 / 12,000 (not rendered), carries **12,180,000 discrete items on its belts**, yet per-frame item-render work is **180,000 item-evals = the 300 Near0 lines × 600 items/line** (the *only* band that calls `GetLineItems`). **>98% of items (12,000,000) are collapsed away** into LOD-1 flow-material / LOD-2 impostor / LOD-3 not-rendered and never hit `pathUnitToWorld`. Item-eval work scales with **Near0 LINES (hundreds), not items (millions)**, exactly the §6.2 mechanism.
> - **Draw calls scale with machine-TYPE variety (tens), not entity count.** The same 100k-entity scene issues **72 draw calls** (≈ 3 drawing bands × 20 machine TypeIds + belt-material draws), **NOT ~100,000**, instancing buckets per `TypeId`. A slice-scale scene (400 machines / 200 lines, all near) issues **16** (12 machine types + 4 item materials) vs 600 entities.
> - **Instances stay under the ceiling.** 219,500 live instances (39,500 drawn machines + 180,000 near item meshes), comfortably below the ~2 M instance ceiling (§5.2 budget).
> - **Monotonicity + LOD-3-zero proven.** Pushing a fixed population Near0→Mid1→Far2→OnRails3 strictly reduces cost; **LOD-3 (on-rails) contributes EXACTLY ZERO** draws, instances, and item-evals (the proxy is demoted, factory-sim §5).
>
> This retires the *paper* qualifier on RC-8: the stream contract demonstrably clears the wall for both a slice factory and a 100k-entity stress factory inside one per-frame budget. **What a cost model cannot measure remains the Phase-1 integrated co-validation residual (§5.3 / R5):** the real-hardware LOD-0 `pathUnitToWorld` instance-build cost, Nanite-on-small-meshes, LOD-band hysteresis, and camera-cut burst budgeting, the *render-side* hot spots, which this model flags but only a real renderer can time. (Source: factory-sim FS-14; `render_cost_tests` green in the 14-suite headless core.)

**1. LOD-band → stream mapping (RN-3 ladder, §5.4, against factory-sim §6.2).** Each band pulls strictly less from the stream as distance grows, the mechanism that decouples sim-scale (millions of items) from render-scale:

| RN-3 band | What we draw | What it pulls from the stream | Per-item cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **LOD-0 (near)** | Full instanced machine meshes + **discrete animated item meshes** on belts; inserter/craft anim from `AnimPhase` | `FFactoryEntityState` per machine (one instance row) **+ `GetLineItems(LineId)`** to place item instances along the sim's baked `pathUnitToWorld` | **O(visible items)**, the *only* band that pays it |
| **LOD-1 (mid)** | Instanced machines; belt items as a **scrolling-flow material** (no discrete item meshes) | `FFactoryEntityState` + `FFactoryBeltFlowState`: `FlowSpeedQuant`→material scroll rate, `Density`→fill look, `Compressed`→cheaper path. **No `GetLineItems`, no per-item data.** | **O(visible lines)** |
| **LOD-2 (far)** | Machine **impostors** (billboard/octahedral); no items, no belt material | `FFactoryEntityState`: `TypeId`,`Position`,`VisualState` only (one tiny instance row); belts collapse into the impostor field | **~0** |
| **LOD-3 (on-rails)** | **Not rendered**, chunk is demoted to `ISimProxy` rate-model (factory-sim §5) | **nothing**, proxy emits no per-entity stream when on-rails | **0** |

The load-bearing guarantee we are confirming: **`GetLineItems` (the lone O(items) call) is pulled only at LOD-0, on demand, per line we *chose* to draw discretely.** The instant the camera pushes a line past LOD-0, its item cost collapses to one `FFactoryBeltFlowState` material param set (O(lines)), then to nothing. `Lod` in `FFactoryEntityState` is the sim's *hint*; **we own the final band decision** (screen-space size / distance), and the contract explicitly lets rendering override it, correct division of authority.

**2. Rough budget (assumptions stated).**
*Assumptions:* one commodity desktop GPU + UE5 instancing (HISM/Nanite-backed machine meshes per RN-4/RN-5); ~2 M instances/frame is a sane GPU-instance ceiling; target 60 FPS / ~16.6 ms; belt physics from factory-sim §2 (**256 sub-units/tile, 64-unit saturation spacing → 4 items/tile/lane × 2 lanes = up to 8 items/tile saturated**; lines capped at 100 tiles).

- **LOD-0 item ceiling (where `GetLineItems` O(items) starts to hurt).** A fully saturated 100-tile line = ~800 items (both lanes); a realistic visible near-field rarely shows whole 100-tile lines saturated. Budget the *discrete-item* draw, not the line count: aim to keep **LOD-0 discrete belt items in view ≲ ~50–100k item instances**. At that range the per-frame work is (a) the `GetLineItems` pulls, O(items) but a flat read of the sim's gap arrays, cheap relative to (b) building/refreshing ~50–100k instance transforms via `pathUnitToWorld`. **`pathUnitToWorld` evaluation, not `GetLineItems` itself, is the LOD-0 cost** (each visible item = one arc-length→transform eval + one instance write). So LOD-0 should cover roughly **a few hundred to ~1–2k machines + the belts physically near the player** (the foreground bay), which at 8 items/tile yields tens of thousands of item instances, comfortably inside the instance ceiling. Past that, LOD-1.
- **Where LOD-1+ must engage.** LOD-0 ends at the distance where a belt item subtends **≲ ~1–2 px** (discrete items no longer legible, the scrolling material is indistinguishable and far cheaper). For ~0.5 m items at 1080p/60° FOV that is on the order of **a few tens of meters**; we drive it on **screen-space size, not a hard metric distance**, so it auto-scales with zoom/FOV. LOD-1→LOD-2 at the distance a *machine* drops below ~a few px (impostor indistinguishable from mesh). LOD-2→LOD-3 is **not ours**, it coincides with core-engine's on-rails demote band (factory-sim §5 / FS-4), so "far enough to be on-rails" and "far enough to not render" are the *same* band by construction.
- **Draw-call / instance / bandwidth ballpark for a realistic base (thousands near, 100k total, most far/on-rails):**
  - *Draw calls:* machines instanced **per `TypeId`** → draw calls = O(distinct machine types in view) ≈ **tens, not thousands** (one instanced draw per type per LOD bucket). Belt LOD-1 material = one instanced/merged draw per material. This is the whole point of RN-3 + instancing: **draw calls scale with *type variety*, not entity count.**
  - *Instances:* LOD-0 ≲ ~1–2k machine instances + tens of thousands of item instances; LOD-1 machines = instanced rows (cheap); LOD-2 impostors = up to ~tens of thousands of 2-tri billboards (trivial). Total live instances comfortably **< the ~2 M ceiling**.
  - *Stream bandwidth:* `FFactoryEntityState` ~32B, **delta-only**. Machines don't move → `Position` is silent; only `AnimPhase`/`VisualState` (≤~3B) tick for *active* machines in view. A few thousand visible active entities × a few bytes × 60 Hz = **single-digit MB/s**, negligible. Belts emit `FFactoryBeltFlowState` only on flow-state change → near-silent in steady flow. The only heavy pull is `GetLineItems` at LOD-0, and it is **read-only, bounded by visible-item count, and never per-tick-pushed.**
  - **Conclusion:** a realistic factory (thousands near, 100k total with most far/on-rails) **clears the wall**: only the small foreground set ever hits the O(items) path, draw calls stay in the tens via instancing, and stream bandwidth is trivial. The 100k entities are mostly LOD-2 impostors (≈0) or LOD-3 on-rails (0). The contract's LOD-0-only `GetLineItems` rule is exactly what makes this hold.

**3. Verdict + residual risk.** **CONFIRMED, the contract plausibly clears the render wall.** The §6 stream gives us everything RN-3 needs and, critically, *lets us stop pulling per-item data the instant we zoom out*, the precise mechanism the render wall demands. The contract is sufficient **as-is** to build LOD-0/1/2/3; the one addition below is an *optimization for culling/band-selection*, not a correctness gap. **Residual render-wall risk → must be measured in the Phase-1 integrated co-validation (jointly with factory-sim):**
  - (a) **Instance build/refresh cost at LOD-0**, whether ~50–100k `pathUnitToWorld` evals + instance-transform writes/frame fit the frame budget on real hardware (this, not `GetLineItems` itself, is the suspect hot spot). Measure with a saturated near-field bay.
  - (b) **Nanite on thousands of small factory meshes** (RN-4/RN-5, rendering.md R1), Nanite's cost on many small static-ish machine meshes is still unmeasured; this is *the* open Nanite question (terrain already settled to classic).
  - (c) **LOD-band hysteresis / popping** at the LOD-0↔1 boundary (discrete-items → scrolling-material swap), must cross-fade or it pops, the factory analogue of R2.
  - (d) **Stream drain vs. camera-cut spikes**, a fast pan that promotes many lines to LOD-0 in one frame causes a burst of `GetLineItems` + instance builds; need amortized/budgeted promotion (spread builds across frames, like world-gen's per-tick mesh budget).

**4. Field requests to factory-sim (non-breaking; routed to Admin).** `FFactoryEntityState`/`FFactoryBeltFlowState` are **sufficient as-is for correctness**. One *additive* request would materially help our band-selection/culling and is cheap for the sim (it already stores `StaticDef.AABB`, §1.3 / `bounds`):
  - **`AABB Bounds` (or a packed bound-radius) on `FFactoryEntityState`**, lets us frustum-cull and compute screen-space size for LOD-band selection **without** a per-type asset-bounds lookup on the render side, and without evaluating geometry. Sim already carries `StaticDef.bounds`; surfacing it (or a 2-byte bound radius) in the stream row is non-breaking and removes a render-side indirection. *Nice-to-have, not a blocker.*
  - **(Already in contract, just affirming we rely on it):** the `Lod` hint field and rendering's right to override it; `Compressed` on the flow state (cheaper LOD-1 path); `FlowSpeedQuant`/`Density` for the scrolling material. **No other additions needed.** If the `AABB` add is declined, we fall back to a render-side per-`TypeId` bounds table, slightly more render bookkeeping, zero contract change.

- **[RN-2225 to RN-2234, CLOSED 2026-08-20 by `lane/aerial-trees`, full record in section 2.14] THE AERIAL POSE HAS NO TREE SOURCE, and the far tier cannot be judged until it does.** All three items are answered. (1) The tick: `vegOrigin` plus a player-free `VegetationScope`, and the flyover now streams 683 harvest trees and 20 rocks in a scenario that built no `Gameplay` -- **and moved the frame by zero pixels, because the 620 m ring sits below the bottom edge of a 1,200 m frame whose ground starts at 1,243 m.** (2) The canopy tier: ON by default as the FAR tier only, from `CANOPY_NEAR_M` (550 m) outward, so the atlas is neither deleted nor half-live and every reachable tree is still minable; its `_LOD3` rung now carries the entire far forest and its LOD0/LOD2 rungs are unreachable from this tier. (3) `MAX_CELL_M`: untouched at 64 for the ground tiers, with `CANOPY_MAX_CELL_M` 128 for the canopy alone, and the 3-D-versus-ground distance bug is fixed on the canopy gates with the arithmetic written down. **Still open and routed on:** the impostor costs FOUR instances for twelve triangles (a single-material `_LOD3` in `tools/blender/build_props_canopy.py` divides this tier's whole cost by four and is the correct next move), the aerial picture is limited by world-gen's canopy density table (1.8 per cent ground coverage at the spawn), and the `vista` judgement pose is blind to vegetation because its site is above the treeline. Three separate findings, each measured on the real build by lane A5 and each currently costing the impostor rung its entire reason to exist. Admin has allocated **RN-2225 to RN-2234** for them; they are listed here rather than left in 2.12.6's prose so they are allocatable off a list instead of off a paragraph.
  1. **`--scenario=surface` builds no `Gameplay`,** so `of.game()` is `null` and `TreeField` -- ticked from `GameplayFrame:31` off `d.player.body.feet` -- never runs. The `flyover` pose has never had a tree to draw at any radius, with or without an impostor tier, which is why it reads 188,081 triangles before and after this lane. Needs a tree source driven by the OBSERVER rather than by a player body, or an aerial scenario that builds one. **This is the blocker: until it lands, no vegetation lane can honestly claim an aerial result.**
  2. **The scenery canopy tier is retired at runtime.** `Config.canopyRadiusM` defaults to 0 (WG-116 and Reid's "all trees should be minable"), so `props_canopy.glb` is not loaded by default and `ScatterTuning.CANOPY_RADIUS_M` / `CANOPY_LOD3_M` are documentation constants nothing reads. The canopy `_LOD3` rung RN-2202 authored is correct, contracted and validated, and dormant. Either the atlas becomes harvest nodes (the consequence `build_props_canopy.py`'s own header flagged and declined to start) or the tier is deleted; leaving it half-live is what made this measurable at all.
  3. **`MAX_CELL_M = 64` caps the scatter's reach at about 3.4 km from a 1,200 m eye,** because the finest resident chunk band there is depth 9 at 57.9 m cells and depth 8 at 116 m is refused. The gate is a 3-D distance from the EYE, so a radius R at altitude h covers a ground disc of only `sqrt(R^2 - h^2)` -- a fact worth writing down before anyone raises a radius expecting the ground under it to fill.

- **[RN-45, OPEN, needs world-gen] A per-chunk noise PHASE in the terrain chunk format.** Sub-metre terrain surface detail of any kind is unreachable from planet-centred metres: float32 at Forge's 6e5 m radius has a 0.0625 m ULP, which is 3 to 15 times the pixel footprint of the ground under the player, so any SCREEN DERIVATIVE of a field keyed on it quantises into concentric arcs (measured, `docs/screenshots/RN45_iso_bump.png`). The fix is a phase reduced modulo the octave period on the CPU in float64, carried alongside the integer cell index, so the shader adds a small local offset to a small local coordinate and never forms a 6e5 intermediate. That is a chunk-format change and therefore world-gen's. The macro COLOUR term does not need it and has shipped.

- **OPEN, INSTRUMENT (RN-1250, 2026-08-03) - in the close-up machine frame the VEGETATION boxes are not repeatable and cannot serve as controls.** A same-flag null pair moved **7,403 pixels of 59,200 (12.5 per cent)** in a foreground ground box and **1,183 of 15,000 (7.9 per cent)** in a box containing distant trees, both symmetric darker/lighter, i.e. wind phase rather than light. The MACHINE box is bit-identical across the same pair (0 pixels moved, maxDelta 0.0), so in this scene the subject is the repeatable thing and the "control" is not. This is RN-1202's glove finding in a second place, and the general rule is the one that generalises: **publish a same-flag null pair for every box you intend to trust, not only for the subject.** A control box that moves 12 per cent under no change will absorb any effect smaller than that and report a pass.
- **OPEN, AND IT IS A REAL DOUBLE OCCLUSION (RN-1252, 2026-08-03) - a machine is occluded three times over and one of them is a tiling texture that has never seen its geometry.** `attachSurface(m, 'panel', ...)` binds `of_panel_orm.png` as `aoMap` (red channel mean 0.7224, floor 0.4196), `PostDefaults.aoStrength = 0.9` multiplies TOTAL radiance and says so in its own comment, and `csStrength = 0.72` does the same. On the terrain, where direct sun dominates, "holding a little back is the honest correction for occluding light that was never occludable" is exactly right. On a machine's camera-facing face, which this lane has now measured to be **100 per cent indirect**, a term that multiplies total radiance is occluding light that was already occluded, and the tiling AO map is doing it with a pattern authored for a flat panel rather than for the box it is wrapped around. `?ao=0` is worth 24.9 per cent on that face. **Deliberately NOT changed here**, because `aoStrength` and `csStrength` were calibrated by RN-208's `lookdev.js` on terrain frames with no machines in them, and retuning a calibrated constant without re-running its own instrument is the failure INSTRUMENTS.md opens with. The shape of the work is a machine-lit arm of `lookdev.js` first, then one pair per constant.
- **OPEN, AND IT IS THE REST OF RN-1203 (2026-08-03) - the machine batch still pins `panel` onto six families that are not `panel`, and the honest fix is five surfaces, not "one extra fetch".** `Rubber` belt decks and slats, `Rock`/`RockDark` on the smelter hearth, the foundation body and the launch pad's blast slab and flame trench, `Plate` on the station deck (99.7 per cent of all `OF_Plate` area), `Iron` and `Coal` on the station's torn structure and scorch, and most of `items_atlas.glb` all wear plate seams, rivet rows and a weld bead. `flat` is closed; the other five are not. **Do not close it by baring them**: bare removes the wrong map and leaves nothing, and those are large areas. The shape of the work is a family index baked per vertex beside `aRole`, plus the tiling surfaces bound as explicit uniforms rather than through `material.normalMap`, and it needs a DW-10 argument and a sampler budget before it is worth starting.
  - **CLOSED 2026-08-13 BY RN-1478, AND THE SHAPE PROPOSED ABOVE IS THE ONE THAT WAS REFUSED.** The sampler budget this paragraph asked for was computed and it kills the per-vertex-index design: `MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS` measured **16** on the real D3D11 path, one machine program already spends **9** (5 surface samplers + PMREM env + three cascade shadow maps), and 3 more per extra family puts `beltCargo` at 18. What landed instead is one `BatchedMesh` PER FAMILY with the ordinary `attachSurface` call, so the per-program sampler count does not move at all and the cost is **+8 draw calls on the machine shot**. `leaf` is the one family that stays folded into `panel` and it is refused structurally rather than left undone: a card family is unit-UV and alpha-cut, and this path's UVs are metres, so a card sampled here would punch leaf-shaped holes through a solid item chunk (`Surfaces.isTilingFamily`, verified against the manifest's own `uv_space`).
- **OPEN, AND IT IS A LOOKDEV FINDING RATHER THAN A MATERIALS ONE (RN-1200, 2026-08-03) - a machine's camera-facing surface is lit almost entirely by ambient, at every hour this site can reach.** Swept in the channel-off arm across the whole reachable sun band at the spawn, the close-up machine box runs **6.89 / 9.64 / 11.07 / 12.24 mean counts of 255 at sun dot 0.20 / 0.45 / 0.65 / 0.80**: monotonic, and never above 12.24, while the GROUND in the same frames reaches 105. A player places a machine in FRONT of themselves and then walks up to it, so the face they see is the one turned away from a rising sun, and the site's azimuth is fixed. **This is why a large per-role material change moves the median by 9 per cent rather than by 30**: there is very little light on the surface for any material response to act on. It is the same shape as ART-DIRECTION.md's sequencing rule, pointed at the machines: the response curve and the ambient are upstream of the material.

An earlier quiet-scene pair had shown 6 pixels for the null and 11,317 for the subject, which reads exactly like a real effect on the player's hands and is not one. **Any machine measurement must exclude that box and must publish a same-flag null pair rather than one, because a single null can land on the same animation phase by chance.**
- **PARTLY CLOSED, PARTLY ESCALATED (RN-850, 2026-08-03) - R17's Beach half is not a shader-constant problem and never was.** RN-843 left the default unchanged "pending an anisotropy instrument". The instrument exists (`probes/aniso.js`), validated 0.066 isotropic against 0.9993 corduroy, and the default stays where it is on a much stronger footing: Plains has a clean interior minimum AT the shipped 31.85 texels, and Beach has no minimum reachable from this knob because its corduroy is in `of_ground_relief` under biome 1's channel weights rather than in the finite difference. **CINDER'S HALF IS STILL LIVE and would yield to the support** (its difference-spectrum peak moves 9.4 px to 54 px across the sweep, which is the signature of a support stamping its own scale), but no single value serves both bodies, so a per-biome or per-body support is the shape of any real fix and that is a bigger decision than one constant. **A KNOWN GAP IN THE INSTRUMENT, stated because it bounds the conclusion:** the index is a CORDUROY detector, not a SCRIBBLE detector. A synthetic globally-isotropic scribble (nested contour bands, locally 1-D everywhere) reads 0.0204, indistinguishable from noise, and the structure-tensor coherence built to cover that case did not separate it either. The measured artefact at all three sites has an oblique preferred direction well above floor, so the instrument applies here, but that is a fact about these sites and not a guarantee about the next one.
- **OPEN, AND IT IS ANOTHER LANE'S BUT IT BLOCKS MINE (RN-846, 2026-08-03) - Cinder's night ground is a CONSTANT 15.93 counts and nothing in this domain accounts for it.** Measured at four sun elevations below the horizon: p05 12.93 and p50 15.93 at -0.35, -0.60 and -0.85 alike, so it does not vary with how far the sun is down and is therefore a constant term rather than a residue of grazing light. It survives `?lamp=0`, `?iblground=0` and `?bouncelit=0` UNCHANGED to the hundredth of a count, and `?horizonocc=0` moves it 0.71. It is not a tone-curve lift: pointed at the sky, the airless night sky is **0.00 exactly across 144,000 pixels, p05 through max**, so black maps to black and this is real light on the terrain. **Consequence, and it is why this is filed rather than fixed here: planetshine at full Forge is 1.837e-4 of sunlight, worth about 0.9 of a count, so it is 1/17 of a floor whose source is unknown. No night-lighting change on an airless body can be measured until this is found.** The suspect is a constant `ambient` term in `TerrainShader`; that file plus `TerrainMaterial.ts` and `TerrainArt.glsl.ts` are all dirty with another lane's edits tonight, so this lane did not open them. Whoever takes it gets the measurement for free: `probes/lunarnight.js` plus `?sundot=` at four values.
- **OPEN, R70 IS NOW VISIBLE AND HAS A RATE (RN-845, 2026-08-03) - the drawn moon and the frame-graph moon separate at 542.5 m/s.** `orbital.h` says plainly that `sim_world.h` installs Cinder as a STATIC frame offset while `transfer.h` solves against a Cinder that moves, and that reconciling them is a world decision. Admin ruled that Cinder orbits, so the renderer reads `of_body_state` every frame. The two therefore diverge, and the rate is not small: the orbit is 542.5 m/s (verified against the client, which reported z = -2305.6 m at simSecs 4.25, i.e. 542.5 x 4.25 to the metre), so after one hour of sim time at 1x the drawn moon is **1,953 km from where the frame graph has it, which is 9.8 Cinder radii**. Under warp it is much worse, because the day clock takes a warp credit and this one does not. Nothing is wrong in the renderer: it is drawing the ephemeris Admin chose. **But an autopilot that flies to the frame graph's Cinder will now visibly miss the one in the sky**, and that is the first time R70 has had a symptom anyone can see. Admin's to route.
- **OPEN (RN-849, 2026-08-03) - the bake is 591 ms of the boot thread and nothing amortises it.** One body, 262,144 oracle calls, measured; the ladder is 51.6 / 169.9 / 591.0 / 2,398.1 ms at 128 / 256 / 512 / 1024. It is paid once and it is not on any frame, so it is a boot regression rather than a frame one, but it is a seventh of a second and a third body would double it. The cheap fix is the oracle WORKER, which already exists and already has its own body handle (`WorkerProbe.ts`), so the bake could be posted rather than blocking; the disc would then need a low-resolution first texture and an upgrade, which is a real design and not a tweak. Named with the sizing attached rather than done in a hurry at the end of a lane.
- **OPEN, R59, AND IT IS THE FINDING OF THIS PASS (RN-833, 2026-08-02) - the hall's wall "ring" is twelve identically oriented boxes, and the walker falls out of the room in 81.1 per cent of azimuths.** The brief that sent me here stated the twelve segments "form an unbroken ring (4.536 m segments against a 4.341 m side, so they overlap at the corners)". They do not, and the shipped bytes say so. `walls.append(("col_HallWall%s" % ..., (0.30, HUB_RI * 0.56, CORR_CZ + 2.0), (c[0] * d, c[1] * d, ...)))` moves `loc` round the circle and never touches `size`, so all twelve are the SAME axis-aligned slab at twelve positions. Only A (0 deg) and G (180 deg) are tangential, and those are precisely the two I have just turned into doorways. D and J (90 / 270 deg) are 4.5 m RADIAL FINS pointing out of the room, reaching z = 10.518 past a hull whose outer radius is 8.40. The other eight are oblique. Measured at 180 azimuths off the shipped glb: 146 fall, worst unfloored run 10.2408 m at azimuth 88.0. TWO ROOT CAUSES AND THE SECOND IS THE HARD ONE: `of_lib.add_collision_box` never passes the `rot_z` that `MeshBuilder.box` supports, AND the runtime consumes every proxy as an axis-aligned bound anyway (`SpaceStation.learnStationProxies` reads `geometry.boundingBox` through the node matrix, and `Solid.boxes` are AABBs in the solid's frame), so a rotated chord could not survive the trip even if Blender authored one: a 30 deg chord arrives as a 2.42 x 4.08 m blob. THE COLLISION REPRESENTATION CANNOT EXPRESS THIS ROOM, so the fix is a rectilinear staircase and not a rotation. PRICED: holding the 0.276 m sagitta the twelve-gon was authored to needs 12 steps per quadrant, which is about 60 axis-aligned proxies for the hall alone against 63 for the entire station today, plus a `max_tris_collision` raise, plus it moves the input to `StationGravity.ts`'s per-deck volume derivation, which is another lane's. That is an Admin scheduling decision, so it is named here with the sizing attached rather than slipped into a render lane mid-task, and `check_station_deck.py` runs the measurement in a second.
- **OPEN, R60 (RN-833, 2026-08-02) - the four `col_GalleryFloor*` slabs already commit R59's sin in the opposite direction.** Each is a quadrant slab `(HUB_RI - MEZZ_RI, HUB_RI * 1.02, CEIL_PROXY_T)` placed on a diagonal, so its outer CORNER sits at radius 10.41 while the hall wall it is meant to be inside is at 8.10: there is standable proxy 2.3 m outside the drum at gallery height, with no mesh under it and no rail on the outboard side. Whoever closes R59 must decide the gallery in the same pass, because the two are approximating the same drum and a staircase wall with a square gallery poking through it is worse than either alone.

Owned by whoever owns `Registry.ts`; this lane cannot land it under a `web/src` freeze and will not ship dead geometry to fake it.
- **CLOSED (RN-311, 2026-08-01; fixed RN-1500/RN-1501, 2026-08-13 by `lane/art-foliage`) - the grass card carries no lateral silhouette, and the leaf card's base is cut away.** Both fixed: grass root half-width narrowed from 0.058..0.082 to 0.026..0.040 (root-row opacity 100% -> 68.6%, real gaps now exist), leaf given a root flare so the base row stops alpha-cutting into the ground. See RN-1500/RN-1501 in section 3 for the full measurement. **The original finding, unedited below for the record:** a subagent decoded `assets/textures/dist/of_grass_a.png` and found ZERO transparent columns: all 256 columns are one opaque run reaching the bottom row, so the "bundle of 11 blades" is a bottom-anchored MAT with a serrated top edge. Consequence: **any u band of any width returns the same 0.6009 opaque fraction**, so `GRASS_BAND_HALF_U` controls only the variance of a per-blade HEIGHT crop (sd 0.120 at the shipped 0.045, collapsing to 0.024 at 0.25) and widening it buys no extra visible blade. **The 0.045 is correct and was left alone**; the defect is `texgen._grass_strips`, which authors 11 blades on a 0.0455 half-pitch with 0.058 to 0.082 half-widths so the roots overlap. Separately, `of_leaf_a.png`'s bottom row is only 22.7 percent opaque, so every Leaf/LeafDry strip (`Detail_GrassCardC`, `Detail_BroadleafForb`, the sprig heads, `Beach_DuneGrass`) is alpha-cut at its base and roots into thin air. **NOT TAKEN because regenerating either PNG moves a shared generated artifact whose sha256 every textured contract carries**, and because a card's albedo is look-development's under ART-DIRECTION.md's sequencing rule. The mask's SHAPE is arguably geometry and arguably this lane's; Admin should say which.

Card A is the single most instanced mesh in the game (1,080,000/km2 after the scale), so this is worth a targeted look: the cheap candidates are `segs` 3 on card A (+6 triangles, ~+41,000 in the 45 m radius, which is why it was not done blind) or a stronger `kink` at unchanged `segs`. `Detail_SedgeRosette` likewise barely moved (0.577 to 0.584).

The IoU 0.745 to 0.580 fix, the 900 to 1000 file-total raise and the 1.00 x 1.00 to 1.14 x 0.86 footprint are therefore all real and all invisible. **Either give it a row or retire it**; it is currently paying BatchedMesh geometry slots at load for nothing, which is the same cost the RN-284 hand-off warned about for NEW stems.

Priced: `seg` 4 to 6 on the bush's nine masses is +72 triangles, which would take LOD0 from 270 to 342 against a 300 budget, so it is a contract raise and not a free change. The alternative that costs nothing is a third ring at the same `seg` (same +8 per mass). Deferred deliberately rather than guessed, because on `bush_scrub` it would buy a picture nobody can see (above) and on the mushroom caps it is 57 LOD0 instances.
- **CLOSED (RN-310, 2026-08-01) - the WG-13 rule was gated on ONE SIDE ONLY, and the rule itself is now retired.** Reid ruled: *"there should be no scenery trees. all trees should be minable."* There is one family, so there is nothing to separate; `assert_bare_trunk` is removed and no bare-trunk fraction is constrained anywhere. **The gate was right while the rule stood and it is recorded as such** (it caught the broadleaf pair 0.014 of height apart), and **the lesson survives its rule: a constraint that separates two families cannot be checked by measuring one of them.** What replaced it is the same measurement, printed and unasserted, plus a refusal on a canopy tree with NO foliage, which is a build defect rather than a design rule; negative control run (predicate inverted, refused by name on all three, reverted, glb byte-identical). **The consequence NOT taken: if every tree is minable, `props_canopy`'s three stop being scatter props and become harvest nodes. That is a Registry, world-gen and gameplay change and is Admin's to route.**

Mean pairwise silhouette IoU across yaw: pine 0.845 to 0.465, broadleaf 0.658 to 0.381, fir 0.822 to 0.617. **Authored variants were NOT shipped, and the reason is worth keeping: a new prop stem needs a row in `web/src/assets/Registry.ts`, and `PropLibrary.register` calls `addGeometry` for every stem it finds in a GLB whether or not any biome table references it, so an unreferenced stem costs BatchedMesh geometry slots and moves the `geometries` invariant other lanes measure, for zero visible benefit until the registry row lands.** If Admin wants a fourth and fifth canopy form, the ask is one `C('Canopy_<Name>', <density>)` line per stem in each biome table that should carry it (`Registry.ts:283-300`), and the builder work is then small.

Nothing stops the HARVEST trees drifting UP to meet it, and the broadleaf pair came within 0.014 of height of being indistinguishable during this pass with no check noticing. The clean fix is a floor AND a ceiling asserted from one table both build scripts read, or a `validate_glb` check driven by a contract field. `validate_glb.py` was not this pass's to edit.
- **OPEN (RN-274, 2026-08-01) - the canopy triangle raise is UNPRICED IN ENGINE.** props_canopy went 932 to 1996 file total, estimated at roughly +9 percent of Forest-site scene triangles (about +100,000, four draws on about 75 trees inside WG-17's 78 m radius). The arithmetic is in the commit; no frame was measured, because this pass ran without a browser. **The measurement owed is an A/B/A/B interleaved pair in ONE binary at the Forest site**, per INSTRUMENTS.md on timings while other lanes are building.
- **OPEN (RN-101 re-test, 2026-08-01) - the geometry-versus-texture split under the new target.** ART-DIRECTION.md asks for RN-101 to be re-tested now that leaf and grass cards have landed and measured essentially free at the Forest site (RN-183). **The geometric recommendation, stated without a frame measurement because none was possible this pass: keep GEOMETRY for the crown OUTLINE and move to CARDS for the crown INTERIOR.** RN-101 was right about the thing it measured, which is the silhouette: an alpha card's outline is its own rectangle until the alpha test cuts it, and RN-177 deliberately set coverage 0.665 ABOVE the 0.35 cutoff so far mips converge toward SOLID rather than eroding. That property is exactly what makes a card a poor silhouette and a good interior. Under the new target the two jobs separate: the crown EDGE is where "detail at every distance" lives and geometry is the only thing that can put a hole in a silhouette; the crown INTERIOR is where "no flat regions that resolve into nothing" lives and a card carries leaflet serration, midrib and translucency for zero triangles. Concretely: spend triangles on fewer, larger, better-shaped boughs and clumps at the crown's outer envelope, and spend cards on more and smaller foliage inside it, where overdraw is bounded because the clumps already occlude each other. **The cost re-measurement this recommendation is NOT allowed to assume is a fill-rate A/B at the Forest site with the interior card count raised, which RN-183 established the method for and which this pass could not run.**
