The file wants the batch bookkeeping split from the load/registration path, and that split should not happen while multiple lanes are live in it.
- **R1 (terrain Nanite, RESOLVED for Spike 1):** terrain uses **classic streamed meshes, not Nanite** (RN-5), world-gen already LODs and Nanite blocks the depth path. **Nanite cost on thousands of small *factory* meshes is the surviving open Nanite question** → now scoped as a named RC-8 Phase-1 residual (§5, item b): measure in the integrated factory-render co-validation, not Spike-3 (which is sim-only).
- **OWED DEBT (RN-61, 2026-07-28) - node scale does not carry the harvest reach.** `NodeField.build` now gives trees a per-instance size of 0.86 to 1.14, but `art.radiusM` (harvest reach) and `art.hitUpM` (hit point) in `NodeArt.ts` are per-KIND constants and do not scale with `pl.scale`. So a big tree and a small tree are chopped from the same distance and struck at the same height. The range was capped at +/-14% specifically to keep this under the aim tolerance rather than to hide it. **Any lane widening node scale must scale those two with it**, or the art change becomes a gameplay bug. Same applies to outcrops, whose `pl.scale` comes from deposit richness and can already exceed this range.
- **R5 (render-wall LOD-0 hot spot, from RC-8 §5), now the SOLE surviving render-wall residual; the *contract* half is closed headlessly.** The numeric render-cost model (factory-sim FS-14, `render_cost_tests`) confirms the suspect cost is **not** factory-sim's `GetLineItems` (a cheap flat read whose work is bounded to the Near0 lines, 180k item-evals for 300 near lines in the 100k stress scene) but **our** per-frame `pathUnitToWorld` evals + instance-transform writes for those ~50–180k discrete LOD-0 belt items, plus burst spikes when a camera cut promotes many lines to LOD-0 at once. The model proves the *count* that reaches us is bounded (Near0 lines × items/line, O(lines)), what it can't time is the **per-item build cost on real hardware**. Mitigation direction unchanged: screen-space-driven LOD-0 band kept tight (foreground bay only), amortized/budgeted line-promotion (spread instance builds across frames), LOD-0↔1 cross-fade to kill the discrete-items→scrolling-material pop. **Measured in the Phase-1 integrated co-validation (jointly owned with factory-sim).**
- **R2 (cross-fade, mitigation DESIGNED, pass/fail set):** scaled↔near pop + lighting mismatch on fast approach. Addressed structurally in spike1-rendering §2 (proxy-as-backdrop + occlusion-first cross-fade + single shared sun + depth-aware horizon haze). Retired by validation **RV3/RV8** (frame-stepped orbital-speed descent: no silhouette jump, no terminator discontinuity, no band-edge flicker). **Primary residual visual risk until the build runs.**
- **R4 (new, depth × Nanite):** Nanite can't take a custom per-pixel `SV_Depth` write → log-depth and Nanite-on-terrain partly incompatible. Resolved by RN-5 (classic terrain) + measuring reversed-Z-float-first (RN-2). Flagged to Admin as a standing UE5 constraint.
- **R3 (Admin Q3):** 1st vs 3rd person affects camera rig and near-field detail budget. Rig (spike1-rendering §1) is perspective-agnostic, NearCam parents the pawn either way; decision still pending gameplay.

LOD0 2564 -> 4256 tris and 7 -> 10 materials buy a deck poured in bays and edged in steel, a deluge header and a caged ladder in the trench, hold-downs that read as hydraulic machines, a T-0 umbilical mast (nothing connected the propellant tank to the vehicle before it), a cable network that terminates, and `SteelRust`/`SteelWorn` on the surfaces the plume and the traffic actually reach. **The pad was the only asset in the project at the full 4.0x marginal shadow multiplier** (LOD1 14090.06 mm, LOD2 14100.00 mm, both refused by every cascade, because LOD1 dropped `furniture()` and that is where the three 15.9 m lightning masts are); RN-1623's method takes LOD1 to **53.85 mm** and the multiplier to **2.0x**, which turns a 66 per cent geometry raise into a 22 per cent frame cost. **The trap, worth reading before the next proxy pass: `check_shadow_lod` scores BURIAL exactly as badly as omission** (a 0.10 m post 0.10 m inside a big block measures 100.00 mm), so a proxy must hug the feature's own section, and no box can bring a 12-gon of radius 1.50 under cascade 1 at all. Previously: RN-1675, RN-1676 used of the RN-1675 to RN-1689 block, `lane/shadow-proxies`: **THE TWO SHADOW-PROXY DEBTS RN-1623 NAMED, ONE CLOSED AND ONE MEASURED HONEST-NEGATIVE.** RN-1623 gave the reusable method (trace `of_lib.MeshBuilder._add` over an asset's own LOD0, block in every feature standing over one shadow texel proud of the coarser tier at its MEASURED envelope, nearest-surface metric) and left it owed on two fronts: the smelter's LOD1 stalled at 127.60 mm/3.0x, and the miner's LOD2 measured 619.07 mm and earned nothing. **THE SMELTER LOD1: 127.60 mm -> 52.80 mm, UNDER CASCADE 1 (56.25 mm) AND NOT ONLY CASCADE 2, cascades draw tiers 0,0,1 -> 0,1,1, marginal multiplier 3.0x -> 2.0x.** 27 LOD0 features were still proud past 56.25 mm (the stack's flared foot and cleanout it never had, the roof junction box, the hood's mounting brackets, the firebox coaming/hinges/latch/peep, both port throat plates, the louvre, the step tread, the ladder's own rungs, the service duct, the gauge cluster and hatch, the status bezel, four cable trays, the anchor pads, the body ribs), traced by instrumenting `MeshBuilder._add` with the actual source line and exact vertex bounds rather than eyeballing. **The one case that broke a single box, exactly as RN-1623 predicted:** the junction box's own four lid bolts sit deep inside the combined housing+plate+bolt envelope in every axis (RN-1623's junction-box-lid-bolts case again) and needed a second thin plate at their own layer. Two supplemental boxes (the intake/outlet throat plates, the body-rib slab) landed exactly on an existing part's own plane and were re-roled to match rather than moved, which is why `check_coplanar` is 0 same-facing pairs before and after (not merely unchanged: 8 were introduced mid-pass and traced out by cross-referencing each new box's own faces against the baseline's). LOD1 548 -> 872 triangles, `max_tris_total` 3000 -> 3300, argued in `contracts.json`; LOD0 (2276 tris), every socket and `col_Smelter` proven byte-identical by SHA-256 of the shipped mesh/node bytes, not argued from the build script. **RN-1676, THE MINER LOD2: MEASURED AND REVERTED, AN HONEST NEGATIVE ON RN-1599's OWN PRECEDENT.** The same traced method against LOD2's 210.94 mm cascade-2 texel found the detail is not concentrated but spread over the WHOLE machine: 29 independent LOD0 features (duct, gantry slab and columns, drill guide and its guard cage, two full-footprint rings, four port-mouth bands, canopy, service face, motor detail, standing detail, hose, wet-steel band) each exceed 210.94 mm alone. Blocking in the worst ten (36 -> 156 triangles) still measured 325.00 mm; blocking in all 29 (36 -> 336 triangles, 58% of LOD1's own 576) reached 199.00 mm - technically under the texel, on a 12 mm/5.6% margin, and it does not move the marginal multiplier at all (cascade 0 already requires LOD0 regardless of LOD2, so the miner is 2.0x either way per RN-1623); the only purchase is swapping cascade 2's own draw from LOD1 (576) to LOD2 (336) on a tier whose entire point is to be materially cheaper than LOD1 rather than 58 per cent of it. Not shipped; `miner.glb` is byte-for-byte unchanged, the attempt and its numbers are recorded in `build_miner.py`'s `build_lod2` docstring and `contracts.json` so the next lane does not re-measure the same 29 features. `check_shadow_lod`, `check_coplanar`, `check:roles`, `check:proxies`, `validate_glb --all` (56/56), `tsc` and `vite build` all green. No Cycles receipt owed (both tiers touched are invisible shadow/silhouette LODs, no visible form changed) and no browser look probe owed (same reason); both stated explicitly rather than skipped silently. Blender-only pass, CPU rasterisation, one instance at a time, no browser opened.)

First pass: **RN-1415's NULL IS EXPLAINED AND THE EXPLANATION IS THAT THE ENVIRONMENT MAP CONTAINS NO BRIGHT SOURCE AT ALL.** Read at a 256 cube through the new `OFRenderer.cubeRadiance` seam, before PMREM and before ACES: mean 0.1399, max 1.1178, `peakRatio` 7.99, `brightFrac` 0.0000 of 393,216 texels. Previous entry: RN-1422, `lane/ruin-maps`: **THE GAP RN-1421 NAMED AND DID NOT CLOSE, NOW CLOSED.** RN-1421's own D-016 consumer verification found, in passing, that `RuinSites.ts` draws the ruin through `loadGlb` + `selectLod` and never calls `attachSurface`, so the storyline's first destination (RN-1450's asset, the structure high-water mark) shipped with NONE of the five DW-35 surface slots wired: no albedo, no normal, no ORM. `RuinSites.ts`'s `spawn()` now traverses the cloned template exactly once per placement (guarded by a `surfaced: Set<THREE.Material>` field, because `clone(true)` SHARES the material across every instance the way `PlayerRig.ts`'s own dedup set exists to catch) and calls `attachSurface(mat, familyForMaterial(mat), 'ruin:'+mat.name)` per unique material. > `lane/a1-image`, `uStrength`/`aoRadiusM`/`aoPower`) already closed two thirds

> 32% darker than bare (part hypothesised as cover-colour-under-canopy, part
> AO), and a near-field AO excess on meadowfield's r4 rung five times the
> mid-field's. Post files only (`AoGlsl.ts`, `PostConfig.ts`, `PostDefaults.ts`,
> `PostStack.ts`, plus `run.mjs`'s flag whitelist). Frames:
> `docs/screenshots/RN2190_{forestfloor,meadow}_{before,after}.png`.

### 2.12.1 THE CAUSE SPLIT ON FORESTFLOOR, AND THE HYPOTHESIS THAT DID NOT SURVIVE

One-flag controls, one build, `forestfloor` `box`, real capture:

| arm | luma |
|---|---|
| bare, AO+contact on | 28.93 |
| bare, AO+contact off | 32.75 |
| carpet, AO+contact on (pre-lane) | 19.79 |
| carpet, AO off, contact on | 27.32 |
| carpet, AO+contact off | 35.51 |
| carpet, AO+contact on, `?grasstint=0` | 19.4 |

The carpet reads **31.6% darker than bare** with everything on (the cited "32
per cent"). Turning AO off alone closes about half of it (31.6% -> 16.6%);
turning contact shadows off too closes most of the rest (16.6% -> 6.6%). **The
colour hypothesis did not survive contact with `?grasstint=0`**: pinning every
blade to the exact substrate colour (no green rotation at all) moved the box
from 19.79 to 19.4, under 1%, statistically noise. `GrassPalette.coverAlbedo`
renormalises to the substrate's own luminance BY CONSTRUCTION (RN-2145 section
2.11.1), so this null result is the design working as documented, not a
surprise.

**So the split is: roughly half AO, a bit less than half contact shadow, and a
genuine 6.6% residual that is NEITHER AO NOR COLOUR.** `GrassGlsl.ts`'s lighting
expression is "the same lighting expression the ground uses" by RN-2145's own
rule, but it is evaluated against the BLADE's normal, and an upright card
catches less of a near-zenith sun (`ndl = dot(n, sd)`) than the flat terrain
plane it stands on does. That is a real geometric/lighting difference between
carpet and terrain, not a palette defect, and it is **not routed to A3's
palette or A5's assets as RN-2190 anticipated** -- it belongs to A2's own grass
shading, which this wave does not touch (`grass/` is off limits for this lane).
Recorded here rather than fixed; the contact-shadow finding (a screen-space term
comparable in size to AO, previously never separately measured on the carpet)
is new and is Admin's to scope into a future block if it is worth a lane of its
own.

### 2.12.2 THE AO TUNE, AND THE APPROACH THAT MEASURED BACKWARDS

**A distance-invariant edge signal.** `AoGlsl.ts`'s `normalAndEdgeFromDepth`
(renamed from `normalFromDepth`) returns, in `.w`, the mean absolute view-space
depth deviation of the four full-res neighbours already sampled to build the AO
normal -- zero extra texture reads. A blade silhouette a texel wide puts one or
two of those taps past the blade onto whatever is behind it, tens of
centimetres to metres away; a solid surface's four taps stay on the same sheet.
`thin = clamp(edge / aoThinEdgeM, 0, 1)`, `aoThinEdgeM = 0.05` m.

**FIRST ATTEMPT, SHRINKING THE SEARCH RADIUS BY `thin`, MEASURED BACKWARDS.**
`OF_AO_STEPS` is a fixed count spread across `[0, radiusUV]`; shrinking
`radiusUV` on a thin pixel does not exclude the near occluder that makes it
thin, it resamples the SAME close region at higher density and finds that
occluder's true horizon angle more precisely than the coarser full-radius
search did. Measured, one flag apart: meadowfield r4 read **69.73 with the
shrunk radius against 72.16 with the term off entirely** -- DARKER, the wrong
sign, confirmed on forestfloor's box too (19.52 against 19.79). Rejected and
kept in the shader as a comment, because the failure mode is reusable: a
fixed-sample-count search cannot be narrowed to mean "ignore this region", only
"resample this region more finely".

**THE FIX THAT SHIPPED: damp the RESULT, not the search.** `ao = mix(raw, 1.0,
thin * aoThinAmount)`, applied after the horizon integral. No coupling to
sample density.

**THE DISTANCE GATE, AND THE ROW IT ACTUALLY PROTECTS.** meadowfield's own
`box` rectangle inverts to about **5.7 m** (not the mid-field -- do not confuse
it with the unrelated `midfield` shot's 27 m strip of the same field name), so
`box` and the `r4` rung (4 m) are nearly the same range and get the SAME
treatment from an edge-magnitude signal that does not know distance.
`aoThinNearM`/`aoThinFarM` (8 m / 22 m) instead protect the FAR field: with the
gate disabled (`?aothinnear=0&aothinfar=0.02`), `box` and `r4` reproduce the
`?aothin=0` control to the digit (90.16, 72.16), the positive proof the gate
does nothing until asked. At the shipped 8/22, r25 and r55 (inside the
carpet's own fade zone) move by about 2-3 counts (~2%) against their own
`?aothin=0` reading rather than by zero, because the row is 5 px tall and its
far edge dips inside 22 m at this pose's range compression; disclosed rather
than chased further.

**`aoThinAmount` = 0.35, chosen because `box` and `r4` disagreed on what the
right number was.** meadowfield, `?aothin=0` (pre-lane) against a bare control:

| rung | carpet (pre-lane) | bare | excess |
|---|---|---|---|
| box (~5.7 m) | 15.8% | 16.2% | already closed |
| r4 (4 m) | 20.7% | 15.1% | 5.6 points |

`box` had effectively no defect before this lane touched anything; `r4` did.
One amount cannot fix `r4` without moving `box`, because they are almost the
same range. At `aoThinAmount = 0.6`, r4 lands at 13.9% (good, 1.2 points inside
bare) but `box` is driven to 9.3%, **6.9 points UNDER its own bare reading** --
a bigger new error than the one being fixed. At 0.35, r4 lands at 16.7% (1.6
points over bare, an honest partial fix) and `box` at 12.0% (4.2 points under,
smaller than 0.6's overshoot). 0.35 is the point where neither rectangle's new
error exceeds the other's old one. A rectangle-specific fix for `box` is future
work and is not this default.

### 2.12.3 THE TWO HERO JUDGEMENTS

**`meadow` (A1's hero pose, yaw 120 / pitch -8):** `box` 74.69 -> 78.29 (+4.8%),
`nearG` 68.44 -> 72.12 (+5.4%), `shade` (the understorey shadow patch) 77.8 ->
80.88 (+4.0%). Looking at the pair rather than the numbers: the gaps between
blades at the player's own feet read a shade less black, a small, honest lift
rather than a rescue -- this lane's own charter named it a residual, not the
original defect, and it reads like one. The frame is still, correctly, a dense
green field rather than a lit one; nothing here was asked to fix the khaki
horizon band or the flat mid-field, which are other lanes' subjects.

**`forestfloor` (canopy shade, no direct sun):** `box` 19.79 -> 20.53 (+3.7%).
The pair looks close to identical at a glance, and the number says why: this
lane's mechanism only owns the AO half of section 2.12.1's split, and AO's own
share of forestfloor's darkening is a smaller fraction of the total than on
open ground (canopy shade already suppresses the sun term this shader's
`ndl * shadow` needs to read bright). The floor is still dark and still reads
as litter in shadow, which is correct: it is canopy shade, not a bug, and nothing
in this pass was asked to relight it. What DID move is honestly small, and the
frame does not oversell it: no rescue, no "alive" green where the scene is
genuinely unlit.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `vite build` clean. Determinism:

### 2.12.6 OWED

- **Contact shadows are a comparable-sized, previously unmeasured contributor**
  to the carpet's own darkening (2.12.1). Nobody has chartered a lane to look

- **The 6.6% forestfloor residual is a lighting-geometry parity gap between
  upright blade normals and the flat terrain plane**, not cover colour. A2's

  measured limit of a single distance-invariant amount trying to serve two
  rectangles at nearly the same range with different underlying defects. A
  material-level exclusion (grass pixels masked out of AO sampling entirely)
  was named as an option in the brief and not attempted: the AO pass is
  depth-only by design (`AoGlsl.ts`'s own header, "WHY DEPTH ALONE") and has no

## 2.13 THE CARPET SHADING RESIDUALS: THE BLADE-NORMAL BEND AND THE CONTACT-SHADOW SHARE (RN-2220 to RN-2224, 2026-08-20, `lane/carpet-shading`)

Two items, two commits, routed by section 2.12.6's own OWED list: the 6.6%
forestfloor residual (a lighting-geometry parity gap, not colour) and contact
shadows as a comparable-sized, previously unmeasured contributor to the
carpet's own darkening.

### 2.13.1 ITEM (b): THE BLADE-NORMAL BEND

`GrassGlsl.ts` shades the carpet with "the same lighting expression the ground
uses" (its own header), which implicitly assumes an up-facing normal because
that is what flat ground has. `GrassCard.ts`'s own `BEND_UP` (0.74) already
bends the GEOMETRIC normal toward up at construction, but for a different
reason (a tuft's own lit side, so a field of randomly-yawed cards does not read
as salt-and-pepper) and it still leaves an upright card taking measurably less
near-zenith `ndl` than the flat plane it stands on. This lane adds a SECOND,
independent blend in the fragment shader: `vec3 ns = normalize(mix(n, up,
uBendUp));`, spent only on `ndl` and `skyView`, the two terms that stand in for
the ground's own diffuse response. The wrap/forward translucency term (why a
real meadow glows into a low sun) stays on the unbent `n`, because that is the
facet's own thin-tissue read and bending it too would flatten the per-blade
variation that lets the wind shimmer read.

`uBendUp = 0.7` (`GrassMaterial.ts`), inside the 0.6-0.8 range named in the
brief, picked by the forestfloor number and by eye on the meadow pose.
`?grassbend=0` is the exact pre-RN-2220 control (mix identity) and reproduces
RN-2190's own recorded numbers to the digit, which is itself a strong
determinism check: forestfloor AO+contact-off box 35.51, shipped forestfloor
box 20.53, meadow box/`nearG`/`shade` 78.29/72.12/80.88.

**THE RESIDUAL, MEASURED.** Forestfloor, AO+contact off (isolating the residual
exactly as section 2.12.1 did), one build, one flag apart, fresh process: bare
38.02, carpet before 35.51 (6.60% gap -- the cited "6.6 per cent" to the
digit), carpet after 36.43 (4.18% gap). This closes a little over a third of
the residual, and MORE BEND DOES NOT CLOSE MUCH MORE OF IT: `?grassbend=1`
(full bend, `ns` becomes exactly `up`) reaches 36.57, a 3.81% gap, which is
this mechanism's own ceiling. THE REASON IS IN THE SHADING MATH, not a tuning
shortfall: `skyAmb` already reads from `up`, not `n` (`ofAtmoScatter(pM, up,
...)`), and `GrassCard`'s own geometric `BEND_UP` already holds `dot(n, up)`
in the 0.79-0.94 range before this lane touches anything, so `skyView` (the
only other `n`-dependent ambient term) was already close to 1 pre-lane. What
is left, closable by THIS mechanism, is small by construction. The remaining
~3.8-4.2% gap is disclosed rather than chased: a plausible cause is the
cascade-shadow term (`ofCascadeShadow(vViewZ)`) sampling a slightly different
texel for a blade card standing tens of centimetres above the ground it
replaces, which is a genuinely different subject (shadow-map self-consistency
between a card and its substrate, not blade-normal shading) and is future work,
not this lane's.

**SHIPPED SETTINGS.** Forestfloor box 20.53 -> 21.24 (+3.5%). Meadow box 78.29
-> 81.98 (+4.7%), `nearG` 72.12 -> 75.55 (+4.8%), `shade` 80.88 -> 84.9 (+5.0%).

### 2.13.2 ITEM (a): CONTACT SHADOWS, MEASURED THEN TUNED

**THE SHARE, MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS TOUCHED.** One-flag `?contact` pairs,
real capture, fresh process. Forestfloor's own box: contact off 27.35, on
21.24, a 22.3% share; a BARE control (`?grass=0`) at the same pose reads 33.41
off, 29.21 on, a 12.6% share -- a 9.8-point excess, comparable in size to the
AO share RN-2190 measured and never separately isolated before this lane.
Meadowfield's `rangeRects` found the IDENTICAL SHAPE RN-2190 found for AO: the
excess lives at the near rung and is gone by the next one out. `r4` (4 m):
carpet 16.8% share against a 12.6% bare share (a 4.2-point excess). `r10`
(10 m): carpet ALREADY READS UNDER its own bare share (8.0% against 14.2%),
before this lane's fix even runs -- the far rung's own geometry (a broad,
mostly-solid turf card, not a thin blade) simply does not cast/receive contact
shadows the way the near tufts or bare ground do.

**THE TUNE REUSES AoGlsl's THIN-GEOMETRY PATTERN, NOT ITS NUMBERS.**
`ContactGlsl.ts`'s `normalFromDepth` is renamed `normalAndEdgeFromDepth` and
now returns, in `.w`, the same mean absolute view-space depth deviation of its
four depth taps that AoGlsl's does -- zero extra fetches, same construction,
same reason (a grass-blade silhouette a texel wide puts one or two taps past
the blade onto whatever is behind it). The march's final `occl` is damped by
it (`occl *= 1.0 - thin * uThinAmount`), not the march itself, for AoGlsl's own
stated reason: a fixed step count does not couple to this signal the way a
search radius would, so there is no "measured backwards" trap to repeat here,
but damping the result is still the minimal, march-independent change.
`csThinEdgeM` (0.05) and `csThinAmount` are the pass's OWN tunables with the
pass's OWN default, sharing no uniform with AoGlsl's `aoThinEdgeM`/`aoThinAmount`
(which this lane does not retune, per the brief).

**AN UNGATED DAMP REPRODUCES AO's OWN r4-vs-box CONFLICT, MEASURED RATHER THAN
ASSUMED FROM THE PRECEDENT ALONE.** At `csThinAmount=0.35` with no distance
gate, `r4`'s excess closes (16.80% -> 13.65% share, 1.02 points over bare) but
`box`/`r10`/`r25`/`r55` -- already running UNDER their own bare share before
this term touched anything -- are pushed FURTHER under it, by more than their
own pre-existing deficit (`box`: 2.37-point deficit before, 4.99 after, a
bigger new error than the one being fixed; `r10` deficit 6.21 -> 8.72; `r25`
3.90 -> 4.95; `r55` 2.03 -> 2.44). This is AO's own selection conflict
(section 2.12.2) reproduced by direct measurement on a different pass.

**THE GATE IS NARROWER THAN AO's BECAUSE THE CONFLICT IS TIGHTER.** AO's own
`aoThinNearM`/`FarM` (8/22) never had to separate `r4` (4 m) from `box`
(inverts to ~5.7 m, section 2.12.2's own note) -- both sit well inside 8 m and
get the same (compromise) treatment. Contact's own conflict is different in
KIND: `r10` (10 m) is already worse than baseline even before `box` is
considered, so the gate has to protect the far side much closer in. At
`csThinNearM/FarM = 5/9` (AO's own proportions, scaled down), `r4` closes to
13.65% (1.02 points over bare) and `r10`/`r25`/`r55` are correctly restored to
their un-thinned readings (109.2 against a 109.13 baseline, etc.) -- but `box`
still moves, because `box`'s own ~5.7 m sits inside the 5-9 m transition band,
and its deficit (13.62% bare vs 8.63% shipped, a 4.99-point new error) still
EXCEEDS its own 2.37-point pre-existing one. Narrowed further to `4/5` --
tight enough that most of `box`'s own range sits outside the gate entirely --
`r4` still closes to 13.82% (1.19 points over bare, closing 71% of its
excess) and `box`'s new deficit (2.54 points, 13.62% bare vs 11.08% shipped)
no longer exceeds its old one (2.37), the SAME criterion AO's own
`aoThinAmount` was chosen by ("neither rectangle's new error exceeds the
other's old one"). Forestfloor's own box is unaffected by the narrower gate:
21.85 identical at 5/9 and at 4/5, because its eye-to-ground range never
reaches 4 m in the first place.

**SHIPPED: `csThinEdgeM=0.05`, `csThinAmount=0.35`, `csThinNearM=4`,
`csThinFarM=5`.**

### 2.13.3 THE SOLID-SHADOW CONTROL

Contact shadows on SOLID objects must not weaken, and the risk is real: a
solid prop's own silhouette against the ground is ALSO a depth-edge, and the
same edge-density signal that targets grass could in principle catch it too.
Measured rather than assumed. `tools/smoke/probes/rn2220_propcheck.js`
reproduces `propshadow.js`'s own pose (a real shadow caster, a
`Forest_FallenLog`, ahead of the camera); a hand-picked rectangle on the log's
own ground-contact shadow reads 23.753 (`?csthin=0`, the exact pre-lane
control) against 23.781 shipped -- noise-level, NOT weaker
(`docs/screenshots/RN2220_propshadow_before.png` /
`RN2220_propshadow_after.png`). The `machine` shot's `box`/`hearthL`/`hearthR`
rectangles (solid architecture, no grass in frame) are bit-identical to the
counts printed: 23.53/23.54, 24.67/24.67, 21.52/21.54. The reason this holds is
the same one AoGlsl's own header gives for solid AO: the BULK of a shadow sits
on continuous ground depth (edge magnitude near zero, `thin` near zero), and
only a texel-wide rim at the object's own silhouette could be affected at all.

## 2.14 THE AERIAL TREE SOURCE (RN-2225 to RN-2234, 2026-08-20, `lane/aerial-trees`)

`lane/aerial-trees`, base `origin/main` at 7c92931e. **All ten numbers used.**
Frames `docs/screenshots/RN2225_*`. Served from a `vite preview` this lane
owned on `127.0.0.1:5297`, `--strictPort`, sentinel `dist/of-sentinel-rn2225
.txt` written into this worktree's own dist and fetched back over the port
before every probe run, ownership confirmed by `Get-NetTCPConnection
-LocalPort 5297` (PID 34728), killed by that PID. Real Windows D3D11 (ANGLE),
RTX 4060 Ti, 1600x900. `web/wasm/dist` and `test/expected.json` untouched.

This closes section 6's RN-2225 row, all three of its items, and it found two
more on the way.

### 2.14.1 The tick, and the walk identity that is the whole regression argument

`--scenario=surface` builds no `Gameplay` (`BootGameplay:80` gates on
`player !== null && cfg.gameplay`), so `TreeField` was never CONSTRUCTED, let
alone ticked. The same defect wears a second costume in the shipped game: board
a rocket and `ViewRouter` hands the eye to the vessel while the capsule freezes
at the pad, so the rock and tree rings stay pinned to the launch site and the
whole climb is over bare ground.

One rule, two halves. **`GameplayDeps.vegOrigin`** replaces the direct
`d.player.body.feet` read at `GameplayFrame:31` and is
`router.onFoot ? player.body.feet : router.position` -- ON FOOT IT IS THE SAME
OBJECT, which is why a walk scenario reads a byte-identical point through a new
name. One `router.onFoot` test rather than a flight-status test, because the
router IS the authority on which source is the streaming observer (W9), and
asking anything else is a second opinion that can disagree with the terrain.
**`VegetationScope`** (dynamically imported, on `BootGameplay`'s own standing-
rule-7 precedent) is the second caller of the new
`VegetationFields.makeVegetationFields`, which is the ONE authority for the four
player-free objects `composeGround` used to construct inline. Its boot gate is
the exact NEGATION of `BootGameplay`'s, so the two can never both build a tree
field or both skip one.

The rings take an altitude ceiling, `ScatterTuning.VEG_ORIGIN_MAX_ALT_M` =
12,000 m, owned by `RockField.update` and `TreeField.update` themselves so the
rule has one home. Derived: 12 m median tree at 1,086 px per radian is one
pixel at 13,032 m, rounded DOWN to the `ascent` scenario's own altitude so the
one scenario that straddles the cutoff sits on the cheap side. Growth stops;
nothing placed is dropped and `NodeField` keeps picking rungs, which is why
`vegOrigin` returns a point rather than null.

**THE WALK PROOF, quoted.** `walkdet` (`--scenario=walk --sandbox=1`) is
byte-identical across two fresh processes on this build, and byte-identical
again between the shipped arm and `?canopy=0`: 989 ticks, six marks, eye and
feet to six decimals. `forestfloor` at `?canopy=0` reads **1,272,522
triangles**, which is A5's own recorded shipped number TO THE DIGIT, so nothing
outside the canopy tier moved in the walk path.

**AND THE TICK ALONE WAS WORTH ZERO PIXELS, which is the finding.** With the
tick landed and the canopy still off, the flyover reads **188,081 triangles,
box 125.03, skyBand 149.03, hzBand 190.65, under 108.99, shadowStep 111.02** --
identical to the pre-lane frame in every field, with **683 harvest trees and 20
rocks standing in the world** (`of.report().wild`, delivery 0.9768). They were
placed and they were OFF SCREEN. At 1,200 m with a 60 degree vertical fov and
pitch -14 the frame spans depression -16 to +44 degrees, so its ground runs from
`1200/tan(44)` = **1,243 m** out to a **37,966 m** horizon with the centre at
`1200/tan(14)` = **4,813 m**, and the harvest ring's outermost possible edge is
690 m. The whole ring sits below the bottom edge of the frame.

### 2.14.2 The reach, and the radius that was not a radius

**THE GATES WERE 3-D EYE DISTANCES COMPARED AGAINST RADII THAT MEAN GROUND.** A
radius R at altitude h covers a ground disc of `sqrt(R^2 - h^2)`, and at the
flyover's 620 m canopy over a 1,200 m eye that is not a real number: the tier
was off, everywhere, from the air, **silently**, because every cell it would
have reported on failed the gate before it was counted. `Scatter.groundDistM`
converts, applied to the CANOPY gates only -- the chunk residency test, the
per-cell `maxR2`, `canopyDistanceWeight` and the rebuild bands. The ground
tiers keep the 3-D distance deliberately: they live inside 170 m of a 2 m eye
where the correction is **12 mm at the ring's edge**, big enough to flip a cell
sitting exactly on the boundary and worth nothing, and spending the whole
standing-eye bit-identity claim on a millimetre is a bad trade. `?canopy=0`
therefore takes the identical arithmetic and reproduces the pre-lane frame to
the digit (above).

**THE CELL BUDGET.** `MAX_CELL_M` = 64 is the ground tiers' limit and is
UNTOUCHED; the canopy gets its own, `CANOPY_MAX_CELL_M` = 128, read by the
canopy branch alone. On Forge (R = 6e5 m) a face root quad is `pi*R/2` =
942,478 m, a depth-k quad is that over `2^k` and its cell is a thirty-second of
the quad, so 64 m is depth 9 (1,841 m quad, 57.5 m cell) and 128 m is depth 8
(3,681 m, 115.0 m). The streamer splits while `quadEdge / observerDist >
splitRatio` (1.4, `Config.ts:168`), so depth 8 is the finest band out to
`3681/1.4` = 2,630 m of eye distance and depth 7 (230 m cells) takes over past
5,259 m -- which is where `CANOPY_MAX_RADIUS_M` = 5,200 clamps, so a ring can
never be asked for ground it will silently refuse to grow on. Depth 7 is
refused for a reason and not for tidiness: a prop is placed by bilinear
interpolation inside one mesh cell, so the cell size IS the tree's positional
quantisation, and 230 m of it puts a stand on the wrong side of a valley.

Realised at the flyover: **16 chunks scattered, 3 refused, 22,940 canopy trees
over 62.7 km2** (366 per km2 against Hills' 1,200 ask, the difference being the
stand field, the treeline and the distance gradient), **91,760 instances**,
backlog 0, `chunksCapped` 0, `cellsCapped` 0, pool `exhausted` 0 and `refused`
0 against a 32,768 per-material cap.

**THE RUNG'S OWN COST, separated by `?canopy=0`:** 188,081 -> **312,601**
triangles, **+124,520 for 22,940 trees**, i.e. 5.4 triangles per tree per
frame after per-instance culling, against the 12-triangle `_LOD3` card the
asset ships (`contracts.json`: Pine 742/50/12, Fir 334/28/12, Broadleaf
784/58/12). Every canopy tree draws its impostor at every range this tier
exists at, because `CANOPY_NEAR_M` (550 m) is past `CANOPY_LOD3_M` (420 m):
**RN-2202's rung now carries the entire far forest and its LOD0 and LOD2 rungs
are unreachable from the canopy tier.**

**THE STANDING-EYE IDENTITY, AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS PARAGRAPH WAS
MEASURED OFF THE WRONG ARM.** The structural half is sound: at a 2 m eye no
chunk inside the ground tiers' own 170 m ring is near either cell limit (depth
12, 7.2 m cells), the canopy fade is exactly zero inside 550 m, and
`canopyStepOf` returns 0 there, so the near band integer is the shipped 0..3
unchanged. **The measured half was not.** The row quoted `propsPlaced` 41,300
and `deliveredFraction` 1.0002 as holding in BOTH arms. Those are the
`?canopyshade=0` numbers. The true pair, forestfloor, one flag apart, fresh
process each:

| | `?canopy=0` | shipped (shade on) |
|---|---|---|
| `propsPlaced` | **41,300** | **25,391** |
| `wantedPerM2` | 0.4617 | 0.28366 |
| `placedPerM2` | 0.46181 | 0.28392 |
| `deliveredFraction` | 1.0002 | 1.0009 |
| `cellsScattered` | 25,655 | 25,655 |
| `cellsCapped` / `chunksCapped` | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

**The understorey was thinned by 38.5 per cent** (15,909 props of 41,300; the
ASK itself falls 38.6 per cent, and with both delivery ratios at 1.00 and
nothing capped it is the density and not a ceiling). The cells are identical, so
"the same cells are resident" was true and was not the claim that mattered. The
cause is `CANOPY_SHADE`, which section 2.14.8 had disclosed only as a 0.83-count
luma move on one meadow rectangle -- **the largest single change this lane made
to the ground a player walks on, riding in under an identity claim.** The
lane's verifier caught it; it is corrected here rather than argued, on the
NUMBERS.md rule this file's own catalogue exists for.

**WITH `canopyShade` NOW DEFAULT OFF (2.14.7b), the identity claim is true as
originally written and is re-measured:** forestfloor `?canopy=0` 41,300 /
0.4617 / 1.0002 / box 22.82 and the shipped arm **41,300 / 0.4617 / 1.0002 /
box 22.82**, every ground-cover counter and the box identical to the digit;
meadow `?canopy=0` 52,139 / 0.51782 / box 85.59 / nearG 80.58 and shipped
**52,139 / 0.51782 / box 85.59 / nearG 80.58**, likewise. The canopy's counters
are separate from the ground cover's, which is exactly why RN-15 separated
them.

### 2.14.3 `canopyRadiusM`: a real default, and it does not contradict WG-116

**Decision: the tier is ON by default and it is the FAR tier only.** WG-116
retired it to 0 and that was right for what it then was -- a scenery ring from
0 to 620 m standing exactly where `TreeField`'s minable trees stand, which
Reid's "there should be no scenery trees, all trees should be minable" refuses
outright. It is not that any more. `CANOPY_NEAR_M` = `TREE_RADIUS_M -
TREE_EDGE_WANDER_M` = 550 m holds it out of the whole harvest ring and
`CANOPY_NEAR_FULL_M` = 690 m is where it reaches full density, so **every tree
a player can reach is still a node they can chop** and what the tier draws is
the ground BETWEEN the harvest ring's edge and the terrain material's own far
tier. That is the horizon treeline `CANOPY_RADIUS_M`'s own docstring asked
rendering for in as many words ("a horizon treeline needs a far-field impostor
layer, and this client has none") and that RN-2202's rung was built to carry.

The crossfade band IS the wander band, which makes it the statistical
complement of the harvest ring's own ragged edge: `TreeField` displaces its
membership radius by a smooth field over +/-70 m, so expected harvest coverage
falls from 1 at 550 m to 0 at 690 m, which is the canopy's ramp read backwards.
Total tree density across the seam is about constant. `TREE_RADIUS_M` and
`TREE_EDGE_WANDER_M` MOVED to `ScatterTuning` and are re-exported from
`TreeTuning` unchanged, for the reason that file's own header gives about the
treeline: a boundary owned by two files is a boundary that drifts.

**Disclosed, not hidden:** the two lattices are different, so walking through
the 550-690 m band re-shuffles which trees exist. At 620 m a 12 m tree is 21
pixels tall. Above `VEG_ORIGIN_MAX_ALT_M` there is no harvest ring to
complement and the 690 m hole under the eye stays empty; from 12 km that is 3.3
degrees of frame and it is accepted rather than special-cased, because a canopy
whose existence depended on the observer is the one thing `canopyWeight`'s own
comment says a forest must never be.

### 2.14.4 Two instrument defects the wider reach exposed, neither visible at 170 m

**A REFUSED CHUNK WAS RE-OFFERED FOR EVER.** `Scatter.build` has two early
returns that record nothing -- a biome with no prop table, and a mesh cell
coarser than the limit -- so a refused chunk took the whole
`BUILDS_PER_UPDATE` budget of ONE every frame and left everything behind it in
the backlog permanently. It is the identical defect the `placed.set` at the foot
of `build` already carries a paragraph about, in the two paths that paragraph
did not cover, and it was invisible while the ring was 170 m because two or
three chunks drain anyway. Fixed with a `barren` set, counted as
`chunksRefused` (3 at the flyover).

**THE SETTLE GATE COULD NOT SEE THE SCATTER.** `loop.settleGate` asked only
whether the TERRAIN had converged. Converged terrain says every chunk has
ARRIVED and says nothing about whether anything has been grown on it. The first
flyover taken with the far tier on was captured with **5 chunks scattered and 13
queued** -- 28 per cent of a forest -- and reported as a settled frame, with
`scatterBacklog` sitting on the same page and nothing reading it. The gate now
also requires `scatterBacklog === 0`. **This is a NUMBERS.md-class defect and it
would have contaminated every future far-field measurement**, so it is the most
transferable thing in this lane.

### 2.14.5 Aerial perspective on the props, which the picture found and no counter could

`RN2225_flyover_nohaze.png` is the far canopy switched on with the terrain's
haze under it and none on the trees. The ground at 3 km is washed to a flat pale
green by the air; the trees standing ON it are drawn at full contrast, so every
one is a hard dark speck and the frame reads as **dirt on the lens**. The
`under` rectangle moved 108.99 -> 108.63, four tenths of a count, and would have
signed it off. This is DW-7 exactly.

`PropSkyAmbient` takes a third anchor. The SAME TWO CALLS the terrain makes
(`TerrainFragLight.glsl.ts:198-210`), in the same order with the same
arguments, from the same shared uniform objects, so a tree and the ground it
stands on are hazed by one function rather than by two that can disagree. On
`<fog_fragment>` and NOT on `irradiance`, because aerial perspective is a
transmittance on what LEAVES the surface: folded into the incoming light it
reddens a tree instead of fading it, and those are not the same picture. Three's
own fog is neither read nor collided with (`#ifdef USE_FOG` guards its body) and
must never be used here -- a second haze authority is the DW-26 failure over the
exact term A4 spent a lane calibrating. `OF_AP_VIEW`/`OF_AP_LIGHT` are
`TerrainProgram` defines a stock program does not have, so the two step counts
are transcribed as the literals 4 and 2 and the transcription is named in the
file. `?prophaze=0` is the value control; the third anchor gets its own miss row
so a three upgrade that renames the fog chunk reports a lost haze.

### 2.14.6 The canopy does not cast, and it is a theorem

`CANOPY_NEAR_M` is 550 m and `ShadowRig`'s furthest cascade split is 300 m, so
**no canopy instance is ever inside any cascade, ever**. `PropLibrary` gives the
canopy atlas its own batch key (`CANOPY_SUFFIX`, on `DETAIL_SUFFIX`'s precedent
and argument) with `castShadow = false`, and `BootBodyScope` ASSERTS the
inequality at boot rather than trusting it, because it is two numbers in two
files and the failure mode -- a missing tree shadow -- is invisible in every
aggregate.

Why it mattered: `attachFarShadowSkip` hides the impostor rung per INSTANCE per
CASCADE per FRAME, which is right at the scale it was built for and is a
`getGeometryIdAt` plus a `setVisibleAt` plus a draw-list rebuild over **91,760
instances three times a frame** at this one. **Flyover, one build, one commit
apart: p50 21.4 -> 7.4 ms, near pass 21.4 -> 6.5 ms, calls 41 -> 29, and every
measured rectangle reproduces to the digit** -- box 125.08, hzBand 190.65,
under 108.85, shadowStep 111.15 in both arms.

**THE PIXEL CLAIM IS SOFTENED TO ITS OWN NOISE FLOOR, because "identical to the
digit" was written of the RECTANGLES and read as if it were written of the
FRAME.** The lane's verifier measured the pair per-pixel: **2,377 pixels moved
against a 608-pixel same-build floor.** So the frames are not bit-identical and
the honest statement is the smaller one: **14 ms of shadow pass buys essentially
no image** -- four times the same-arm noise, on a 1,440,000-pixel frame, i.e.
0.17 per cent of it, and invisible in every rectangle the shot publishes. That
is still a negative control worth the change; it is not a null.

**AND ONE HYPOTHESIS MEASURED AND REFUTED, recorded because it was wrong.** The
obvious follow-on was that per-instance culling should also come off the canopy
(12-triangle cards against a matrix decompose and a sphere transform). Measured
at forestfloor, one flag apart: culling off is **31.2 ms against 20.7**, and
2,796,348 triangles against 1,591,457 -- 27.6 triangles per tree, so the canopy
is NOT drawing a flat 12. The shared answer stands and the flag was withdrawn
rather than shipped as a knob nobody would ever move.

### 2.14.7 The reach is bounded by the eye's height

The same 4,200 m radius is **7.4 ms from the air and 20.7 ms from the ground**,
and on the ground it buys almost nothing: forestfloor `box` 22.82 -> 23.05, a
quarter of a count, for 13.4 ms. That asymmetry is geometry, not tuning. From an
eye at height h, ground at distance g is foreshortened by h/g, so the ground's
screen area falls as `h/g^3` while a tree on it falls as `1/g^2`: **trees per
pixel of ground grow as g/h.** From 1.6 m the 4 km ring is a sliver at the
horizon holding forty thousand trees; from 1,200 m it is most of the frame.

`canopyReachM(radiusM, altM) = min(radiusM, max(2000, 3.5 * altM))`. The 3.5 is
`4200 / 1200`, so the ceiling binds exactly at the pose it was derived from
rather than two constants disagreeing about which is in charge there. Both ends
set by the 16.6 ms budget measured at Forest density (3,840 per km2, three times
Hills), forestfloor being the hero ground frame:

| floor | canopy trees | triangles | p50 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| off (`?canopy=0`) | 0 | 1,272,522 | 7.3 ms | -- |
| 2,000 m (shipped) | 12,778 | 1,294,255 | 9.2 ms | +1.9 ms |
| 3,000 m | 28,420 | 1,405,023 | 14.1 ms | +6.8 ms |
| 4,200 m | 55,297 | 1,591,457 | 20.7 ms | OVER BUDGET |

`canopyDistanceWeight` fades to the REALISED reach, not the configured radius:
ending it at the radius while the reach is shorter puts the last tree at full
weight against the cut, which is the hard ring the gradient exists to prevent.

### 2.14.7b `CANOPY_SHADE`: default OFF, pending an Admin ruling

Routed here by the lane's verifier. The term is `1 - CANOPY_SHADE * shadeW`
applied to the understorey density, `CANOPY_SHADE` is 0.45, and `shadeW` is
`canopyWeight(altM, stand)`, the PLANET's stand weight. It has been **dead code
since WG-116**: `sampleChunk` computes `shadeW` only inside `if (canopy.total >
0)`, which has been false in every shipped build since the canopy tier was
retired. RN-2231 woke it.

Woken, it is worth **38.5 per cent of the forestfloor understorey** (41,300 ->
25,391 props) and **18.1 per cent of the meadow's** (52,139 -> 42,719; Plains
carries less stand weight than Forest). Frames committed as
`docs/screenshots/RN2225_shade_{forestfloor,meadow}_{on,off}.png`, taken at the
shipped constants one flag apart.

**FORESTFLOOR, JUDGED.** It does not read as a canopy shading its floor. Put the
pair side by side and what the 38.5 per cent removes is mostly the LARGE pale
broadleaf fronds and the taller dark clusters that break up the blade mass: the
OFF frame has a layered floor with distinct plant silhouettes scattered through
it, and the ON frame is a more uniform carpet of small blades with the litter
and mud showing through in slightly more places. It never goes bald, because
A2's ground-cover carpet is a separate layer this term does not touch, so the
failure is not "sparse" -- it is **plainer**. And the reason it cannot read as
shade is structural rather than a tuning miss: at a forest site `shadeW` is
close to 1 across the entire visible floor, so the term lands as a spatially
UNIFORM cut, with none of the patchiness (dark under the crowns, bright in the
gaps) that the eye actually reads as canopy shadow. A uniform 38.5 per cent is
indistinguishable from someone having turned the understorey density down.
**Verdict: slightly worse.**

**MEADOW, JUDGED.** Very nearly indistinguishable, and I looked for it knowing
the number. Both frames are a full, healthy grass field to the horizon; with the
term on there is marginally more ground visible between clumps in the near band
and a few fewer of the tall blades. There is also nothing in frame to attribute
it to -- the only trees are the new far-canopy line on the horizon, hundreds of
metres away, so an 18 per cent thinning of the grass at the player's feet has no
visible cause. **Verdict: neutral, no harm and no gain.**

**SO THE DEFAULT IS OFF**, per the standing instruction that a lane whose own eye
says "worse" flips and says so. `?canopyshade=1` is the arm to rule on and the
frames above are the evidence; **Admin rules, and this record does not
pre-decide it beyond the flip.** The physical argument for the term is real -- a
closed canopy does dim its floor, which is why `build_props_forest.py` authors
ferns and litter in the first place -- so the shape of a fix, if it is wanted,
is **patchiness rather than magnitude**: a `shadeW` that varies over tens of
metres (crown-scale) instead of one that saturates over a whole biome. That is a
world-gen question about the stand field, not a rendering constant.

### 2.14.9 The two hero judgements, written against the bar

**FLYOVER, BEFORE** (`RN2225_flyover_before.png`). Bare ground under a good sky.
The ground material and A3's far tier are doing real work -- there is a green
that reads as vegetated land and a large soft cloud shadow with a properly
stepped edge -- but nothing stands on it anywhere in the frame. It reads as an
aerial photograph of a golf course, or of a planet before anything grew: the
haze ramp is right, the horizon is right, and the surface is a texture rather
than a place. It is not a forested world and nothing in the frame suggests one
exists below.

**FLYOVER, AFTER** (`RN2225_flyover_after.png`). It is honestly better and it is
honestly not a forest. The ground material is still under it and still reads
correctly, and the trees are now unmistakably present, correctly hazed --
they lose contrast into the distance at exactly the rate the ground does, which
is the whole content of RN-2232 and is visible the moment it is put beside
`RN2225_flyover_nohaze.png`, where the same trees are hard black grit sitting on
top of the atmosphere instead of inside it. **The canopy edge is a fade and not
a ring:** there is no line anywhere in the frame where the trees stop, the
density thins continuously into the haze, and I looked for the boundary
knowing where it should be and could not place it. **But it reads as fine
speckle, not as woodland.** That is measured and it is not this lane's
machinery: the realised density is 366 trees per km2, a mean spacing of 52 m,
and an 8 m crown covers **1.8 per cent** of the ground. The site is Hills, whose
canopy table asks 1,200 per km2 before the stand field and the treeline take
two thirds of it, and even the Forest biome's 3,840 is 16 m spacing. **The
source, the reach, the rung, the haze and the budget are now all correct end to
end, and what limits the picture is the density the planet asks for.** That is
world-gen's table and it is routed rather than quietly tripled here.

**VISTA, BEFORE AND AFTER** (`RN2225_vista_*.png`). Unchanged, and correctly so:
the pose stands on a 4.7 km ridge above the treeline, so there is no canopy for
the tier to place at any radius. Both frames read the same -- the far ridgelines
hold their shape, the haze ramp is the A4 lane's and is good, and the middle
distance is still the bare-material problem A3 owns. **The honest note is that
this shot was on the brief as a judgement pose and it turns out to be blind to
the subject**, which is worth writing down so the next vegetation lane picks a
pose with trees in it rather than re-running this one.

### 2.14.10 Owed, and the largest one is an asset change

0. **THE `CANOPY_SHADE` RULING IS OPEN AND THE DEFAULT IS OFF** (2.14.7b).
   Frames are committed and judged; Admin rules. If it is wanted back, the ask
   is a crown-scale `shadeW` from world-gen, not a different constant here.
1. **THE IMPOSTOR IS FOUR INSTANCES FOR TWELVE TRIANGLES, and that is the single
   biggest remaining lever on this tier.** 22,940 trees occupy 91,760 slots,
   because `props_canopy.glb` authors its `_LOD3` across four materials (Bark,
   Leaf, LeafLight, LeafDeep) and `PropLibrary` keys one batch per material. The
   whole cost of this tier is per-instance CPU -- measured at about 0.87 us per
   tree, linear in tree count over a 5x sweep -- so **a single-material impostor
   card would divide the instances, the cull cost and the draw calls by four**
   and would take the reach ceiling from 4,200 m to roughly 8,000 m at the same
   frame. It is a `tools/blender/build_props_canopy.py` change plus a manifest
   row, and it is the correct next move on this tier.
2. **The forest density is what limits the aerial picture, and it is world-gen's
   table.** 1.8 per cent ground coverage at the spawn (arithmetic in 2.14.9).
   Whoever raises it must raise it with the cost model above in hand.
3. **The `vista` pose is blind to vegetation** (2.14.9). A new aerial judgement
   pose over the Forest biome is owed.
4. **A depth-7 canopy band is refused and the reason is placement quantisation**
   (2.14.2). If the far tier ever needs to pass 5,200 m it needs a placement
   path that does not interpolate inside a 230 m mesh cell.

## 2.15 THE SINGLE-MATERIAL CANOPY CARD (RN-2240 to RN-2244, 2026-08-20, `lane/card-material`)

`lane/card-material`, base `origin/main` at faa31238. Routed by 2.14.10/2.14.9's
own owed item: "the biggest remaining rendering lever is that the impostor
costs FOUR instances for twelve triangles." All five numbers used.

### 2.15.1 The defect was never in the twelve triangles

`props_canopy.glb`'s `_LOD3` (RN-2202) drew a Bark trunk stub (8 tri) plus
crossed Leaf quads (4 tri), and reading that as "two materials, twelve
triangles" understates it. `PropLibrary.register` batches by (stem, material)
found ANYWHERE the stem appears (`PropLibrary.ts:248-307`), not per LOD, and a
canopy tree's LOD0/LOD2 use all four of `Bark`/`LeafDeep`/`Leaf`/`LeafLight`
(RN-271's bottom-to-top crown shading). So `PropLibrary.partsOf('Canopy_Pine')`
was always FOUR parts, and `ScatterEmit.emit`'s placement loop
(`ScatterEmit.ts:193`) acquired one instance slot per part for every canopy
tree unconditionally, because a placed prop is the union of its parts by
construction. `_LOD3` authored Bark and Leaf directly; LeafDeep and LeafLight
had no rung of their own there, so `PropLods.meshAtTier`'s walk-down rule
(correct for an asset with NO far rung at all) silently bound them to their
LOD2 cone/dome geometry -- the far tier was drawing partial LOD2 mass through
two of its four "instances" at every canopy range, not just a spare stub.
Every canopy tree is ALWAYS at this tier: `CANOPY_NEAR_M` (550 m) is past
`CANOPY_LOD3_M` (420 m), asserted at boot, so there is no nearer request any
of this was ever answering.

### 2.15.2 The fix, in two files

**Asset** (`tools/blender/build_props_canopy.py`): `_impostor` (all three
`lod3=` callables) drops the Bark taper entirely and authors ONLY the crossed
Leaf quads, matching `build_tree_conifer.py`'s own `_card` precedent word for
word ("dropping the trunk is the whole of the saving"). Canopy_Pine/Fir/
Broadleaf `_LOD3` go from 12 triangles / 2 materials to 4 triangles / 1
material each. The trunk costs nothing to lose: the thickest canopy stem
(Broadleaf, 0.26 m radius) is under a pixel wide at `CANOPY_LOD3_M` in the
shipped 1600x900/60 degree frame, the identical arithmetic `NODE_LOD3_M` was
derived from. `contracts.json`: `Canopy_*_LOD3.max_tris` 12 -> 4,
`max_tris_total` 2032 -> 2008 (742+50+334+28+784+58=1996 base, +3x4). `pc.Prop`
role checking (`_check_roles`) only requires used roles be a SUBSET of the
pinned order, so dropping Bark from one tier needs no contract role change.

**Client** (`web/src/world/ScatterEmit.ts`, `emit()`): a canopy prop
(`spec.canopy === true`) now skips acquiring a part whose OWN `lods[LOD3]` is
`-1` (`part.lods[PROP_LODS - 1] < 0`), rather than letting it fall back. This
is the half that actually divides the instance count: dropping Bark from the
card alone would not have, because the stem's material union (still 4, from
LOD0/LOD2) is what `partsOf` returns regardless of what LOD3 itself authors.
With the skip in place AND the card single-material, Bark/LeafDeep/LeafLight
all read `lods[3] === -1` for a canopy stem and are refused; only `Leaf`
survives. Gated on `spec.canopy` so every other scatter prop (none of which
author a `_LOD3` today) is untouched. `PropLods.ts` itself needs no change: it
already keys a rung by tier, not by how many materials use it.

### 2.15.3 The numbers, measured

Sentinel-owned `vite preview --outDir dist-before/dist-after --port 5471/5472
--strictPort`, sentinel text fetched back over each port before probing,
killed by PID after. `run.mjs --scenario=surface --evalfile=artframe.js
--evalargs="{shot:'flyover'}"`, `window.__of.stats().props` read on the same
settled frame. Real Windows D3D11 (ANGLE), RTX 4060 Ti, 1600x900.

| | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| canopy instances (`OF_*:canopy` sum) | 91,760 | **22,940** | **exactly a quarter** |
| `OF_Leaf:canopy` live | 22,940 | 22,940 | unchanged (1 per tree) |
| `OF_Bark/LeafDeep/LeafLight:canopy` live | 22,940 each | **0** | refused, not fallen back |
| flyover triangles | 312,601 | 209,525 | -103,076 (-33.0%) |
| flyover draw calls | 29 | 26 | -3 (empty batches drop out) |
| `canopyProps` (trees placed) | 22,940 | 22,940 | unchanged -- same forest |

WG-189's interleaved paired method, 3 pairs, arm order before/after each pair,
two independently-owned preview servers so neither arm is rebuilt mid-sweep:

| pair | before p50 | after p50 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 9.9 ms | 3.5 ms |
| 2 | 7.2 ms | 3.6 ms |
| 3 | 7.5 ms | 3.6 ms |
| **median** | **7.5 ms** | **3.6 ms** |

Frame time roughly halved on this pose (-52% at the median), consistent with
WG-189's own finding that "the aerial frame's cost is instance-count CPU, not
geometry" (2.14.10).

### 2.15.4 Determinism and gates

`props_canopy.glb` rebuilt twice from the changed script: byte-identical both
times, sha256 `cfa22846...`. `git status` after both rebuilds shows exactly
the four intended files changed (the glb, the two build/contract files, and
`ScatterEmit.ts`) -- nothing in `web/wasm/dist` or `test/expected.json`
touched. `validate_glb.py props_canopy`: PASS, all rows including
`tris_total 2008 <= 2008` and `materials 4 <= 4`. `check_shadow_lod.py
props_canopy`: unchanged verdict (canopy never earns a cascade, as before --
RN-2233's theorem is about `CANOPY_NEAR_M` vs cascade splits, untouched by
this lane). `cd web && npm run check:proplods`, `check:proxies`, `check:roles`:
all green (proplods' own self-test asserts the ladder behaviour this lane
relies on -- a part with no rung at a tier falls back for an asset with NO
far rung, which is still exactly what happens for every non-canopy prop).
`npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` clean, `cd web && npm run check` **8/8**
twice (once mid-lane, once on the final tree after the before/after
measurement round-trip).

**A methodology trap worth recording**: the first before/after attempt
measured IDENTICAL bytes on both arms, because `web/public/assets` is a
one-time `copyFileSync` snapshot (`scripts/sync-assets.mjs`), not a live
mirror of `assets/models/dist` the way a symlink would be -- `git stash`
reverts the SOURCE glb but not the already-synced copy vite actually serves.
Fixed by re-running `node scripts/sync-assets.mjs` after every stash/pop
before rebuilding, and confirmed by hashing `public/assets/props/
props_canopy.glb` before each `vite build`. Also: PowerShell mangles embedded
double quotes in `--evalargs='{"shot":"flyover"}'` into an unquoted `{shot:
flyover}`, which `run.mjs`'s direct-interpolation eval (`(${evalArgs})`,
`run.mjs:87`) then throws as `ReferenceError: flyover is not defined` --
sidestepped by passing single-quoted JS-literal values instead
(`--evalargs={shot:'flyover'}`), valid because `evalArgs` is interpolated as
JS source, not `JSON.parse`d.

### 2.15.5 The judgement (RAILS: cards must not visibly change)

`pngdiff.mjs` on the flyover frame: before-vs-after **1.36%** of pixels moved
(darker 9,492 / lighter 5,974, roughly balanced -- a silhouette change, not a
darkening), against a same-build fresh-process floor of **0.05%** (27x). This
is real, not noise, and it is honestly attributable: losing the Bark stub and
the two materials' worth of stray LOD2 fallback mass changes a small edge on
every one of 22,940 trees, and the fresh-process floor being two orders of
magnitude smaller says the change is systematic rather than jitter. By eye
(both frames captured with the debug HUD, which independently confirms the
same instance/triangle/call numbers as the JSON): same forest, same 22,940-
tree population, same speckle extent and density at this altitude, no missing
stands, no popping silhouette -- the difference is confined to each tree's own
few pixels and reads as a slightly crisper card (one clean leaf material)
rather than a softer one (four overlapping partial materials), not as
degraded fidelity. Judged against the RAILS bar ("same forest, cheaper"): met.

### 2.15.6 Owed

**The 8 km reach ceiling this quartering opens up is not spent here.**
`ScatterTuning.CANOPY_MAX_RADIUS_M`/`canopyReachM` are untouched by design --
the RAILS for this lane forbid the density tables and `Registry.ts` (owned by
the concurrent canopy-density lane), and reach tuning is the same family of
decision. Whoever raises the ceiling now has a real quarter of the old
instance cost per metre of reach to spend it with.

**The audit found a second instance of the same defect and did not fix it.**
`TreeConifer_Full/Half/Low_LOD3` and the `TreeBroadleaf` equivalents are
already single-material (`OF_Leaf`, 4 tri, confirmed by decoding
`tree_conifer.glb`/`tree_broadleaf.glb` directly), matching what 2.14.10
guessed. `TreeConifer_Stump_LOD3` and `TreeBroadleaf_Stump_LOD3` are NOT: 24
triangles across `OF_Bark` (20) and `OF_LeafDry` (4), because the Stump
variant's own comment says its far rungs are its LOD1 reused unchanged ("the
Stump variant is contract-required (`lod_nodes`) but never drawn --
`NodeBatch.ts`'s `VARIANTS` list is Full/Half/Low only"). Same shape of
defect, zero measurable cost: Stump geometry never enters `NodeBatch`'s live
render path, so unlike the canopy case there is no instance count or triangle
count this is currently spending. Named and left alone rather than touched,
on the same logic RN-2200 used for the pre-ladder two-slot bug: dormant is not
the same as free to ignore forever, but it is not this lane's budget.

**The `docs/controllers/rendering.md` header line had grown to 280 KB** of
concatenated lane summaries (every prior lane appended its blurb onto the
`Last updated` line instead of replacing it), large enough that this lane's
own Read/Grep tools could not load it. Replaced with a short pointer to this
section rather than appended to; flagged so the NEXT lane does not revert the
habit.

## 2.16 THE POOL CEILING (RN-2260 to RN-2264, 2026-08-20, `lane/pool-ceiling`)

`lane/pool-ceiling`, base `origin/main` at f08edd7c. Routed by the WG-220
verifier: at the FOREST biome the canopy tier saturates the shared 65,536
instance pool (HUD `POOL FULL`, 12,462 not drawn, 16% of the stand), even
after 2.15 halved pool pressure by making the far card single-material. All
five numbers used.

### 2.16.1 Why the card merge made this WORSE, not better, for one batch

2.15 collapsed a canopy tree from four material parts (`Bark`, `Leaf`,
`LeafDeep`, `LeafLight`) to one: `ScatterEmit.emit` now skips acquiring the
three parts whose own `_LOD3` is absent, so only `OF_Leaf:canopy` ever
receives a slot. That is the right fix for instance COUNT (a quarter as many
slots for the same trees) and the wrong shape for CEILING PRESSURE: the whole
tier's demand, which used to spread across four independent 65,536-slot
batches (so no single batch could plausibly fill), now lands on ONE. A forest
that would have asked each of four batches for ~19,500 instances instead asks
one batch for the full count. The ceiling was never raised to match, because
nothing before this lane had actually measured a FOREST-biome aerial frame
against it (WG-227's `forestair`, added in the same lane that raised the
density table, is the first shot that reaches the number).

**Measured directly against `origin/main` at f08edd7c (the unmodified
"before"), `forestair`, real Windows D3D11 (ANGLE), RTX 4060 Ti:**
`canopyProps` (the scatter's own count of trees it placed) 77,998;
`OF_Leaf:canopy` batch `live` 65,536, `cap` 65,536, `refused` **12,462**
(15.98%, the "16%" the routed finding names). `PropLibrary.grow()`'s
`console.error('[of] prop pool ... is FULL ...')` fires exactly once
(`b.warned`) and, correctly, fails any `run.mjs` invocation that captures this
pose (`smoke: FAILURES`) -- the defect is loud in the harness sense already.
What it was NOT loud in: `artframe.js`'s own JSON never read the pool's
`refused` count, so a hero-frame capture that only inspects the returned
object (rather than the exit code) could still read `valid: true` over a
truncated stand. See 2.16.3.

### 2.16.2 The ceiling, and its memory arithmetic

`web/src/render/instancing/PropLibrary.ts`. `Batch` gained its own `maxCap`
field, set at `batchFor()` time: `CANOPY_MAX_CAPACITY` (new, 131,072) for the
canopy suffix's batch, the existing `MAX_CAPACITY` (65,536, unmoved) for every
other. `grow()` reads `b.maxCap` instead of the module constant; `stats().
ceiling` sums each batch's own `maxCap` instead of `batches.size *
MAX_CAPACITY`, so the reported guard rail is exact rather than assuming every
batch shares one number.

**Sized the same way every ceiling in this file already is sized**: the next
power-of-two double from `START_CAPACITY` (2,048) that clears the worst
measured case. 77,998 sits between 65,536 and 131,072, so one more double:
`2,048 -> ... -> 65,536 -> 131,072`, 68% of headroom above the worst case
measured so far (the WG-220 lane's own FOREST-density figure), same growth
shape (O(1) amortised, a batch that never fills never pays) as every other
pool in the project.

**A DEDICATED ceiling rather than a raised shared one, and the reason is
evidence, not caution.** Canopy already had its own BATCH (RN-2233's
`CANOPY_SUFFIX`, so scrub and rocks were never sharing a reservation with
trees in the first place -- `PropLibrary`'s batches are keyed one per
material+suffix and grow independently). What was shared was the CEILING
CONSTANT. Raising `MAX_CAPACITY` itself to 131,072 would apply the new
guard to the understorey's `:detail` batch and every near-biome batch too,
none of which has ever been measured anywhere near the old 65,536 (the
densest, `OF_Grass`, is the batch the constant was already raised FOR, and
sits far under it today). A blanket raise would be a guard that guards
nothing for those classes while doubling their worst-case reservation for no
measured reason, so the split constant is the one with evidence behind it.

**Memory.** Same arithmetic as the existing `MAX_CAPACITY` comment (100 B of
CPU-side typed array plus 80 B of texture per slot), doubled: 131,072 slots is
about 10.5 MB of texture (up from 5.2 MB) plus about 13.1 MB of CPU-side typed
array, and it is paid ONLY by the one batch (`OF_Leaf:canopy`) that actually
grows into it -- `grow()` still starts doubling from 2,048. The three other
canopy-suffixed batches (`Bark`/`LeafDeep`/`LeafLight`) also carry the raised
`maxCap` now (they share `isCanopy`'s branch, since a batch's ceiling is
decided by its suffix, not by whether 2.15's skip ever lets it fill), but they
stay at `live: 0` by construction -- 2.15's `ScatterEmit` skip refuses every
acquire against them -- so the extra headroom on those three costs nothing
real; `stats().ceiling`'s reported sum (below) counts it anyway, which is
conservative rather than wrong.

### 2.16.3 Loud when hit: the settleGate-class fix

2.14.4 found the identical SHAPE of defect in the scatter backlog: a gate
that only asked whether the terrain had converged, not whether anything had
grown on it, so a partial forest was reported as a settled frame. The pool
ceiling has the same failure mode from a different angle: `console.error`
fires once per batch (`b.warned`), so a sweep taking several readings in one
process would only see it on the FIRST hit, and `artframe.js`'s own returned
JSON carried no `refused` field at all -- a hero frame could be captured,
inspected, and judged without anyone reading the one place the truncation was
recorded.

`web/tools/smoke/probes/artframe.js`: every shot's return now computes
`poolRefused` from `stats().props.refused` (0 when there is no props record at
all, e.g. an orbital shot) and sets `valid: poolRefused === 0` instead of the
old unconditional `valid: true`. `poolRefused` and `poolCeiling` are also
added to the `scatter` block for every shot, alongside `canopyProps` and the
rest of WG-220's own counters, so a reader never has to cross-reference a
separate pool query to see whether a frame was truncated. This makes hitting
the ceiling structurally impossible to publish as a settled frame from this
probe again, on the same logic 2.14.4 used for the backlog.

### 2.16.4 The proof: `forestair`, before and after

Two builds (`vite build --outDir dist-before` at unmodified f08edd7c,
`--outDir dist-after` on this branch), two owned `vite preview` servers
(127.0.0.1:5561 / :5562, `--strictPort`), sentinel text written into each
dist and fetched back over its own port before the first probe, both killed
by PID (`netstat -ano` on the `LISTENING` port) after. `tools/smoke/
rn2260sweep.mjs` (new; `wg220sweep.mjs`'s own `shot === 'flyover' ? 'surface'
: 'walk'` routes `forestair` to the wrong scenario, since WG-227 built
`forestair` as `flyover`'s pose over different ground and needs `surface`
too), WG-189's interleaved method, 3 pairs, arm order rotated.

| | before (f08edd7c) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `canopyProps` (trees placed) | 77,998 | 77,998 (unchanged -- same forest) |
| `OF_Leaf:canopy` live / cap | 65,536 / 65,536 | **77,998 / 131,072** |
| pool `refused` | **12,462** | **0** |
| `valid` (this lane's own gate) | **false** | **true** |
| frame triangles | 251,873 | 251,873 |
| draw calls | 27 | 27 |
| `vramEstimateMB` | 104.2 | 104.2 |
| `poolCeiling` (sum of `maxCap`) | 1,376,256 | 1,638,400 |
| p50 (3 interleaved pairs) | **5.70** (5.8/5.6/5.7, spread 0.20) | **6.40** (6.2/6.7/6.4, spread 0.50) |

**Triangles and draw calls are IDENTICAL to the digit in both arms, and that
is a real finding rather than a null result.** The 12,462 refused trees were
never in this pose's view frustum at all (canopy batches keep per-instance
frustum culling, RN-2204): they were somewhere else on the 3,500 m-radius
disc, not necessarily behind the camera at THIS yaw. The defect is therefore
not "this exact picture is missing trees" but "16% of the forest does not
exist anywhere the camera could ever turn to see it" -- which is the worse of
the two and the reason a live-count/refused-count fix matters even when one
photographed frame does not visibly move. `p50` before, **5.70 ms, matches the
WG-220 verifier's own 5.8 ms reading** (the brief's stated headroom check).
After the fix: **6.40 ms, +0.70 ms, 10.2 ms under the 16.6 ms budget.**

**VRAM: `vramEstimateMB` does not move (104.2 -> 104.2), and this is an
INSTRUMENT GAP, not a finding that the ceiling is free.** `StatsProbe.ts`
computes it from `extraVramBytes + r.post.vram` -- render-target and
post-stack memory -- and does not account for `BatchedMesh`'s own per-instance
matrix/colour textures at all, contrary to what the `MAX_CAPACITY` comment in
`PropLibrary.ts` claims ("Reported as `vramEstimateMB` before and after").
**The real delta is the arithmetic in 2.16.2: +5.2 MB of texture (65,536 more
slots x 80 B) on the one batch that fills, +6.5 MB of CPU-side typed array**,
against the study's 104 of 260 MB budget -- comfortably inside it either way.
Flagged rather than fixed: `vramEstimateMB`'s blind spot to instance-pool
textures is a pre-existing gap this lane did not introduce and is out of this
lane's scope to correct.

**Determinism**: three fresh Chrome processes (the sweep's own 3 repeats) on
the after build return `canopyProps` 77,998, triangles 251,873 and
`poolRefused` 0 to the digit every time. **Walk-scenario counters untouched**,
checked directly rather than assumed (the fix is scoped to the `:canopy`
suffix and the understorey's `:detail` batches are a different key entirely):
`forestfloor` `propsPlaced` **41,300**, `meadow` `propsPlaced` **52,139**,
both matching WG-220's own 6.9.7 identity table exactly, `cellsCapped`/
`chunksCapped` 0/0, `scatterBacklog` 0 on the after build.

### 2.16.5 Rails

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` clean, `cd web && npm run check` 8/8.
Only three files changed vs `origin/main`: `PropLibrary.ts`, `artframe.js`
(the `poolRefused`/`valid` wiring), and the new `tools/smoke/rn2260sweep.mjs`.
`web/wasm/dist/*` and `test/expected.json` untouched. No texgen/Blender file
and no density table touched (other lanes' scope). Both scratch preview
servers killed by PID after the sweep; `dist-before`/`dist-after` are
`web/dist-*/`-gitignored and were deleted rather than committed. Branch
`lane/pool-ceiling`, not merged to main.

## 2.17 THE CROWN ASSET (RN-2245 to RN-2249, 2026-08-20, `lane/crown-asset`)

`lane/crown-asset`, base `origin/main` at f08edd7c. **RN-2245 to RN-2249 used;
RN-2250 to RN-2254 surrendered unused** (abandoned per NUMBERS.md rule 4, never
reuse): two commits covered the block. Frames `docs/screenshots/RN2245_*`.
Routed here by BOTH WG-220 verifications, which reached the same sentence
independently: the air view is now purely asset-limited, because a nine-pixel
green blob has no canopy texture.

### 2.17.1 The defect, and why no density could have fixed it

The far tier (2.14) draws every tree past `CANOPY_NEAR_M` as a four-triangle
crossed-quad impostor, and since RN-2202 that card has worn `leaf`. **`leaf` is
a picture of one conifer FROND.** It has to be: `OF_Leaf` is also the material
on the bough cards of `tree_conifer.glb` and the crown cards of
`tree_broadleaf.glb`, i.e. on the tree the player is standing next to, and a
frond is the right picture there.

Minified to the three-to-nine pixels an aerial tree actually gets, a frond is a
featureless green chip. **Measured on the shipped bytes** (box-filter to 3x3,
cut at the manifest's own `alpha_test` 0.35, Rec.709 luma):

| | 3x3, texels surviving | luma range | spread | 6x6 spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `of_leaf_a.png` | 7 / 9 | 185..205 | **20** | 38 |
| `of_canopy_a.png` | 8 / 9 | 109..236 | **127** | 175 |

The leaf card's nine-pixel read is 200, 200, 200. The crown card's is a rounded
blob with a top corner cut and a **223 / 178 / 113** ramp down its three rows.
That is the whole lane in one table: WG-220 put six times the stems in the
frame and every one of them was still a flat chip.

### 2.17.2 THE LID, PRICED AND REFUSED, AND THE REFUSAL IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE

The classic third quad, a horizontal lid across the crown top, was the brief's
own second item. The lazy refusal is "at 14 degrees of pitch a lid presents
`sin 14` = 0.242 of its area against the vertical pair's `cos 14` = 0.970, so
it is a quarter of a quad for fifty per cent more triangles". **That argument
is wrong twice and it is worth writing down why**, because the next lane to
look at this will reach for it.

**(1) The pitch is not 14 degrees where it matters.** -14 is the camera's, i.e.
the frame CENTRE's. The flyover frame spans depression -16 to +44 (2.14.1), and
the visible canopy runs from the frame's bottom edge at 1,243 m ground (44
degrees) out to the reach at 3,500 m (19 degrees). The lid-to-pair ratio is
`(d/h) * tan(depression) / 1.273` (the 1.273 is `E[|cos|+|sin|]` over yaw for
the crossed pair). **(2) The area ratio `d/h` is not small for the species that
matters.** Off `contracts.json`, crown card height is `H * (1 - crown_lo)`:
pine 3.85 x 5.40 (`d/h` 0.472), fir 2.90 x 6.60 (0.333), **broadleaf 8.40 x
10.50 over a 5.04 m card, `d/h` = 2.083** -- and WG-222 made the mix
broadleaf-led on purpose. So at the frame's near edge a broadleaf lid would
present **1.58x the crossed pair's projected area**, not a quarter of it. The
cheap refusal is arithmetic that flatters the answer it was reaching for.

**THE REAL REFUSAL IS THAT THERE IS NO PICTURE TO PUT ON IT.** A lid needs a
TOP-DOWN crown. This family authors a SIDE view and must, because `cos` beats
`sin` at every depression in the frame and the vertical pair is 97 per cent of
the read at the centre. Mapping the side card onto a horizontal quad lays an
ovoid crown flat with its apex pointing sideways, foreshortened, **worst
exactly where the lid is most visible**, at the near edge. Authoring a top-down
picture is a second family, a second megabyte and a second role: a lane, not a
line. And the fill cost is the bad kind, an alpha-tested plane at grazing
incidence over 46,575 instances.

**So: two crossed quads, unchanged, and the condition is written down rather
than the conclusion.** The lid becomes right the moment a top-down crown
texture exists, and its value is `(d/h) * tan(depression)`, which for the
broadleaf at the frame's near edge is 2.0. That makes it the largest remaining
lever in the far tier and it is routed as owed (2.17.8), not dismissed.

### 2.17.3 The card, and what "judged at nine pixels" changed about it

`texgen._canopy_strips`, a third entry in `ALBEDO_FAMILIES` under every
determinism rule that module already holds: no RNG (`_hash01` only), no
transcendental past `sqrt` (which is why the crown profile and the rim are
parametrised by DEPTH down the card rather than by an angle), and
`_render_card` **untouched**, so `leaf` and `grass` rebuild bit-identical.

Three things survive a mip chain to a 3x3 read and nothing else does: the alpha
coverage, the LOW-frequency value field, and how ragged the outline is. So the
card is five tiers of large crown MASS (capsule strips, so the compositor's
deepest-clearance rule turns every meeting between two masses into an internal
shadow line) darkening from base 1.00 at the apex to 0.55 at the underside,
with a finer half-lit/half-shadow clump tier over them, a rim of round tufts
straddling an ovoid profile, and nine detached outliers. **Leaf detail was
deliberately not authored**: it is gone by the second mip and the tier ramp is
still there at the last one.

Three shapes were built and removed, each for a reason the code records: a ring
of radial spikes (read as a cactus; replaced by round tufts, because what breaks
a real canopy outline is clumps straddling it), four thin apical sprigs (read as
antennae), and one wide leader (read as a horn). The conifer read comes from
`pc.build_atlas` stretching one card into the pine's 3.85 x 2.55 and the
broadleaf's 8.40 x 10.50 boxes, which is where a species difference belongs
when one card serves three crowns.

**Coverage 0.7217 at the shipped 1024, measured then asserted** in a 0.66..0.78
band. The floor is the load-bearing edge and this family is the one that most
needs it: mip alpha converges toward the card's own coverage, so a card under
`alpha_test` 0.35 dissolves at exactly the distance this family exists to be
seen from. 0.66 is nearly twice it. `wrap` is **clamp in both axes**, the one
line differing from its two siblings: `leaf`/`grass` are periodic fields,
`canopy` is one object with a transparent margin.

### 2.17.4 A NEW ROLE THAT COSTS NO DRAW CALL, WHICH IS THE PART TO READ

`build_props_canopy.py`'s `ORDER` gains a fifth name, over a comment that said
a fifth name is a draw call. It is not, and the reason is RN-2244's own fix:
`ScatterEmit.emit` refuses a canopy part whose OWN `lods[LOD3]` is -1. `Canopy`
is authored at `_LOD3` alone, so all four near roles are now refused and
`OF_Canopy:canopy` **replaces** `OF_Leaf:canopy` as the one live batch rather
than joining it. An empty batch drops out of the frame, the same mechanism
RN-2244 measured taking the calls 29 to 26, and the `:canopy` suffix never
casts, so no cascade pays either. Measured, both hero poses: `props.batches`
21 -> 22 (one more BatchedMesh REGISTERED) and `render.calls` unchanged
(nothing more DRAWN). Those two counters disagreeing is the claim, not a
discrepancy.

`isFoliageMaterial` gains `OF_Canopy`, and it is the edit a reader would not
predict from "the far card gets its own texture". That one prefix test is the
sole authority behind the foliage base-contact bake, the normal bend, the wind,
the sky-ambient term and `setLeafVar`. Move the card onto a role that does not
start with `OF_Leaf` and all four stop silently, with no error and nothing in a
counter. Same shape of defect as the one this lane is fixing.

**TINT VARIATION WAS ALREADY WIRED AND IS PRESERVED RATHER THAN ADDED**, which
is the honest answer to the brief's third item. `ScatterEmit.emit` calls
`tintFor(look, seed, k)` per instance, then `PropLibrary.tint`, then
`setColorAt`; `tintFor` carries the value jitter (0.66 plus a 0.60 span), the
5.5 per cent flower branch, A2's dry drift (`DRY_T_GAIN` 0.85 toward
1.34/1.10/0.58) and an independent chroma mute. `look` comes from
`lookOf(parts.map(material))`, and a canopy stem's part list still contains its
`OF_Leaf*` LOD0/LOD2 crowns, so it still resolves `foliage` after this change.
**So the cards were never all one green; they were all one SHAPE**, and the
tint had nothing to vary except the overall level of a flat chip. With a crown
that has a lit top and a shaded underside, the same per-instance value drift
now separates one crown from its neighbour, which is visible in the flyover
pair.

Palette hex and `FoliageTone` row are `Leaf`'s **to the digit**, and that is a
measurement decision: the surface pipeline divides each family's own
`albedo_mean_linear` back out through `material.color`, so an identical hex
makes the frame's mean green provably unmoved and leaves the whole before/after
difference attributable to structure. It also closes the 550 m seam, where a
harvest tree's `_LOD3` card just inside `CANOPY_NEAR_M` is `OF_Leaf` and a
canopy crown just outside it is this.
