## 2.30 THE PLAINS FAR GROUND (RN-2475 to RN-2482, 2026-08-21, `lane/n1-plains`)

> **Numbers:** RN-2475 to RN-2482 of the RN-2475 to RN-2489 block; RN-2483 to
> RN-2489 surrendered unused. **Base:** `origin/main` at `8549155d`.
> **Charter:** world audit R4's **rank 1**, the top blocking row: "the plains far
> ground is a flat painted plane past ~130 m", diagnosis first.
> **Frames:** `docs/screenshots/RN2475_*`.

### 2.30.1 THE ONE-LINE ANSWER

The rectangle the gap was ranked on is **above the horizon and contains no
terrain**, the plains far ground is a **thirteen-row band** no rectangle in the
project had ever framed, and inside that band **RN-2421's analytic stand-in is
the only term drawing at all** -- at an amplitude fitted at an aerial pose over a
forest, with the massif's two kilometre octaves correctly gated off by a relief
band a plain cannot open. The fix is one multiply on the massif gate's own
complement; the residue is not in this material and is named in 2.28.7.

### 2.30.2 RN-2475, THE INSTRUMENT: `meadow.hzBand` IS SKY

**One paint settles it.** `lit = vec3(4.0, 0.0, 4.0)` at the end of
`TerrainFragLight.glsl.ts`, i.e. every terrain fragment magenta, one build,
reverted with the hash proof in 2.28.6.

| rectangle | shipped rgb | terrain-painted rgb | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meadow.hzBand` | 214.08 / 207.56 / 188.60 | **214.11 / 207.55 / 188.64** | **not one pixel is terrain** |
| `meadow.mid` | 97.41 / 122.38 / 63.23 | 97.80 / 122.49 / 63.62 | 0.4 counts, i.e. carpet |
| `vista.hzBand` | (shipped) | **248.30 / 190.78 / 220.08** | fully painted: the positive control |
| `vista.mid` | (shipped) | **252 / 193 / 223 at iqr 0** | 100 per cent terrain |

`meadow.hzBand` sits at frame rows 270 to 306. A row profile of the shipped frame
across x 80 to 1520 puts the sky/ground transition at rows **317 to 325** (per-row
iqr 3.93 at 307, 15.50 at 318, 130.28 at 323), and the rectangle's own committed
iqr of 4.06 is the same 3.9-to-4.2 the haze band reads on every row above it.
**Three audits watched a number not move because no ground term can move it, and
`?aerosol=0` "buying only 0.79 counts" there was a measurement of the sky.**
R4's RN-2453 is right that the shot set was blind to this subject and one level
short of how blind: the rectangle was not merely at the wrong SITE, it was on the
wrong SIDE OF THE HORIZON. Frame: `RN2475_term_terrain_meadow.png`.

**And the subject's real extent, off the same paint.** Terrain covers rows
**310 to 322 at `midfield` at 100 per cent** and **278 to 296 at `meadowfield` at
48 to 74 per cent** (the rest is distant scatter), and 0.000 to 0.02 of every row
below 330 at `midfield`, because the carpet and the props own the whole lower
frame. The plains far ground is a THIRTEEN-ROW BAND, which is why no hand-placed
fraction had ever landed in it and why rank 1 needed a rectangle.

### 2.30.3 RN-2476, THE CONVICTION: THE MASSIF GATE READS EXACTLY ZERO THERE

Painted `hzDbg = msfBand`, one line, one build, both poses in the same run.

| rectangle | painted `msfBand` |
|---|---|
| `midfield` far band (rows 310-322) | **luma 0.17, iqr 0, p95 0.00** |
| `midfield.r250` | luma 0.20, iqr 0, p95 0.00 |
| `vista.mid` | **215.76 at iqr 0**, i.e. saturated |
| `vista.hzBand` | 213.22 |

Frames `RN2475_term_msfband_midfield.png` and `RN2475_term_msfband_vista.png`.
**The gate is not broken and must not be opened.** `MASSIF_BAND`'s own note
promises "the plains a player walks for the first several hours are
bit-identical", and it is right to: the massif's 390 m and 1240 m octaves carry a
NORMAL half, and a normal perturbation at that scale over flat ground lights a
meadow like a dune field. What the gate does not do is tell anything else that a
plain has therefore been left with one macro term where a hill has three.

### 2.30.4 RN-2477, THE SEVEN-ARM TABLE, and it is what the project never had

`midfield.r250`, the new rectangle (2.28.5), one flag apart, fresh process each,
one build.

| arm | r250 iqr | what it says |
|---|---:|---|
| shipped | **32.63** | |
| `?horizoncellan=0` | **17.42** | RN-2421's analytic stand-in removed |
| `?horizon=0` | **17.42** | the WHOLE far-ground term removed, and it lands on the same number to the digit |
| `?horizonmassif=0` | 32.63 | the massif is a **null**, from the other side of 2.28.3's paint |
| `?aerosol=0` | 32.62 | **the air is a null**: 0.01 counts |
| `?grass=0` | 32.63 | the rectangle is pure terrain, independently of the paint |
| `?horizoncellan=6` | **133.05** | and the term responds to amplitude |

**Read those seven rows together and only one conclusion is available: on the
plains far ground the analytic stand-in is not the main term, it is the ONLY
term.** Its amplitude, `HORIZON_A_ANALYTIC = 1.65`, was fitted at RN-2421 to hold
`forestair`'s patch std at 6.24 -- an AERIAL pose over FOREST -- and the plains
far ground inherited it without anyone measuring there, because there was nothing
to measure with.

**R4's conclusion survives its own broken evidence.** RN-2453 concluded from a
sky rectangle that "at the plains site the lever is the GROUND and not the air".
It is: on a rectangle that can actually see the subject, `?aerosol=0` moves it by
**0.01 counts**.

### 2.30.5 RN-2478, THE TWO RECTANGLES

`midfield` gains `r250` and `meadowfield` gains `r250`: the same named range at
the same site, one pose with `props: false` (100 per cent terrain) and one with
the props the player actually gets (48 to 74 per cent). Placed by `rangeRects`
rather than as fractions so the report prints `rangeM` and `footM` beside them
and the guard refuses outright if the range walks off the frame. 600 m was
measured and refused: its strip is three rows from the horizon line, where any
pose drift walks it into the sky. Full argument in the manifest rows themselves.

**AND A CAVEAT THAT IS PART OF THE FIXTURE, not a footnote.** `rangeM` and
`footM` are a FLAT-PLANE inversion. At this site they are wrong past about 100 m
and 2.28.6 is the measurement that says so; the rectangle is a reproducible
PLACEMENT, not a survey, which is exactly what the mechanism's own header claims
for it.

### 2.30.6 RN-2479, A DESIGN BUILT, MEASURED AT 20x, AND THROWN AWAY

The first fix was two coarser octaves (640 m and 2560 m) handed over on the
160 m octave's own Nyquist complement. It was built, wired to its own uniform and
flag, typechecked, shipped to the preview and measured: **`?horizonfar=20` moved
`midfield.r250` by 0.00 counts.** An amplitude sweep that moves nothing is a term
outside its own gate (`HORIZON_ECO_GATE`'s own scar, one range band out).

**Why, and it is the instrument trap this lane contributes.** The design was
sized against the SHOT MANIFEST's `footM`, which inverts a flat plane and reports
0.257 m at 18 m, 0.957 at 35, 2.79 at 60, 11.1 at 120, **48.6 at 250** and 292 at
600. The SHADER's own `footM` is `max(length(dFdx(vWorld)), length(dFdy(vWorld)))`
and, painted as a step ladder at the ladder's own boundaries (1.8 / 8.0 / 20.0 /
53.3 / 213.0 m) at that same rectangle, exactly **one step passes**: the shader
sees **between 1.8 and 8.0 m** where the manifest says 48.6. The two disagree by
an order of magnitude because the ground at this site is not a plane -- it swells,
so the visible horizon is a crest a few hundred metres out rather than the
1,549 m geometric one, and the incidence is nothing like grazing. Every octave in
the material is therefore still Nyquist-legal out there and there was never a
hole in the ladder.

**A second lesson from the same afternoon, and it invalidated two readings before
it was noticed.** A painted intermediate whose value sits above about 0.3 is read
through the SHOULDER of the grade: on this build a painted 0.25 photographs at
177.55, 0.5 at ~207 and 1.0 at 215.76, so half the term's range is compressed
into nine counts. Two arms were re-run at one fifth scale for that reason. **Paint
diagnostics into the bottom of the curve, and prefer a `step()` ladder to a
continuous value.**

### 2.30.7 RN-2480, THE FIX: THE PLAINS MACRO GAIN

One multiply. The analytic stand-in's amplitude carries
`1 + HORIZON_AN_PLAINS_GAIN * (1 - hzMsfBand)`, i.e. it is given the macro
headroom the massif's relief gate is withholding, on that gate's OWN COMPLEMENT
so it is exactly 1.0 wherever the massif is at full strength and every relieved
pose is bit-identical by construction rather than by tuning. No new fade constant:
the boundary is the one `MASSIF_BAND` already draws. That is RN-2195's
complementary-fade idiom, which this file already spends twice, applied to the one
seam that had nothing on the far side of it.

`msfBand` moved out of `TerrainMassif.glsl.ts` and became `hzMsfBand`, computed
once in `TERRAIN_HORIZON_BLOCK` outside the `OF_SCALED` guard and read by both
consumers, for RN-1855's reason: the two now have to sum to a constant across
that boundary, and two copies of one smoothstep would give a shoulder both terms
and a crest neither the day one of them moved.

**The gain is 0.5 and it is read off a ladder rather than liked.** The sweep at
`midfield.r250`: **17.42 at 0x, 32.63 at 1x, 43.83 at 1.5x, 53.56 at 2x, 133.05
at 6x.** The mid field's own committed rectangles at this pose read 41.78 at r35,
41.41 at r60 and 47.33 at r120, so "the far ground carries what the mid field
carries" is the 41-to-47 band and 1.5x lands at **43.83**, inside it.

### 2.31.1 THE INSTRUMENT HAD TO COME FIRST, AND IT IS ONE LINE OF ARITHMETIC

Four audits have said "the crowns are blue-black confetti" and every number in
the file has been inside its band the whole time. The reason is that the
project had no instrument for the claim. `warm` is `meanR - meanB` and is
**blind to green by construction**; `sat` is a max-minus-min that a red-and-blue
pair satisfies exactly as well as a green one. So this lane publishes

```
gx = meanG - (meanR + meanB) / 2        counts, positive is green
```

on every named rectangle (`rn2495arms.mjs`), and pairs every arm against
`?canopy=0` **on the same rectangle** -- RN-2275's own instrument (2.19.4)
reused rather than a new hand-placed crown rectangle, so pose, range, haze, sun
and substrate are common-mode by construction and nothing is placed by eye.

### 2.31.2 THE CAST, ATTRIBUTED, AND THE AUDIT'S TWO NAMED SUSPECTS SPLIT 235-TO-1

`forestair`, box green excess, one page param apart. **Every row below comes
from the `?canopysat=0.62` baseline in ONE session, fresh process each** -- see
2.31.8 for the correction that made that sentence necessary. The baseline arm
reproduces R4's own table to the digit (`box` 93.39 / iqr 28.49, `world` 123.53
/ warm -8.07 / sat 0.166).

| arm | box gx | what it costs the frame |
|---|---:|---|
| baseline, `?canopysat=0.62` | **3.92** | -- |
| `?canopy=0` (the clearing) | 4.80 | the wood is **LESS green than its own treeless clearing** |
| `?propsky=0` | 3.91 | **PropSkyAmbient's sky fill: 0.01 counts.** EXONERATED |
| `?foliagetrans=0` | 3.90 | RN-2205's translucency: 0.02 counts, at the noise floor |
| `?prophaze=0` | 4.50 | the props' aerial perspective: 0.58, and it is the air |
| `?crownshadecard=0` | 4.80 | RN-2275's CARD half: **0.88** |
| `?foliagetone=0` | 6.27 | **FoliageTone's canopy desaturation: 2.35** |

| `?crownshade=0` (both halves) | 10.30 | 6.38, against 0.88 + 5.39 = 6.27 taken singly |

0.58 > sky fill 0.01**, and the last line is the consistency check: the two

`props:OF_Canopy:canopy` present in `chained`. The term is installed and live on

### 2.31.3 THE FIX: A CROWN IS NOT A LEAF

`FoliageTone.ts`'s `canopy` row is `{ sat: 0.62, val: 0.86 }`, RN-2245's
deliberate copy of `leaf` **to the digit**. `leaf`'s 0.62 was authored against
one measurement named in that file's own header: a near leaf card at a standing
eye. The `canopy` family is worn by exactly one object, the `_LOD3` crown
impostor, and it is a WHOLE TREE CROWN never drawn closer than
`CANOPY_NEAR_M` = 550 m.

Canopy radiative transfer says those are not the same colour: a photon leaving
the top of a closed stand has interacted with foliage more than once and each
interaction multiplies the leaf's spectral selectivity, so a canopy is strictly
MORE saturated than the leaves it is made of. The two-stream dense-canopy limit
`rInf(w) = (1 - sqrt(1-w)) / (1 + sqrt(1-w))` on broadleaf single-scattering
albedos (0.27 green, 0.08 red, 0.06 blue) gives, in LINEAR reflectance:

| | R/G | B/G |
|---|---:|---:|
| one leaf | 0.417 | 0.333 |
| dense crown | 0.265 | 0.197 |
| **the shipped card at sat 0.62** | **0.580** | **0.467** |

**The crown card was less saturated than a single LEAF, outside the bracket on
the unsaturated side.** `sat = 1.08` is solved to put its linear R/G on the
bracket's geometric midpoint, 0.3324 -- the midpoint and not the crown end,
because `rInf` is a semi-infinite limit and our stands are not closed
everywhere. `val` stays at **0.86 to the digit**: value is the axis RN-2275's
inversion is measured on, so the one axis this lane does not touch is the one
that could break it.

**THE MOVE IS EXACTLY LUMA-PRESERVING** and that is the safety argument, not a
nicety: the saturation term is `l + (c - l) * sat` with `l` the Rec.709 luma and
the three weights summing to one, so the transformed luma is `l` for every
`sat`. Measured across a five-point sweep of the constant, `forestair` `box`
luma reads **93.38 / 93.38 / 93.39 / 93.40 / 93.41** -- 0.03 counts of spread
over a 49 per cent chroma change. **RN-2275's pass condition is a LUMA condition
and is therefore protected by algebra rather than by a sweep.**

**A HUE AXIS WAS DRAFTED, MEASURED AND REFUSED, and the refusal is a finding.**
A luma-preserving blue-reduction term (`chloro`, blue's luminance handed back to
R and G by scaling the pair, so R:G is exactly invariant) was built and is worth
**0.6 counts of whole-frame warm** at `forestair`. It is not shipped: the same
two-stream numbers put a crown's blue at 0.74 of its red, and this row at
sat 1.08 is already at 0.46, so the saturation move **overshoots** blue downward
rather than leaving a deficit. Shipping a blue cut the model contradicts would
be exactly the constant nobody later dares move. **The corollary is the lane's
headline negative result: the frame's blue-grey is not the card's hue.**

### 2.31.5 THE JUDGEMENTS, against the SE bar, and one of them is PARTIAL

`docs/screenshots/RN2495_forestair_before.png` and `_after.png`;

**The FIELD: PARTIAL, and scoped to the MID field.** The mid field genuinely
reads as ground cover now rather than as a pale desaturated wash, and that is
the win. **It is not a pass, and a fresh-context verifier's eye and mine agree
on why: the FAR third is still a milky wash with no vegetation read at all, and
the NEAR stand still reads as dark confetti. The frame does not survive the SE
side-by-side.** Recorded as PARTIAL rather than MET; an earlier draft of this
section said MET and was overstating a real but narrow improvement.

The whole of it is carried by the far treeline PAINT rather than by the cards
(`SurfaceBind` publishes the finalised canopy colour to `TerrainTreeline` in the
same statement, 2.18.5, so one authority moves both and they cannot disagree),
and `?treeline=0` sizes the split exactly: with the paint in, the lane moves
`box` gx **3.92 -> 5.85 (+1.93)**; with `?treeline=0` it moves **3.86 -> 3.93
(+0.07)**. **The paint carries 1.86 of the 1.93 and the cards carry 0.07**,
which is the 0.1025 card shade showing up from the other side.

**The CROWNS: NOT MET, and it is the lane's routed finding rather than an
opinion.** At 3x the crowns are dark blue-violet specks before and dark
blue-violet specks after. The cause is measured and pictured:
`CanopySelfShadow.updateCanopyCardShade` multiplies the finalised card colour --
`FoliageTone`'s own output -- by a single **ACHROMATIC** scalar, read live at
`cardShade` **0.1025** at the Forest site. A crown card is painted at a tenth of
whatever colour is authored upstream before the air is added, so doubling its
chroma at source moves the `crowns` rectangle by 1.19 counts and can move it by
no more. `RN2495_crowns_crownshadecard0.png` is the same crop with
`?crownshadecard=0` and the crowns are unmistakably GREEN, with lit and shaded
sides from the card's own normals. **That frame is the whole argument.**

### 2.31.6 OWED, ROUTED, with the headroom already measured

1. **RN-2275's SHADE IS THE AERIAL CANOPY'S COLOUR, BOTH HALVES, and the
   follow-up shape is agreed.** `?crownshadecard=0` on this build keeps the
   inversion at THREE of the four pairs (`forestairnoon` -1.03, `forestairlow`
   -0.90, `flyovernoon` -6.05) and breaks the fourth (`flyoverlow` **+1.38**),
   reproduced independently by a fresh-context verifier, so the card half
   cannot simply go to zero. **The accepted shape is not a partial amp: it is a
   SPECTRALLY-SELECTIVE attenuation derived from the same leaf optics as 2.31.3,
   with the Rec.709 luma of the per-channel triple PINNED at today's 0.1025**,
   so every luma RN-2275 is judged on is unchanged by construction and only the
   hue of the shaded crown moves. The physics is the same argument this lane
   used on the albedo: leaf single-scattering albedo is ~0.27 in the green
   against ~0.07 in red and blue, so a shaded canopy is a saturated dark GREEN,
   never a neutral dark grey, and an achromatic Beer-Lambert multiply is the
   wrong spectral model even where its luma is right.
   **THE PRIZE IS RE-SIZED BY 2.31.8's CORRECTION and the far paint is the
   bigger half: card 0.88, far paint 5.39.** So the follow-up takes BOTH halves
   through the shared `SurfaceBind` seam rather than the card alone, which is
   also the only way the two cannot disagree about what a shaded crown is.
   The file is `render/materials/CanopySelfShadow.ts`, which no R4 lane owns;
   this lane did not take it rather than expand scope silently. Disarming the
   card half also improves the warm budget on every aerial pose
   (`forestairnoon` -1.56 -> -0.76, `flyovernoon` +4.97 -> +5.82).
2. **`forestair`'s remaining -5.59 is not a canopy problem** (2.31.2) and
   belongs to the substrate/aerosol lever family, as L3's owed item 2 already
   said. Any future brief that asks a canopy lane to close it is asking for
   something arithmetically out of reach.
3. **`PropSkyAmbient`'s two named terms are both at the noise floor on the
   aerial canopy** (0.01 counts each) and should not be named as a suspect for
   an aerial colour cast again without a new measurement. If the sky fill is
   ever WANTED at a visible size, the finding to start from is that
   `?propsky=20` moves `forestair` `box` by 0.11 counts, i.e. the term is
   linear and simply small.
4. **BLOOM WAS NOT TOUCHED.** `post/BloomGlsl.ts` and `PostDefaults.ts`'s bloom
   rows are unmodified: the audit attached rank 8's night halo to this lane and

no `assets/textures/dist` byte. New page param `canopysat`, registered in
`run.mjs`'s `PAGE_PARAMS` in the same commit that introduces it (RN-152's scar).

### 2.31.8 Correction pass (2026-08-21, fresh-context verifier, verdict FIX doc-only)

A fresh-context verifier that never touched this lane confirmed the code change
correct and safe: it reproduced the shipped, clearing, `?propsky=0` and
`?foliagetone=0` arms to the digit, reproduced the crown-chroma rectangle,
reproduced the luma guard exactly, and **independently proved that
`?canopysat=0.62` IS the pre-lane build** (it built true pre-lane `bda72279`
from scratch and matched). The 235x headline and `PropSkyAmbient`'s exoneration
are untouched. **Two of the seven rows of the attribution table were wrong and
are corrected here rather than silently rewritten.**

**WHAT WAS WRONG.** `?crownshadecard=0` was published at 6.59 and
`?crownshadefar=0` at 12.85. Neither reproduces on any build in any arm. On the
baseline the table's own header names they read **4.80** and **9.31** (verifier
twice, bit-identical repeats, once via `?canopysat=0.62` on this branch and once
on a from-scratch build of `bda72279`; re-taken here a third time and matching).
The published pair sits BETWEEN the arms, and interpolating in `sat` places them
at an effective canopy saturation of about 0.96 and 0.93 -- **mid-lane candidate
constants.** Both arms were captured during the constant search, after the first
candidate row had already been built, and were never re-taken against the
baseline the table claimed for them.

**WHAT IT CHANGES.** Corrected costs against 3.92: far paint **5.39** (was
8.93), card half **0.88** (was 2.67). **THE ORDERING FLIPS.** The record said
the card shade (2.67) outweighed `FoliageTone`'s desaturation (2.35); in fact
**`FoliageTone` outweighs the card shade by 2.7x**, and the true order is far
paint 5.39 > FoliageTone 2.35 > card 0.88. Three consequences, all applied
above: the lane's own lever is the second-largest term in the frame rather than
the third (2.31.2, and the `canopy` row's own comment); the routed follow-up is
re-sized and re-aimed at BOTH halves of RN-2275's shade rather than the card
alone (2.31.6); and the `?treeline=0` share in 2.31.5, taken in the same
contaminated window, is re-measured at **1.86 of 1.93** (it was published as
1.24 of 1.93).

**THE TRAP, and it is in the catalogue now (NUMBERS.md).** An arm table's header
names ONE build, and every row in it must come from that build in one session.
Rows taken mid-search against candidate constants do not fail loudly: they
interpolate to plausible-looking numbers that sit in the right order of
magnitude, keep the right sign, support the conclusion being drafted, and
reproduce nowhere. Nothing in this project's rails catches it, because every
individual capture was determinate, sentinel-verified and bit-identical on
repeat. The whole table in 2.31.2 has been re-taken in one session and the
header now says so.

**Four further corrections applied in the same pass.** (1) 2.31.5's FIELD
judgement is downgraded from MET to **PARTIAL**, scoped to the mid field: the

## 2.32 THE MID FIELD IS ABOUT FOUR AND A HALF ROWS, NOT FIFTEEN, AND THE PROP RING STANDS IN FRONT OF IT (RN-2510 to RN-2517, 2026-08-21, `lane/n4-midobjects`; corrected 2026-08-21, see 2.32.11)

> **Numbers:** RN-2510 to RN-2517 of the RN-2510 to RN-2524 block; RN-2518 to
> RN-2524 surrendered unused. **Base:** `origin/main` at `0d432bc1`.
> **Charter:** world audit R4's item **N4** as re-aimed by Admin after N1's
> verifier: "at 250 m and beyond, a real plain carries OBJECTS standing on it;
> ours carries nothing, and the ground meets the sky as an empty wash."
> **Frames:** `docs/screenshots/RN2510_*`.
>
> **THIS LANE SHIPS NO PIXEL CHANGE AND SAYS SO IN ITS FIRST LINE.** It ships a
> diagnosis that refutes its own charter's premise, one instrument, and three
> comment corrections. The term it built to satisfy the charter is in this
> branch's history at RN-2511 to RN-2515 and was refused at RN-2516 on its own
> numbers and its own frames.

### 2.32.1 THE ONE-LINE ANSWER

The plains mid field is **about four and a half frame rows** (was fifteen; a
wide-x row-mean smear misread the load-bearing 170 m rung, corrected in
2.32.11) between the biome-prop ring and the horizon, the instance tier places
**nothing at all** in the 380 m between `RADIUS_M` (170 m) and `CANOPY_NEAR_M`
(550 m), and at the pose the player actually stands in **the props inside the
ring stand up in front of most of those rows**. So the charter's premise is
half right and half site-blind: `midfield`, the pose it was reasoned from, declares `props: false`,
and at `meadowfield` the far plain is not empty, it is a dark speckled mat
under a near-black silhouette wall. **Nothing a terrain material can paint out
there is worth a lane**, and this lane proves that rather than asserting it.

### 2.32.2 RN-2510, THE POSE THE PREMISE CAME FROM TURNS THE SUBJECT OFF

`artframe.js`'s `midfield` row declares **`props: false`**. Its own manifest
note says so ("`midfield` is the right site and turns THE PROPS OFF, which is
exactly the layer being judged") and RN-2478 records the consequence ("its
250 m strip is 100 per cent terrain"). N1's `midfield.r250` and the eye verdict
in 2.30.9 that produced this lane's charter were both read on a pose from which
every object had been removed by declaration.

**The player's pose disagrees, and the arm is one flag.** At `meadowfield`,
same site, same range, props on:

| arm | `r250` iqr | `r250` luma |
|---|---:|---:|
| shipped | **47.44** | **96.70** |
| `?props=0` | 43.56 | 116.22 |
| `?canopy=0` | **47.43** | 96.71 |

The scatter at 250 m is worth **+3.88 counts of contrast and -19.52 of level**:
it is there, it is DARK, and it adds almost no structure. And `?canopy=0` --
`canopyProps` 2,870 to 0, `canopyRadiusM` 3,500 to 0 -- leaves that rectangle at
**47.43 against 47.44**, i.e. **not one pixel of the mid-field rectangle is
canopy**, so the tier above cannot be blamed for it either. Frames:
`RN2510_meadowfield_1x.png`, `RN2510_meadowfield_props0.png`, and the 5x crop
`RN2510_meadowfield_midband_5x.png`, which is the ugliest picture in this
section: a pepper of sub-pixel props on the ground and, above the horizon line,
a continuous wall of near-black and grey blobs and thin vertical slivers at
roughly uniform height. It reads as demolition rubble, not as distant copses.

### 2.32.3 RN-2511, WHICH ROW IS WHICH RANGE, AND IT IS THE MEASUREMENT THIS SITE NEVER HAD

`rangeRects` inverts a FLAT PLANE and RN-2479 measured that inversion an order
of magnitude out past 100 m at this site. So the shader's own `dist` was painted
as a step ladder (thresholds 85 / 170 / 340 / 620 / 1400 / 3000 m, 0.03 per step
into the bottom of the grade per 2.30.6's lesson) and read with a new per-row
profile, `tools/smoke/rn2510rows.mjs`. At `meadowfield`:

| ground range | frame row |
|---|---:|
| 85 m | **297.5** |
| 170 m | **281.3** (was 291, see 2.32.11) |
| 340 m | **278.5** |
| horizon | **~276** |

**The 170 m rung was misread.** The first pass took a wide-x row mean, and
iso-range contours curve upward toward the frame edges, so a wide window smears
the step across several rows. Read at a narrow centre column (`x` in [795,
805), ten pixels wide) instead, the 170 m rung sits at row **~281.3**, confirmed
three independent ways: a hue-coded range ladder, a hard binary paint that
saturates rows 279-280 with row 281 as the mixed boundary, and a flat-plane
inversion fit from this lane's own six committed `rangeM`/`extraPx` pairs (`f` =
779.4 px, pitch -12 degrees, eye 1.62 m), which predicts 85 m at row 299.5,
170 m at 291.8, 340 m at 288.0 and the horizon at 284.1. The wide-window 291 was
within a row of that flat-plane prediction, meaning the row-ladder instrument
this lane built to replace the flat-plane inversion had, at its load-bearing
rung, reproduced the flat-plane inversion's own number instead of measuring
independently of it.

**The whole visible plain past the prop ring is about four and a half rows**
(281.3 to 276; was fifteen, from 291 to 276) and the 170-to-340 m band -- the
one the charter is about -- is **about three** (281.3 to 278.5; was twelve and
a half). `meadowfield.r250` (rows 287-292) is measured coverage, not a straddle
claim: per-row fractions of the rectangle that fall past the ring (170 m), for
rows 287 through 292, are **0.290 / 0.259 / 0.231 / 0.204 / 0.181 / 0.168**,
i.e. **about 22 per cent of the rectangle is past the ring and about 78 per
cent is inside it**. RN-2478's caveat that the placement is reproducible and
not a survey is confirmed rather than contradicted. Frame:
`RN2510_paint_rangeladder_meadowfield.png`.

### 2.32.4 RN-2512, THE HOLE IN THE PLACEMENT LADDER, FROM SOURCE AND CONFIRMED BY ARM

Read off `ScatterTuning` and `Registry` and confirmed against 2.32.2's arms:

| tier | outer reach |
|---|---|
| ground-detail cards (`detail: true`) | `DETAIL_RADIUS_M` **78 m**, thinning from 30 m |
| biome props (tufts, flowers, shrub, pebbles) | `RADIUS_M` **170 m**, flat density, **HARD edge, no edge weight** |
| `TreeField` harvest trees | `TREE_RADIUS_M` 620 m, sparse at the Plains density |
| canopy impostors | `CANOPY_NEAR_M` **550 m** to `canopyReachM` = **1,400 m** at a 1.62 m eye |

**Between 170 m and 550 m the instance tier places nothing but the harvest
trees**, and 170 m is row 281.3 (was 291, see 2.32.11) while the horizon is row
276. The gap is real, it is exactly the mid field, and it is a hard step rather
than a fade.

### 2.32.5 RN-2513, THE FIELD THE CHARTER NAMED IS SATURATED AT THIS SITE

The charter pointed at "the CPU stand-field machinery the far-treeline work
established". That machinery is `ChunkCanopy.fillCanopyIndex`, which evaluates
world-gen's `canopyWeight` per terrain vertex and uploads it as `aCanopy`. It
cannot drive a ground mosaic here, and the reason is measured.

`canopyWeight` is `(CANOPY_FLOOR_W + (1 - CANOPY_FLOOR_W) * ramp(stand,
STAND_LO, STAND_HI)) * groveWeight(grove) * (1 - above)` (`ScatterTuning.ts:911`;
the floor rides the STAND factor, which is why the measured min is
`CANOPY_FLOOR_W` 0.10 x `GROVE_FLOOR_W` 0.12 = 0.012 and not 0; `GROVE_FLOOR_W`
at `ScatterTuning.ts:500` and `:458`): two hard thresholds plus a floor, so the
realised field is **bimodal**. Measured over 64 deterministic sites x a 64x64
lattice at 190 m, 262,144 samples: **mean 0.308214, sd 0.344924, min 0.012, max
1.000**. **This mean and sd are site-set dependent**: the 64-site list was
never published, and the verifier's own independent 64-site run read **mean
0.273283, sd 0.320050**, same min, same max, same emphatic bimodality. It is a
wood/no-wood decision and it is right to be.

Painted as a three-threshold ladder at the plains pose
(`RN2510_paint_standsaturated_midfield.png`), **every terrain row from the prop
ring to the horizon came back at the top step, flat to the digit across thirteen
rows** (r 142.00 / g 156.00 against an off level of 7.00). The observer stands
inside one closed stand and the whole mid field is inside it. A term referenced
to a saturated field has nothing to say exactly where it is needed.

The raw octaves UNDER the thresholds are usable and were used instead:
`0.65 * standAt + 0.35 * groveAt` is smooth, unimodal, **mean 0.500540, sd
0.122626, min 0.062, max 0.941**, and a three-step ladder painted at the same
pose puts one side of the frame below 0.35 and the other above 0.55, so the
field does vary across the band. That is the field RN-2514's term ran on.

### 2.32.6 RN-2514, A TERM BUILT AND REFUSED, AND THE THREE THINGS IT COST TO FIND OUT

The term: past `RADIUS_M`, the terrain carries the ground cover the instance
ring has stopped placing -- Beer-Lambert on a per-biome area index derived live
from `BIOME_PROPS`, in the carpet's own `ofFarCoverRotate`, modulated by the raw
stand field so it clumps where the copses are. `TerrainTreeline`'s mechanism one
range band in, on the file whose stated purpose is that the far ground must not
revert to the bare palette. It is complete, typechecked, flagged four ways and
exact under `?coverstand=0`. **It is refused.**

**The arm table originally reported here was headed "fresh process per arm, one
build"; it was in fact a one-session arm-table trap** (measuring arms against a
live, uncommitted working tree rather than committed HEAD -- the class this
file's own catalogue already names under "What actually proves a frozen build
is HEAD" and "The shared WORKING TREE is a collision surface too, so measure in
an isolated one"). The control (`?coverstand=0`) and the `meadowfield` endpoint
**do** reproduce at the recoverable commit `be22fd50`. **The three
`coverstandv` sweep arms below were taken on an UNCOMMITTED intermediate, the
mosaic form, and reproduce nowhere.** The verifier re-measured the committed
cover-layer form's own sweep at `be22fd50`:

| arm | `r250` iqr (as originally reported, mosaic form, uncommitted) | `r250` iqr (committed cover-layer form, `be22fd50`, verifier) |
|---|---:|---:|
| `?coverstand=0` (off) | 43.83 | **43.83** |
| `coverstandv=0.35` | 38.98 | **36.28** |
| `coverstandv=0.8` | 35.99 | **42.63** |
| `coverstandv=1.4` | 37.20 | **42.85** |

**The committed sweep is NOT monotonic**, unlike the mosaic-form numbers
originally reported (which read 43.83 -> 38.98 -> 35.99, monotonically the
wrong way). Every committed arm still reads below the off arm, so **the
refusal's direction survives** even though the mosaic-form ladder that
motivated it does not.

**The record does not establish whether these sweep arms predate the
`TREE_SIN_MIN` discovery in lesson 3 below** (`TerrainTreeline`'s 0.02 rad floor
binds across the whole mid field at a 1.62 m eye). On either form, the sweep
numbers may have measured a floored constant rather than the term itself. **The
load-bearing evidence for the refusal is the eye verdict** (no difference
visible at 1x, either pose) **plus the corrected about-four-and-a-half-row
geometry in 2.32.3**, not the sweep amplitude numbers above. A future lane
resurrecting the term at `be22fd50` must re-derive the sweep on the committed
form with the floor's state recorded, rather than trust either published
sweep.

At `meadowfield` the final cover-layer form reads `r250` **47.44 -> 40.77** and
luma 96.70 -> 93.02: contrast down 6.7 counts. By eye at 1x, in both poses,
**no difference is visible**, and the crop says why: the mid field is about
four and a half rows (2.32.3, corrected) and the prop ring's own instances
stand in front of most of them.

**Three things were paid for on the way and all three are reusable.**

1. **A term inside `TerrainFragAlbedo`'s splat region never reaches the plains
   far ground.** Lines 118 to 340 of that file are one `#ifndef OF_SCALED`
   block; a magenta paint inside the term left the whole band under the horizon
   unpainted while the ground nearer than it went magenta. Moving the block
   between the horizon and treeline blocks, unguarded, painted the band from the
   ring to the horizon (`RN2510_paint_ring_midfield.png`). This is
   `MASSIF_FADE_M`'s own note one term over and it is why RN-2475's gain reached
   this band and a term written beside RN-2195's could not.
2. **A saturating law is the wrong carrier for a mosaic at a grazing view.**
   Painting the mosaic as the difference of two Beer-Lambert cover fractions is
   the tidier statement; at 0.005 depression it compresses a field ranging 0.30
   to 0.60 into a rectangle reading LESS contrast. Keep saturation as a GATE
   (a plain seen edge-on IS a mat of vegetation) and ride the mosaic linearly.
3. **`TREE_SIN_MIN` (0.02 rad) is an AERIAL constant.** It was derived where the
   ground's own depression at the horizon is 1.81 degrees so the floor never
   binds. At a 1.62 m eye the depression at 300 m is 0.0054 and that floor would
   bind across the entire mid field, silently replacing the measurement with the
   constant. Any surface-range term reusing the treeline's law needs its own
   floor and it should be numerical only.

### 2.32.7 RN-2515, THE THREE STALE COMMENTS, AND THEY ARE FIXED

### 2.32.8 THE EYE, AGAINST FIDELITY-GAP SECTION 1

**There is no reference board in this repository.** `FIDELITY-GAP` section 3
Option D asks every graphics lane to ship a side-by-side against two or three
frozen Space Engineers frames; no such file exists under `docs/`, and this lane
may not download one. So the comparison is against section 1's NUMBERED
DIFFERENCES in words, which is R4's own stated method, and the frames shipped
are `RN2510_meadowfield_1x.png` at 1x and `RN2510_meadowfield_midband_5x.png` at
the 250 m band. **A frozen board is owed to Admin and is named in 2.32.10.**

**Closed: none. Partially closed: none. Not touched: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.** This
lane changes no pixel. What it can say about the frame it photographed:

* **Difference 5 (vegetation assets) is the binding constraint at this site,
  not difference 2 (materials).** At 1x the plains mid field's character is set
  entirely by what STANDS in it: a pepper of sub-pixel prop cards and a
  near-black silhouette wall of uniform height on the horizon line. The ground
  under them is about four and a half rows (was fifteen, see 2.32.11) and
  mostly hidden.
* **Difference 1's complaint is inverted out here.** At the feet the ground is a
  table with objects on it; at 200 m to 1 km it is objects with no ground
  visible between them, and the objects are the wrong ones.
* N1's PARTIAL verdict at 2.30.9 stands and its third residue ("a real plain
  carries objects standing on it -- that is `TerrainCoverFar`'s stand field")
  is **withdrawn as stated**: `TerrainCoverFar` has no stand field, the machinery
  that does is saturated here, and the objects are already standing there.

### 2.32.10 OWED, AND WHERE THE NEXT LANE SHOULD BE POINTED

1. **THE ITEM AS BRIEFED CANNOT BE DONE IN A TERRAIN MATERIAL, and this is the
   finding to act on.** The plains mid field is about four and a half rows
   (2.32.3, corrected; was fifteen) with the near prop ring standing in front of
   it. What changes it is what has HEIGHT at 200 m to
   1 km: the 170-to-550 m placement hole, the near-black uniform silhouette wall
   the far canopy impostors make, and the pepper. All three are the INSTANCE
   tier's, and two of them are partly N3's (`FoliageTone`, `PropSkyAmbient`) and
   one is world-gen's (`RADIUS_M`).
2. **A frozen SE reference board does not exist in the repository** and Option D
   has therefore never been executable as written. Every lane since
   FIDELITY-GAP has substituted "my own knowledge of what an SE frame looks
   like". Admin's, not a lane's.
3. **A rectangle for the 170-to-550 m hole, re-derived from the corrected
   ladder (2.32.3).** `meadowfield.r250` (rows 287-292) is about 78 per cent
   inside the ring and about 22 per cent past it, so it can never cleanly
   separate "the ring stopped" from "the ground out there is bare". On the
   CORRECTED ladder (170 m at row 281.3, 340 m at row 278.5), rows 278-284 span
   roughly 340 m at the top to about 150 m at the bottom, a good frame for the
   170-to-550 m question. On the OLD, uncorrected ladder (170 m misread as row
   291) that same rectangle would have contained sky above the horizon, the
   `meadow.hzBand` failure mode. Whoever commits this rectangle must derive its
   placement from their own corrected centre-column ladder and commit the
   measured range beside it, not reuse this lane's numbers unverified.
4. **The term is not lost.** RN-2511 to RN-2515 in this branch's history is a
   complete, typechecked implementation with its own flags and its own drift
   guard, and 2.32.6's three lessons are why it would be cheaper to resurrect
   than to rewrite. It should only be resurrected for a pose whose mid field is
   actually VISIBLE ground -- a raised eye, a slope, or an aerial -- and none of
   those is the plains hero frame. **The record does not establish whether the
   refused term's sweep arms (2.32.6) predate the `TREE_SIN_MIN` discovery**
   (its 0.02 rad floor binds across the whole mid field at a 1.62 m eye), so the
   next lane resurrecting this term must re-derive the sweep on the committed
   form with the floor's state recorded rather than trust either published
   sweep.

### 2.32.11 Correction pass (2026-08-21, fresh-context verifier, verdict FIX doc-only, applied by mini-lane)

A fresh-context verifier confirmed this lane's refutation of its own charter
and every headline arm in 2.32.2 exactly, and found one instrument defect in
the new row-ladder instrument (2.32.3): iso-range contours curve upward at the
frame edges, so a wide-x row mean smears the step, and the load-bearing 170 m
rung was misread as a result. The corrections below were routed by that
verifier and applied here by a correction mini-lane, doc-only, without touching
code, frames, or any other file.

1. **The 170 m rung is row ~281.3 (was 291).** Confirmed three ways: a
   narrow-centre-column (`x` in [795, 805)) hue ladder, a hard binary paint
   (rows 279-280 saturate, row 281 is the mixed boundary), and a flat-plane
   inversion fit from this lane's own six committed `rangeM`/`extraPx` pairs
   (`f` = 779.4 px, pitch -12, eye 1.62 m), which predicted 170 m at row 291.8 --
   within a row of the old, wrong 291, i.e. the row-ladder instrument had
   reproduced the flat-plane number it was built to replace. Downstream: the
   section title and 2.32.1's "fifteen frame rows" is corrected to **about four
   and a half** (281.3 to 276, was fifteen); 2.32.3's "twelve and a half" rows
   for the 170-to-340 m band is corrected to **about three** (281.3 to 278.5,
   was twelve and a half); 2.32.4's "170 m is row 291" is corrected to **row
   281.3**; 2.32.10 item 1's "fifteen rows" and 2.32.8's difference-5 bullet

## 2.33 THE CROWN SHADE GOES SPECTRAL (RN-2525 to RN-2539, 2026-08-21, `lane/n6-crownshade`)

> N3's routed follow-up (2.31.6 item 1), corrected sizing: far paint 5.39
> counts of `forestair` box gx, card 0.88, joint 6.38. Base `origin/main` at
> `7d415332`. Branch `lane/n6-crownshade`, pushed, **not merged to main**.
> Server `127.0.0.1:5525`, `--strictPort`, sentinel `dist/of-sentinel-rn2525.txt`
> written into this worktree's own `dist` and fetched back over the port
> before every server was trusted (three builds, each re-verified: the first
> lacked `dist/wasm` because `npx vite build` alone skips `sync-wasm`/
> `sync-assets`, NUMBERS.md's own scar; the final two reproduce to the digit,
> which is also a determinism check across a full clean rebuild). Killed by
> the PID `netstat -ano` named each time (26268, 15584, 27764, all confirmed
> gone). `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vite build` and `npm run check` run as
> SEPARATE steps, each exit status read on its own: 0, 0, **8 of 8**.

### 2.33.1 THE DEFECT, RESTATED FROM WHERE N3 LEFT IT

`CanopySelfShadow.updateCanopyCardShade` and `TerrainTreeline.glsl.ts`'s
albedo block both multiplied the finalised, already-coloured canopy tone by
ONE achromatic scalar `S` (RN-2275's own inter-crown self-shadow law,
unchanged by this lane). A tenth of any colour reads as dark blue-violet on
this engine's tonemap before it is anything else, which is what four audits
and N3 both photographed. Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light far more
strongly than green, so an achromatic Beer-Lambert multiply is the wrong
spectral model for a leaf mass: a crown deep in its own shadow should read as
a saturated dark GREEN, not a neutral dark grey.

### 2.33.2 THE FIX: ONE SCALAR BECOMES A PINNED TRIPLE

`CanopySelfShadow.crownSpectralSplit(s)` (TypeScript) and
`ofCrownSpectralSplit(s)` (GLSL, in the new `CROWN_SPECTRAL_GLSL` export,
spliced beside `CROWN_SELF_GLSL` in `TerrainTreeline.glsl.ts`'s pars block)
take RN-2275's own scalar `S` -- unchanged, still one law, still one triple
`(amp, K, floor)` -- and split it into a per-channel triple:

```
shade_c = S ^ k_c                              (one exponent per channel)
M       = LUMA . (shade_red, shade_green, shade_blue)   (Rec.709 weights)
shade_c(final) = S * shade_c / M
```

**THE EXPONENTS ARE A DELIBERATE STYLISATION FOR VISIBLE EFFECT, NOT A
PHYSICAL DERIVATION -- this section originally said "derived rather than
picked", and that claim was wrong, caught by a fresh-context verifier.**
FoliageTone.ts documents the leaf's REFLECTANCE triple `r` (0.05 red, 0.12
green, 0.04 blue) and single-scattering ALBEDO triple `w` (0.08 red, 0.27
green, 0.06 blue); transmittance `t = w - r` = 0.03 red / 0.15 green / 0.02
blue was carried through the WRONG relation. Beer-Lambert optical depth is
`tau = -ln(T)`, not `1/T`, and the shipped exponents are proportional to
`1/t_c`, not to `tau_c`:

```
shipped (WAS chosen, not derived):
  k_c = cbrt(t_red * t_green * t_blue) / t_c
      = 1.493802 red,  0.298760 green,  2.240702 blue

honest Beer-Lambert (tau_c = -ln(t_c), same geometric-mean normalisation):
  = 1.183283 red,  0.640180 green,  1.320107 blue

two-stream (k(w) = 2*sqrt(1-w_c), FoliageTone.ts's own rInf model, same
normalisation):
  = 1.035589 red,  0.922476 green,  1.046785 blue
```

The DIRECTION every reference agrees on (green below one, red and blue
above it) is what the leaf optics support; the shipped MAGNITUDE is 2.71x
more aggressive than Beer-Lambert and about 15x more than two-stream, and
that magnitude is an art choice wearing a physics costume. **KEPT ON
PURPOSE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED:** the verifier built, measured and
reverted the honest Beer-Lambert alternative -- it closes only 40.9 per cent
of the `crowns` gx shortfall against the shipped 65.8 (2.33.4), and buys
back only 0.47 counts of RN-2275's tightest guard margin (`forestairnoon`,
-1.76 shipped -> -2.23 Beer-Lambert). The eye verdict is already PARTIAL at
the stronger, shipped setting (2.33.7), so weakening it would not flip
anything. The fix here is to the LABEL, not the constant.

**WHAT THE GEOMETRIC-MEAN NORMALISATION ACTUALLY BUYS, since "product
1.000000" is not the check an earlier draft called it.** Dividing any three
positive numbers by their own geometric mean always gives a product of
exactly one, by definition, so that identity validates nothing about `t_c`;
it only confirms the division happened. The non-trivial property is
different: the pinned `shade_c` (2.33.3) is EXACTLY invariant under an
ADDITIVE shift of all three `k_c` by the same constant, so WHERE the triple
is centred is a free gauge and buys no correctness. What the geometric-mean
choice actually sets is the absolute SCALE the triple's SPREAD sits at (the
"aggressiveness knob"): dividing by a smaller reference would have scaled
every `k_c` up together and crushed red and blue harder at every `S`. It
does not enforce the pin -- the pin holds unconditionally for any three
exponents, by the `/ M` step alone.

### 2.33.3 THE PIN, STATED PRECISELY, BECAUSE THE LOOSE VERSION IS A CLAIM THIS LANE DOES NOT MAKE

`LUMA_R*shade_red + LUMA_G*shade_green + LUMA_B*shade_blue` collapses
algebraically to `S` for every value of `S`, not measured, not swept, an
identity (the same divide-and-recombine `FoliageTone.applyFoliageTone`'s
saturation term uses, generalised from weights summing to one to a ratio
that cancels exactly). **CONFIRMED LIVE** at `forestairnoon` via the probe
surface `canopySelfNow()` now publishes (`cardShadeRGB`, `spectral`):
`cardShadeRGB` (0.014397, 0.171380, 0.003062) against `cardShade` 0.125853,
and `0.2126*0.014397 + 0.7152*0.171380 + 0.0722*0.003062 = 0.125853` to the
digit.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM, and an early draft of this lane's own code
comments did.** The pin is on the SHADE TRIPLE's own weighted mean, not on
`base_c * shade_c`'s. A crown's base colour is not neutral (green is its
largest channel and the channel this term crushes least), so the RENDERED
pixel runs measurably brighter than the achromatic law's own prediction:
same site, `base . shadeRGB` linear luma is 0.02101 against `base_luma * S`
= 0.01704, about +0.004 linear. What the pin actually buys is that this
drift is SMALL and bounded, not that it is zero, which is why 2.33.4 below
RE-MEASURES RN-2275's four pairs rather than trusting the algebra alone to
protect them.

`?crownspectral=0` sets every `k_c` to 1: `shade_c = S*S/S = S` for all three
channels by the same identity, which is the exact pre-lane achromatic frame
algebraically rather than a second code path. Registered in `run.mjs`'s
`PAGE_PARAMS` in this commit.

### 2.33.9 Correction pass (2026-08-21, fresh-context verifier, verdict FIX doc-only) and owed items

**A fresh-context verifier reproduced every MEASUREMENT this lane published**
(the identity claim held at pixel level below the same-build noise floor,
`pinResidual` literally 0, all four guard margins to the digit, the 65.8 per
cent closure exact, scatter proven two orders of magnitude below the
tightest -1.76 margin) **and found the DERIVATION CLAIM wrong.** 2.33.2's
"derived from FoliageTone.ts's own leaf optics rather than picked" carried
the leaf transmittance triple through `k_c` proportional to `1/t_c`; Beer-
Lambert optical depth is `tau = -ln(T)`, not `1/T`. Carried through the
correct relation the honest exponents are 1.183283/0.640180/1.320107
(Beer-Lambert) or 1.035589/0.922476/1.046785 (two-stream, `FoliageTone.ts`'s
own `rInf` model), against the shipped 1.493802/0.298760/2.240702 -- the
shipped magnitude is 2.71x more aggressive than Beer-Lambert. **THE
EXPONENTS ARE KEPT**: the verifier measured the honest alternative (patched,
built, measured, reverted) and it closes only 40.9 per cent of the shortfall
against the shipped 65.8, buying back 0.47 counts of guard margin the eye
verdict (already PARTIAL at the stronger setting) does not need. The fix is
to the LABEL: 2.33.2 and `CanopySelfShadow.ts`'s header now call the
exponents a deliberate stylisation with the physical references named
beside them, not a derivation. The "product 1.000000" line was also wrong as
a validation claim (a geometric-mean divide always gives that product, by
definition); the real property is that the pinned output is invariant under
an ADDITIVE shift of the whole `k_c` triple, which is why the geometric mean
sets the split's aggressiveness rather than its correctness. **The NUMBERS
RN-2525 row's "derived rather than picked" is corrected the same way.**

**OWED, from the verifier, added here so they are not lost:**

1. **THE RESIDUAL IS AN ADDITIVE BLUE FLOOR THIS SEAM CANNOT REACH.** With
   the shade fully OFF (`?crownshade=0`), crown blue moves only +2.27 counts
   while green moves +15.73 -- the shaded crown's blue channel gets 0.3 per
   cent of its value from the base albedo this lane's multiply acts on, yet
   blue is the crown PIXEL's largest channel. The blue-violet residual is
   therefore not a multiplicative term at all: it is additive, most likely
   the aerial in-scatter and/or the blue-dominant ambient daylight floor
   (`TerrainAmbient`'s `AMBIENT_NOON` (0.048, 0.058, 0.084)). **The next
   crown-colour lane must target the ADDITIVE term, a different owner
   (aerial perspective / ambient fill), because no multiply on the canopy's
   own albedo can reach a floor that is added after it.**
2. **RN-2275'S PASS CONDITION IS A SIGN TEST WITH NO BUDGET.** "The wood
   must read darker than its own clearing" has no stated margin floor, and

   pass (-2.80 pre-lane to -1.76 shipped, 2.33.5). A sign test with no
   budget will eventually flip under enough small, individually-justified
   moves; a stated minimum margin is owed before the next lane bites this

## 2.34 THE ADDITIVE BLUE FLOOR IS THE AIR, AND THE CROWN IS AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE TOO DIM TO SURVIVE IT (RN-2540 to RN-2549, 2026-08-21, `lane/n7-bluefloor`)

> N6's routed follow-up (2.33.9 item 1). Base `origin/main` at `8e19d294`.
> Branch `lane/n7-bluefloor`, pushed, **not merged to main**. Server
> `127.0.0.1:5540`, `--strictPort`, sentinel `dist/of-sentinel-rn2540.txt`
> written into this worktree's own `dist` and fetched back over the port before
> any server was trusted (five builds, each re-verified with a distinct token,
> each killed by the PID `netstat -ano` named: 25004, 24292, 27056, 23196,
> 13688, all confirmed gone). `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vite build` and
> `cd web && npm run check` run as SEPARATE steps, each exit status read on its
> own: 0, 0, **8 of 8**.
>
> **THIS LANE SHIPS NO PIXEL CHANGE.** Every committed rectangle at every
> measured pose is bit-identical between a from-scratch build of the pre-lane
> source and the lane build, proved by the pair in 2.34.7 rather than argued
> from the algebra. What it ships is FOUR NEW ISOLATORS and a diagnosis.

### 2.34.1 THE ONE-LINE ANSWER

At the committed `crowns` rectangle at `forestair`, **91.9 per cent of the
crown card's own blue is AERIAL IN-SCATTER added over it, and 0.03 per cent is
its albedo.** The card's whole diffuse contribution to a 32.05-count blue pixel
is **0.01 counts**; the aerial floor's is **29.44**. The floor is applied to the
crown and to the ground it stands on by the SAME model at the SAME range, and
across the whole plausible card-coverage range their per-pixel floors stay the
same size, so **nothing is imbalanced between the two surfaces** (2.34.4 states
what the data can and cannot resolve there). The floor's colour is Rayleigh's
own and its magnitude
is what this atmosphere's own published constants require at 2.3 to 2.9 km.
**THE BLUE IS PHYSICALLY RIGHT AND THE CROWNS NEED MORE GREEN LIGHT**, and
2.34.6 prices exactly how much of that light RN-2275's guard can afford: not
enough, by a factor of several.

**THE CHARTER'S OWN NAMED SUSPECT IS REFUTED.** `TerrainAmbient`'s blue-dominant
daylight floor (`AMBIENT_NOON` (0.048, 0.058, 0.084), blue/green 1.448) costs
the crown's blue **0.69 counts of 80.67**, and the whole ambient family
(`?ambientfill=0` 0.69, `?terrainfloor=0` 0.33, `?skyirr=0` 0.39, `?propsky=0`
0.00) is under a count and a half between them.

### 2.34.2 THE INSTRUMENTS HAD TO COME FIRST, AND TWO OF THE FOUR ARE RN-952's LESSON

Three things had to exist before an attribution was possible, and their absence
is why the routed finding was a suspicion rather than a number.

**1. A PER-CHANNEL READOUT.** `rn2495arms.mjs` publishes green excess, which is
the right instrument for "is the crown green" and cannot see an ADDITIVE term:
`gx`, `warm` and `luma` have already collapsed the three channels into
differences. `web/tools/smoke/rn2540arms.mjs` prints the probe's own raw triple
beside them, on the same runner, the same committed `artframe.js` rectangles and
the same fresh-process-per-call-site rule, so a row from it and a row from
`rn2495arms.mjs` are on one scale.

**2. AN ISOLATOR FOR THE TERRAIN'S HALF OF EVERY CROWN RECTANGLE.** The props'
aerial perspective had `?prophaze=`. The TERRAIN's copy of the same two calls
(`TerrainFragLight.glsl.ts`, the same arguments in the same order) had NOTHING
except the global `?atmos=0`, which deletes the sky with it and is the
contaminated control A4's verifier already threw out (2.12.2). Since the far
treeline PAINT rides the terrain fragment and the cards ride the prop one, half
of every crown rectangle in this project could be neither charged nor
exonerated. `?terrainhaze=` is that isolator, `mix`-shaped exactly like
`?prophaze=` so 1 is the shipped frame by algebra.

**3. A PAINT ARM, BECAUSE AN AMPLITUDE CANNOT SPLIT `col * T + Lin`.** Turning
haze off removes the extinction AND the in-scatter together, so `?prophaze=0`
prices both halves at once and cannot say which one carries a channel.
`?terrainpaint=1` and `?proppaint=1` set the SOURCE RADIANCE to zero and leave
the identical two calls in place, so the fragment renders exactly `Lin` on the
real geometry at the real range through the real phase function. Two arms and
one subtraction then split the term with no model in between.

**4. AND THE ONE THE LADDER ITSELF SURFACED.** With the terrain painted black
and the props' haze off, the card's own un-hazed pixel still read blue
(2.31, 4.11, **3.10**) -- and the card's diffuse blue cannot do that, because
`cardShadeRGB.b` is **0.0017** (read live, 2.34.4). The only radiance on a stock
physical program that is NOT multiplied by the albedo is `totalSpecular`,
three's own sun lobe plus the sky PMREM lobe, and **it had no switch of any
kind**: `?terrainspec=` is the terrain's and reaches no prop, and
`envMapIntensity` has no page parameter anywhere in the project. RN-952's lesson
is that a term with no switch is the one candidate no experiment can eliminate,
so `?propspec=` was built before the conclusion was written. It replaces three's
own `vec3 outgoingLight = totalDiffuse + totalSpecular + totalEmissiveRadiance;`
line with the same line times one uniform, and reports a MISS on its own anchor
if a three upgrade ever rewrites it.

All four are registered in `run.mjs`'s `PAGE_PARAMS` **in the commit that
introduces them** and all four are readable back live through
`web/tools/smoke/rn2540state.mjs`, which is RN-2268's scar: a flag that never
reaches a uniform reports the default and the table describes the default as the
request. Read at the arm: `terrainHaze 0 / terrainPaint 1 / propPaint 1 /
propSpec 0` with all four `flags` true, `propsky.spliced 30`, `folPrograms 15`,
`misses []`, `props:OF_Canopy:canopy` in `chained`.

### 2.34.4 THE CROWN PIXEL, DECOMPOSED, AND THE ALBEDO IS 0.03 PER CENT OF IT

The two paint arms compose into a complete split of the rectangle, because a
card pixel is either card or ground (the cards are alpha-tested, so there is no
partial coverage to smear the mean). `?terrainpaint=1+terrainhaze=0` renders the
terrain EXACTLY black, leaving `f x card`; `?proppaint=1+prophaze=0` renders the
cards exactly black, leaving `(1-f) x ground`. Both are coverage-weighted and
neither needs `f` to be known.

**THE CLOSURE CHECK FIRST, because the split is worthless if it does not
close:** the two complementary arms sum to (63.51, 75.33, 80.32) against the
shipped rectangle's (64.01, 75.98, 80.67), i.e. **within 0.65 counts on every
channel**, 0.4 per cent. The residual is alpha-tested edge pixels plus the post
chain's neighbourhood operators, and it is quoted rather than assumed away.
**The verifier's own observation on it, worth keeping:** the residual is
NEGATIVE on all three channels (the parts sum to LESS than the whole, deltas
0.50 / 0.65 / 0.35), which is the signature of edge pixels and post rather than
of a third surface. An unattributed surface inside the rectangle would make the
parts sum to less than the whole only by being present in neither arm, and both
arms paint one surface black while leaving everything else alone, so a missing
contributor would show as a POSITIVE residual. It does not.

| | r | g | b |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **CARD half** (`terrainpaint=1+terrainhaze=0`) | 21.36 | 25.50 | **32.05** |
| its aerial floor alone (`+proppaint=1`) | 17.78 | 20.76 | **29.44** |
| its own radiance (`+prophaze=0`) | 2.31 | 4.11 | 3.10 |
| its own DIFFUSE alone (`+prophaze=0+propspec=0`) | **0.01** | **1.00** | **0.01** |
| **GROUND half** (`proppaint=1+prophaze=0`) | 42.15 | 49.83 | 48.27 |
| its aerial floor alone (`+terrainpaint=1`) | 26.56 | 30.61 | 42.79 |
| its own radiance (`+terrainhaze=0`) | 14.13 | 21.68 | 10.11 |

**THE CARD'S SHARE OF ITS OWN PIXEL: blue 29.44 of 32.05 is the floor (91.9 per
cent), green 20.76 of 25.50 (81.4 per cent), red 17.78 of 21.36 (83.2 per
cent).** The crown's DIFFUSE ALBEDO -- the thing every crown-colour lane in this
file has multiplied -- contributes **one count of green and one hundredth of a
count of blue** to that pixel. That is the cap, and it is arithmetic: a term
that reaches 3 per cent of a pixel cannot decide its hue, whatever colour it is.
It also explains N6's PARTIAL exactly: `cardShadeRGB` is read live at
(0.009231, 0.140415, **0.001684**), so the card is already almost perfectly
blue-free by construction and could make no difference to the pixel's blue.

**THE TWO SURFACES ARE CONSISTENT WITHIN THE COVERAGE UNCERTAINTY, AND THE DATA
CANNOT RESOLVE A DIFFERENCE OR ITS SIGN. CORRECTED 2026-08-21 BY A
FRESH-CONTEXT VERIFIER; an earlier draft of this paragraph said "within 8 per
cent, and in the right direction", which is true at ONE value of `f` and not
across the range this lane itself quotes.** Converting either half to a
per-pixel radiance needs the card coverage `f`, and `f` is only recoverable
from these same arms as a per-channel estimate: **0.436 red, 0.404 green,
0.421 blue** (from `1 - rect(cards black) / rect(canopy=0)`) -- **CHANNEL LABELS
CORRECTED 2026-08-21 BY LANE N8 (RN-2550), on the nit the RN-2540 verifier
recorded for the guard lane; an earlier draft read "0.404 blue, 0.420 green,
0.436 red", transposing green and blue and quoting the set's own MEAN in place
of blue. Arithmetic, from this section's own two tables: red 1 - 42.15/74.73 =
0.436, green 1 - 49.83/83.60 = 0.404, blue 1 - 48.27/83.34 = 0.421. The VALUE
SET is unchanged to the digit and every conclusion below stands**, since the
mean is 0.420 either way and the range endpoints 0.404 and 0.436 are the same
two numbers -- a spread the gaps'
own neighbour-shadowing explains and the arms cannot narrow. At the mean 0.420
the per-pixel floors are (42.3, 49.4, 70.1) on the cards against (45.8, 52.8,
73.8) on the ground, an 8 per cent gap; **at `f` = 0.404 the blue comparison
REVERSES and at `f` = 0.436 the two sit 13 per cent apart**, so the sign of the
difference is not determined and quoting the 8 per cent as a result is
circular, since the `f` it rests on came out of the arms being compared.

**WHAT THE DATA DOES SUPPORT, and it is what 2.34.1 claims:** across the whole
plausible coverage range the card's floor and the ground's floor stay the same
size, so **nothing is imbalanced between the two surfaces** and no part of the
crown's blue can be charged to the prop splice diverging from the terrain's
model. The prop splice's own comment claims it is "the SAME TWO CALLS in the
same order with the same arguments" as `TerrainFragLight.glsl.ts:198-210`; the
measurement is consistent with that and cannot refute it. Resolving the
difference and its sign needs an independent coverage measurement (a card
painted to a known non-black constant, one more arm) or the linear readout of
2.34.10 item 3, and neither is in this lane.

### 2.34.5 IS THE FLOOR TOO BRIGHT? NO, AND THE MODEL'S OWN CONSTANTS SAY SO

The obvious next move is to accuse the aerial term of being over-strength, and
it is wrong. Three independent readings agree.

**THE OPTICAL DEPTH.** The `crowns` rectangle is solved from the pose the way
RN-2265 solves its handover bands: a 1,200 m eye, 60 degree vertical field,
14 degree pitch, so rows 600 and 700 look down at 24.90 and 31.79 degrees and
hit ground at **2,585 m and 1,936 m, slant 2,850 m and 2,278 m**. Against
`aerosolSigma` 1.4e-4 (RN-2175's own note calls it "a Koschmieder visual range
of 27.9 km", and 3.912 / 1.4e-4 is 27.9 km, so the note checks) and Earth's
`betaR` (5.8e-6, 13.5e-6, 33.1e-6), the optical depth over that slant is about
**0.19 blue and 0.16 green**, i.e. a transmittance of about 0.83 and an
airlight share `1 - T` of about **0.17**. **The aerosol half of that is the
one that needs the 400 m scale height stated, not assumed away:** the layer is
referenced to the observer's own ground altitude (`ofAtmoAerial`'s `uAeroRef`,
RN-2175), the eye is 1,200 m above it, so the density along the ray runs from
`exp(-1200/400)` = 0.050 at the camera to 1.0 where it lands, and the
path-mean over a 2.3-to-2.9 km slant is roughly 0.3, giving an aerosol column
of order 700 to 800 m of full-density air and an aerosol od near **0.10**. The
Rayleigh half at 5.6 km scale height is near full density throughout and adds
about **0.08 blue**. A verifier re-derived the pair from the constants and
agreed.

**THE MEASURED SHARE.** `?terrainpaint=1` renders the airlight at every range in
one frame. At `hzBand` -- the near-horizon band, where the path is long enough
that `T` has gone and the airlight IS the equilibrium radiance -- it reads
(178.45, 166.49, 150.08) against the shipped ground's (180.13, 173.86, 150.63),
i.e. the far ground is **99 per cent airlight**, which is what an infinite path
must give. At `crowns` the ground half's per-pixel floor is 73.8 blue against
that 150.08: **0.49 in 8-bit, and 0.15 to 0.22 once the sRGB encode is undone**
(ACES compresses the bright end, so the true linear ratio is at the bottom of
that range). **That is `1 - T` at 2.5 km, to the precision an 8-bit frame can
carry.** The model is doing Koschmieder correctly.

**THE FLOOR'S HUE.** `betaR`'s own blue-to-green ratio is 2.45; the measured
per-pixel floor's is 1.42 in 8-bit, which is 2.45 seen through the tone curve.
It is Rayleigh's colour because it is Rayleigh.

**SO NO FIX BELONGS ON THE AERIAL TERM.** It is the M1 horizon dissolve, it is
calibrated to a clear day rather than a hazy one, and at the crowns it is
delivering the physically-required 15-to-20 per cent veil. What is wrong is on
the other side of the addition.

### 2.34.6 WHAT THE GUARD CAN AFFORD, PRICED, AND IT IS NOT ENOUGH

If the crown needs more green light, the question is how much RN-2275's sign
test will allow. `?crownshadefloor=` sweeps `CROWN_SELF_FLOOR` (shipped 0.08),
which is the knob the shade is actually limited by at high sun -- RN-2275's own
header says the exponential is 0.016 at K = 3.2, so a closed wood at noon is
FLOOR-limited, not K-limited. Same build, same session; the `?canopy=0` clearing
at `forestairnoon` reads 110.27 at every floor value, to the digit.

| `crownshadefloor` | `forestairnoon` wood - clearing | `crowns` gx | `crowns` blue |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **0.08 (shipped)** | **-1.76** | +3.64 | 80.67 |
| 0.16 | **-0.27** | +5.39 | 80.70 |
| 0.30 | **+2.14, FLIPPED** | +7.94 | 80.79 |

**THE GUARD FLIPS BETWEEN 2x AND 3.75x, AND THE CROWN'S BLUE MOVES 0.12 COUNTS
ACROSS THE WHOLE SWEEP.** That is the cap stated as an experiment rather than as
arithmetic: you can spend RN-2275's entire remaining margin, break the guard,
brighten the crown by nearly four times, and the thing the eye is complaining
about does not move. Holding a margin of about -1.0 (half of what is left) buys
`crownshadefloor` about 0.115 and **gx +0.8 of N3's 2.69-count gap to the
clearing, under a third of it.**

Two facts make it worse for the "just brighten the crown" route. First, the
margin is not an artefact of the haze: measured with BOTH aerial terms off, the
same four pairs read **-1.67 / -2.74 / -10.93 / -3.04** against the shipped
**-1.76 / -1.99 / -7.31 / -1.83**, so the un-hazed frame's margins are the same
size or LARGER and the guard has real signal in it. It is genuinely thin at
`forestairnoon`, for RN-2275's own stated reason. Second, the crown is not
mis-tuned by a little: **its diffuse radiance sits AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE below
the ground's** at the same pose, where the real-world analogue is a factor of
two to three.

**BOTH HALVES OF THAT SENTENCE NEED THEIR METHOD NAMED, and an earlier draft
gave a single figure ("34x") without one; corrected by a fresh-context
verifier.** The renderer figure is the CARD's DIFFUSE alone against the
GROUND's TOTAL, per-pixel (each half divided by its own coverage), sRGB-decoded
with the piecewise toe: **26x to 34x depending on how the near-black decode and
the coverage are taken**, which is why it is quoted as an order of magnitude
rather than as a number. It is also not a like-for-like ratio (diffuse against
total), so it is an **UPPER** bound on how dark the crown is, not a lower one.
**BOUND DIRECTION CORRECTED 2026-08-21 BY LANE N8 (RN-2550), on the nit the
RN-2540 verifier recorded for the guard lane; this sentence said "a LOWER
bound".** The numerator is the crown's DIFFUSE alone while the denominator is
the ground's TOTAL, and the crown's own total is far larger than its diffuse
(2.34.10 item 2: `totalSpecular` is 99.7 per cent of the card's own blue and 76
per cent of its own green), so a like-for-like total-against-total ratio is
SMALLER than 26x-to-34x. The figure therefore overstates the darkness, which
makes it an upper bound. **The direction does not weaken the finding**: even the
like-for-like ratio stays far above the visible-band 2x-to-3x below, and it is
the reason the fix is a roughness correction paired with a raise rather than a
deletion.

**THE REAL-WORLD FIGURE IS A VISIBLE-BAND RATIO AND HAS TO BE.** Conifer canopy
against green grass is about **2.1x** broadband-visible, and a closed canopy in
the GREEN band specifically runs about **1.8x to 3.3x**. The broadband ALBEDO
ratio for a deciduous summer canopy against a meadow is only about **1.2x to
1.4x**, and that number is the wrong analogue here: roughly half the solar
energy is in the near infrared, where a canopy is highly reflective and grass
less so, and this renderer has no NIR channel at all. The visible-band figure is
the one a three-channel renderer can be compared against.

Closing an order of magnitude would take an order of magnitude, and the guard
affords a factor of about 1.4.

### 2.34.8 THE EYE, AND IT AGREES WITH THE LADDER FOR ONCE

`docs/screenshots/RN2540_crowns_shipped_3x.png` against
`RN2525_crowns_after_3x.png` (N6's shipped frame, same committed rect, same
`rn2450crop.mjs` 3x): **indistinguishable, which is the point** -- this lane
changes no pixel. **2.31.5/2.33.7's "CROWNS: NOT MET" STANDS, NOT MET.**

The three diagnostic crops are the finding made visible, and they are the reason
to believe the table:

- `RN2540_crowns_floorAlone_3x.png` (both paint arms): a **completely flat,
  structureless blue-slate sheet**. It has no crowns in it, no ground in it and
  no texture of any kind, and it is exactly the colour the crowns wear. The
  thing four audits photographed and called a crown colour is a picture of the
  air.
- `RN2540_crowns_cardRaw_3x.png` (terrain black, cards with no aerial term):
  the crowns alone, and they are **unmistakably DARK GREEN**. Not blue, not
  slate, not violet. The crown is the right colour and is roughly black.
- `RN2540_crowns_floor030_3x.png` (`crownshadefloor=0.30`, the arm that FLIPS
  RN-2275's guard): green now shows on the sunlit edges of individual crowns
  and the mass is still slate. A 3.75x brightening, bought by breaking the
  guard, buys crown EDGES.

`RN2540_crowns_cardOnly_3x.png` and `RN2540_crowns_cardDiffuse_3x.png` complete
the set, and the 1x frames every crop comes from are committed beside them as
`RN2540_forestair_*.png`.

**FIDELITY-GAP section 1, item by item.** Item 3 ("their sky is a participant;
ours is a backdrop") is the one this lane speaks to and it is **NEITHER closed
nor untouched: it is re-aimed.** Our sky is not failing to light the mid
distance -- it is lighting it so completely that it is the only thing in it.
Item 1 (the grass carpet), item 2 (terrain materials), item 4 (grading) and item
6 (water) are **untouched**. Item 5 (vegetation asset fidelity) is **untouched
as an asset question and sharpened as a lighting one**: this lane's numbers say
a better crown MESH would change nothing at this range until the crown's
radiance changes, because its albedo reaches 3 per cent of its own pixel.

### 2.35.2 THE LARGEST FINDING IS THAT THE GUARD WAS NEVER A GUARD

That is NUMBERS.md's own scar -- *a probe that prints and never asserts passes

and *a sentence in a comment is not an invariant* is the second scar in the same
